summary: This item introduces VISTA, a new training method for GUI Grounding that addresses limitations in Group Relative Policy Optimization. VISTA aims to improve policy learning by using view-consistent self-verified training to avoid biased success/failure groupings in rollouts.

summary: This item describes a method for abstracting cross-domain action sequences from digital application usage logs into interpretable workflows. The goal is to gain meaningful insights from user interactions to improve digital products, overcoming issues of granularity and noise.

title: Towards Direct Latent-Space Synthesis for Parallel Branches in LLM-Agent Workflows
summary: This item proposes a method for direct latent-space synthesis to better support parallel branches in LLM-agent workflows. It aims to address the mismatch between LLMs' sequential text interface and the structured, multi-branch nature of modern agentic systems.

title: GAGPO: Generalized Advantage Grouped Policy Optimization
summary: This item introduces GAGPO, Generalized Advantage Grouped Policy Optimization, a new reinforcement learning method for post-training large language model agents. It aims to address the challenge of credit assignment in multi-turn environments where rewards are sparse.

title: Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging: Transitioning from Uniform Priors to Sparse Posteriors in Ensemble Learning
summary: This item presents Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging (SCSB), a mathematical framework for post-training compression and probability calibration of bootstrap-based bagging ensembles. It aims to improve standard bagging ensembles by transitioning from uniform priors to sparse posteriors.

title: An Agentic Retrieval Framework for Autonomous Context-Aware Data Quality Assessment
summary: This item introduces an agentic retrieval framework designed for autonomous and context-aware data quality assessment. It aims to overcome limitations of static rules or manual strategies by providing a more adaptive approach to evaluating data quality.

summary: This item proposes Random Attention (RA), a lightweight temporal modeling method for efficient mobile sleep staging. It aims to overcome the computational expense of existing sequential models like RNNs and Transformers for deployment on mobile devices.

title: Korzhinskii-Net: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Sub-Surface Mineral Prospectivity Modelling
summary: This item introduces Korzhinskii-Net, a Physics-Informed Neural Network designed for sub-surface mineral prospectivity modeling. This method integrates subsurface physics to improve accuracy beyond traditional data-driven classifiers that rely on surface proxies.

title: Active Inference for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control in Noisy Nonstationary IoT Environments
summary: This item proposes using Active Inference for adaptive traffic signal control in noisy and nonstationary IoT environments. The method aims to maintain effectiveness under challenging conditions like sensor occlusion and nonstationary demand, where conventional controllers struggle.

title: Position: AI Must Become Planet-Centered, Not Just Human-Centered
summary: This position paper advocates for "Planet-Centered AI" (PCAI) as a new design philosophy and research agenda. It argues that contemporary AI paradigms are insufficient and proposes reorienting AI towards supporting planetary-scale socio-ecological systems and long-term trajectories.

title: Can Editing 1 Neuron Fix Repetition Loops in LLMs?
summary: This item investigates whether editing a single neuron can fix repetition loops in LLMs, specifically in Gemma 4 instruction-tuned models. It analyzes a reproducible failure mode where these models collapse into repetition when generating long factual enumerations.

title: HierSVA: A Data Synthesis Pipeline, Dataset, and Benchmark for LLM-Driven Hierarchical Hardware Formal Verification
summary: This item introduces HierSVA, an integrated suite providing a data synthesis pipeline, dataset, and benchmark for LLM-driven hierarchical hardware formal verification. It aims to evaluate LLMs' ability to produce reference SystemVerilog Assertions.

title: Morphology-Aware Sample Assignment: Overcoming IoU Insensitivity for Surface Defect Detection
summary: This item proposes Morphology-Aware Sample Assignment, a method designed to overcome Intersection-over-Union (IoU) insensitivity in visual detection models for surface defect detection. It aims to improve the quality of positive sample sets and the training efficacy of these models.

title: VHDLSuite: Unified Pipeline for LLM VHDL Generation with Data Synthesis and Evaluation
summary: This item introduces VHDLSuite, a unified pipeline for Large Language Model (LLM) VHDL generation, complete with data synthesis and evaluation. It addresses the limited evaluation of LLM performance for Hardware Description Languages beyond Verilog, specifically VHDL.

title: FreoStream:Enhancing Stream Guardrails via Future-Aware Reasoning and Safety-Aligned Optimization
summary: This item introduces FreoStream, a method for enhancing stream guardrails to improve token-level safety detection in AI systems. It aims to mitigate issues like over-refusal of sensitive but safe tokens and improve detection of implicitly harmful content by incorporating future-aware reasoning.

title: A Virtuous AI is an Existential Risk
summary: This paper examines the trade-offs between AI safety and well-being, arguing that a "virtuous AI" could pose an existential risk. It analyzes this concept in relation to finetuning methods like 'Constitutional AI' and complex ethical decision-making.

title: The Weight Norm Sets the Grokking Timescale: A Causal Delay Law
summary: This paper investigates whether the weight norm causes grokking, the delayed onset of generalization in neural networks. It aims to clarify the role of critical norm in this phenomenon.

title: Position: Align AI to Our Aspirations, Not Our Flaws

title: D2H-AD: A Hybrid Model Utilizing Hyperdimensional Computing for Advanced Anomaly Detection
summary: This research introduces D2H-AD, a hybrid model that uses hyperdimensional computing for advanced anomaly detection. It aims to overcome limitations of conventional machine learning methods.

title: Beyond LoRA: Is Sparsity-Induced Adaptation Better?
summary: This paper investigates whether sparsity-induced adaptation offers better generalizability compared to Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for fine-tuning pre-trained models. It examines the efficiency and effectiveness of these adaptation methods.

summary: This research addresses instability in diffusion policy-gradient methods for RL post-training by identifying the "double-drift phenomenon" as the cause. It aims to develop more reliable policy improvement for diffusion policies.

summary: This paper introduces a stationarity-and-coupling criterion for training-free time-lagged spectral embeddings of multivariate time series. It investigates when such descriptors can effectively analyze time series data.

title: Muon$^p$: Muon with Fractional Spectral Powers

title: Natively Unlearnable Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates the challenge of unlearning specific training data from large language models (LLMs) due to entangled source contributions. It explores creating "natively unlearnable" LLMs by isolating source contributions to disjoint parameters.

title: A Longitudinal Attribute-Conditioned Neural Network for Modeling Health-State Transition Probabilities in Temporally Irregular Data: The LANTERN Framework
summary: This paper introduces the LANTERN framework, a longitudinal attribute-conditioned neural network for modeling health-state transition probabilities from temporally irregular data. It has applications in disability insurance pricing and solvency assessment.

title: Gefen: Optimized Stochastic Optimizer
summary: This research proposes Gefen, a new memory-efficient stochastic optimizer designed to address the memory overhead of optimizers like AdamW. Gefen automatically shares second-moment estimates and quantizes first-moment estimates.

title: SpikF-GO: Spiking Fourier Graph Operators for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces SpikF-GO, a method combining Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) with Fourier Graph Operators for multivariate time series forecasting. It explores the energy-efficient advantages of SNNs for this application.

title: Smoothing Dark Areas in Molecular Latent Diffusion
summary: This research addresses the challenge of smoothing "dark areas" in the latent space of molecular latent diffusion models for scalable 3D molecular generation. It aims to ensure a smooth, valid, and navigable latent space.

title: Can Machine Learning Forecast Rice Yields in Data-Constrained Settings? Satellite Climate Data, National Crop Statistics, and Lessons from Sierra Leone
