title: Decompose Sparsely Where You Should, Absorb Densely Where You Should No
summary: This research questions the assumption that all activation content is amenable to sparse decomposition in sparse autoencoders (SAEs). It proposes a new hypothesis regarding how SAEs should decompose sparsely and absorb densely.

title: Non-Parametric Machine Text Detection via Multi-View Gaussian Processes
summary: This paper proposes a non-parametric machine text detection method using multi-view Gaussian processes to improve accuracy under adversarial conditions. It leverages multiple complementary signals from documents to enhance detection robustness.

title: Lyapunov-Based Sample Complexity Analysis for Weakly-Coupled MDPs
summary: This paper analyzes the sample complexity of learning in average-reward weakly-coupled Markov decision processes (WCMDPs) and Restless Bandits (RBs) under a generative model.

title: Numbers Already Carry Their Own Embeddings
summary: This research introduces Adelic operation-preserved embeddings (AOE), a training-free representation that captures both a number's real value and its modular signatures, preserving additive and multiplicative structure.

title: Contract-Based Compositional Shielding for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: This work proposes Contract-Based Compositional Shielding as a method to enforce global safety in multi-agent reinforcement learning systems where agents cannot unilaterally guarantee safety.

title: Decoupled Latent Optimization of Diffusion Models for Full Waveform Inversion
summary: This study presents a decoupled latent optimization method for diffusion models to improve Full Waveform Inversion, aiming to recover subsurface velocity more realistically.

title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
summary: This study investigates mitigating medical hallucinations in LLMs via post-hoc adversarial auditing and multi-agent feedback loops to reduce risks in clinical decision-making.

title: Small LLMs: Pruning vs. Training from Scratch
summary: This work examines the effectiveness of pruning versus training from scratch for creating strong small language models, using Llama-3.1-8B and comparing six different pruning methods.

title: Graph-based Target Back-Propagation for Context Adaptation in Multi-LLM Agentic Systems
summary: This paper introduces Graph-based Target Back-Propagation for context adaptation in multi-LLM agentic systems, aiming to automate prompt engineering and improve credit assignment.

title: Learning High Coverage Discriminative Parsimonious Rulesets
summary: This research focuses on learning interpretable IF-THEN rule representations that achieve high discriminative power and coverage, a key objective in contemporary AI research.

title: Curvature-Guided Geometric Representation for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction
summary: This research proposes a curvature-guided geometric representation to enhance protein-ligand binding affinity prediction, crucial for improving drug discovery processes.

title: Machine Learning for Biomedical Raman Spectroscopy: From Spectral Acquisition to Clinical Translation
summary: This paper reviews the application of machine learning in biomedical Raman spectroscopy, from spectral acquisition techniques to their translation for clinical use, such as cancer diagnosis.

title: Context-aware Modality-Topology Co-Alignment for Multimodal Attributed Graphs
summary: This research explores a context-aware modality-topology co-alignment method for Multimodal Attributed Graphs (MAGs), enhancing representations for graph-centric and modality-centric tasks.

title: Zeta: Dual Whitening for Matrix Optimization via Coordinate-Adaptive Preconditioning
summary: This paper introduces Zeta, a Dual Whitening technique for matrix optimization using coordinate-adaptive preconditioning to address vulnerabilities in existing matrix-aware optimizers for neural network training.

title: DRIVE: Distributional and Retrieval-Augmented Bidding with Value Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces DRIVE, a system for auto-bidding in real-time advertising that uses distributional and retrieval-augmented methods with value evaluation to optimize long-term performance.

title: LapidaryEngine: Fully Conversational Crystal Generation
summary: LapidaryEngine is presented as a text-to-crystal generative model that enables fully conversational interaction, allowing users to design crystal materials through natural-language instructions.

title: Curvature-Informed Potential Energy Surface for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction
summary: This study develops a curvature-informed potential energy surface approach for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction, aiming to improve structure-based drug discovery.

title: Learning the Context of Errors: Black-Box Online Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models
summary: This paper investigates black-box online adaptation methods for Time Series Foundation Models, focusing on learning from errors to improve zero-shot forecasting in diverse domains.

title: Implicit Variational Rejection Sampling
summary: This work introduces Implicit Variational Rejection Sampling, a novel inference technique in Bayesian machine learning designed to better approximate complex posterior distributions.

title: Where Black-box Drug-Target Interaction Prediction Models Look: Cross-Method Explainability
summary: This research conducts an interpretability audit of black-box drug-target interaction prediction models to understand how they use features and where they 'look' in their decision-making.

title: DIFF-ERO: A Conformance-Aware Loss for Deep Learning in Process Mining
summary: This paper proposes DIFF-ERO, a conformance-aware loss function for deep learning models in process mining, aiming to better capture control-flow structure compared to standard objectives.

title: Riemannian Metric Matching for Scalable Geometric Modeling of Distributions
summary: This research introduces Riemannian Metric Matching, a denoising probabilistic framework for scalable geometric modeling of high-dimensional data distributions.

title: More with LESS -- Local Scene Representations for Tactile Imaging
summary: This item presents a research paper on using local scene representations with self-supervised learning for tactile imaging, aimed at reconstructing the internal structure of soft objects for medical diagnosis and robotic manipulation.

title: Squeeze-Release: Iterative Pruning with Exact Structural Minimization
summary: This item describes a technical method called Squeeze-Release for iterative pruning with exact structural minimization, which converts sparse weight tensors into a smaller, dense network for more efficient AI model deployment.

title: When Language Representations Interact: Separability and Cross-Lingual Effects in LLMs
summary: This item discusses a research paper investigating how language representations interact within large language models, focusing on separability and cross-lingual effects to understand their internal mechanisms.

title: Can Deep Neural Networks Improve Compression of Very Large Scientific Data?
summary: This item explores whether deep neural networks can improve error-bounded lossy compression for very large scientific data, a fundamental technique for managing rapidly growing data volumes.

title: SemPiper: Interactive Code Synthesis for Semantic Operators in Machine Learning Pipelines
summary: This item introduces SemPiper, an interactive code synthesis tool utilizing large language models to assist in developing machine learning pipelines by generating semantic operators for data preparation and feature engineering.

title: Stalo sa to, pred čím mnohí varovali: USA odrezali EÚ od najvýkonnejších modelov AI
summary: This item reports that the US government intervened, leading Anthropic to restrict access for foreign users to its advanced AI models Fable 5 and Mythos 5, effectively cutting off the EU from these systems.

title: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
summary: This item describes a method for benchmarking the safety of autonomous web agents by testing their behavior under realistic deceptive interfaces in the e-commerce domain and introduces a plugin called WebDecept.

title: Which Models Perform Better in Inheritance Reasoning?
summary: This item presents team PSL's participation in the QIAS 2026 Shared Task, which evaluates large language models' ability to solve complex Arabic Islamic inheritance reasoning cases requiring legal interpretation and numerical computation.

title: QIAS 2026: Overview of the Shared Task on Islamic Inheritance Reasoning
summary: This item provides an overview of the QIAS 2026 shared task, designed to evaluate large language models' ability to perform complex reasoning in the religious and legal domain of Islamic inheritance.

title: The Culture Funnel: You Can't Align What isn't in the Data
summary: This item introduces 'The Culture Funnel' concept, arguing that current LLM cultural alignment approaches are flawed because models lack sufficient cultural knowledge in their training data, rather than just requiring inference-time interventions.

title: When Plausible Is Not Realistic: Evaluating Human Mobility in LLM-Based Urban Simulation
summary: This item introduces a validation framework for evaluating the realism of human mobility patterns generated by LLM-based generative agents used in urban simulations, addressing whether plausible outputs are empirically realistic.

title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Variational Autoencoder for Neural Topic Modeling
summary: This item presents a proof-of-concept for a hybrid classical-quantum variational autoencoder designed for neural topic modeling, integrating parameterized quantum circuits within the VAE inference mechanism.

title: SANA: What Matters for QA Agents over Massive Data Lakes?
summary: This item explores the critical components for LLM agents performing exploratory question answering over massive data lakes, discussing how agents discover relevant sources, analyze data, and adapt actions.

title: DLawBench: Evaluating LLMs Through Multi-Turn Legal Consultation
summary: This item introduces DLawBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models through multi-turn legal consultations, assessing their ability to elicit information and devise legal strategies.

title: Can Post-Training Turn LLMs into Good Medical Coders? An Empirical Study of Generative ICD Coding
summary: This item presents an empirical study investigating whether post-training can improve large language models' performance as medical coders for Automated International Classification of Diseases (ICD) coding, a core healthcare task.

title: LLMs Contain Multitudes: How Deployment Context Reshapes Model-Level Preferences and Values
summary: This item explores how the deployment context reshapes model-level preferences and values in large language models, challenging the assumption of stable, inherent value systems and examining influences beyond simple prompt variations.

title: MedLatentDx: Latent Multi-Agent Communication for Cross-Hospital Rare-Disease Diagnosis
summary: This item describes MedLatentDx, a system that uses latent multi-agent communication to facilitate cross-hospital collaboration for diagnosing rare diseases, enabling institutions to share case-specific diagnostic insights.

title: Fusing Stylometric and Embedding Systems to Estimate Authorship Likelihood Ratios in Japanese
summary: This item discusses a method for estimating authorship likelihood ratios in Japanese textual evidence by fusing stylometric and embedding systems, applying a forensic science framework to AI analysis.

title: The Holistic Storage of Verb+Up Phrases in Text-based and Audio-based Language Models
summary: This item investigates the holistic storage of verb+up phrases in both text-based and audio-based language models, examining how these models manage stored representations and abstract linguistic knowledge.

title: Dialogue SWE-Bench: A Benchmark for Dialogue-Driven Coding Agents
summary: This item introduces Dialogue SWE-Bench, an automatic benchmark dataset specifically designed for evaluating dialogue-driven AI coding agents, in contrast to existing benchmarks for fully-autonomous systems.

title: Right or Wrong, Models Comply: Directional Blindness in LLM Moral Judgment
summary: This paper introduces a new evaluation method to assess large language models' (LLMs) compliance and moral judgment, focusing on whether they resist user pushback selectively. It highlights limitations in current evaluation approaches for alignment properties.

title: Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing Across Diverse Conflict Scenarios
summary: This work introduces a method to evaluate gender bias in large language models by assessing if they apply consistent moral standards to scenarios involving male versus female actors. It aims to uncover gender-asymmetric moral framing in LLMs.

title: Beyond Perplexity: UTF-8 Validity in Byte-aware Language Models
summary: This paper investigates the UTF-8 validity of sequences generated by byte-aware language models, particularly when encountering rare characters. It explores the relationship between model training scale and the reliability of UTF-8 generation.

title: Implicit Reasoning for Large Language Model-based Generative Recommendation
summary: This research explores how large language models utilize implicit reasoning to access and apply their pretrained world knowledge for generative recommendation systems. It highlights challenges in reliably invoking this knowledge for such applications.

title: CacheRL:Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents via Cached Rollouts and Hybrid Reward
summary: This paper introduces CacheRL, a system designed for training small agent foundation models that achieves high accuracy on multi-step tool-calling tasks with significantly less computational resources. It addresses challenges in practical agent training.

title: OdysSim: Building Foundation Models for Human Behavior Simulation
summary: This paper introduces OdysSim, a large open system designed as a foundation model for human behavior simulation, addressing the 'Sim2Real gap' in current large language model simulators. It aims to provide more realistic human simulations.

title: Detecting undisclosed LLM-generated content in parliamentary texts
summary: This paper evaluates the extent of undisclosed large language model-generated content within parliamentary texts from the United Kingdom and Sweden. It investigates the prevalence of AI-tool usage where disclosure is often required.

title: Decoupled Mixture-of-Experts for Parametric Knowledge Injection
summary: This paper introduces Decoupled Mixture-of-Experts as a new method for parametric knowledge injection into large language models, aiming to overcome the trade-offs of existing approaches like retrieval-augmented generation. It focuses on integrating external, domain-specific knowledge.

title: Does the Judge Prefer English? Evaluating Language-Switching Invariance in LLM-as-a-Judge
summary: This paper evaluates the language-switching invariance of large language models used as automatic judges, investigating whether the input language affects their evaluation consistency. It addresses a new reliability question for LLM-as-a-Judge practices.

title: Retrospective Progress-Aware Self-Refinement for LLM Agent Training
summary: This paper introduces a retrospective progress-aware self-refinement method for training large language model-based agents, aiming to improve their metacognitive awareness of task progress and long-horizon performance.

title: Achieving Precise Text-To-Cypher Via Grounded Knowledge Graph Data Generation
summary: This paper presents a method using grounded knowledge graph data generation to achieve precise Text-To-Cypher parsing, enabling more accurate conversational interfaces for querying property graph databases.

title: Learning to Hear Hesitation: Continual Learning for Disfluency-Aware ASR
summary: This paper explores using continual learning to enhance Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, enabling them to better process and retain disfluent speech like hesitations, rather than omitting them.

title: MoDiCoL: A Modular Diagnostic Continual Learning Dataset for Robust Speech Recognition
summary: This paper introduces MoDiCoL, a modular diagnostic continual learning dataset designed to improve the robustness of Automatic Speech Recognition systems against real-world distribution shifts. It aims to address performance gaps in current ASR benchmarks.

title: A Computational Audit of Demographic Association Encoding in ClinicalBERT Language Predictions
summary: This paper conducts a computational audit of ClinicalBERT language models to understand how demographic associations from medical documentation are encoded and propagate into model predictions, particularly given their use in clinical decision support.

title: Fodor and Pylyshyn's Systematicity Challenge Still Stands
summary: This paper discusses whether the recent successes of neural networks in producing human-like language adequately address Fodor and Pylyshyn's Systematicity Challenge in cognitive science and artificial intelligence.

title: BayLing-Duplex: Native Full-Duplex Speech Dialogue with a Single Autoregressive LLM
summary: This paper introduces BayLing-Duplex, a new system enabling native full-duplex speech dialogue with a single autoregressive large language model. It allows real-time listening and speaking for next-generation spoken chatbots.

title: SIMMER: Benchmarking Latent Failures in LLM Executable Planning with a World Model
summary: This paper introduces SIMMER, a new benchmarking method designed to detect and evaluate latent failures in large language model-generated plans for autonomous agents. It addresses shortcomings in existing evaluation benchmarks.

title: Persuasion Index: A Theory-Guided Framework for Persuasion Analysis
summary: This paper proposes the Persuasion Index, a theory-guided framework and taxonomy for analyzing persuasive rhetorical cues, with applications ranging from detecting information manipulation to improving AI safety.

title: LoSoNA: A Benchmark for Local Social Norm Adaptation in Group Conversations
summary: This paper introduces LoSoNA, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of LLM-based agents to recognize and adapt to local social norms in multi-party chat environments. It explores how well agents can adjust their conversational style to specific group contexts.

title: Characterizing Cultural Localization in AI-Generated Stories
summary: This research characterizes how artificial intelligence systems generate culturally localized stories, examining the use of cultural markers such as names and locations. It investigates methods for assessing the cultural relevance of AI-generated content.

title: AgentSpec: Understanding Embodied Agent Scaffolds Through Controlled Composition
summary: This paper introduces AgentSpec to analyze scaffolded LLM agents, which integrate reasoning, memory, reflection, and action execution. It aims to provide a controlled composition framework to better understand these complex agent systems.

title: CORA: Analyzing and bridging thinking-answer gap in Multimodal RLVR via Consistency-Oriented Reasoning Alignment
summary: This research presents CORA, a method to analyze and bridge the thinking-answer gap in Multimodal Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). It focuses on Consistency-Oriented Reasoning Alignment to improve the reasoning capabilities of multimodal AI systems.

title: AdaSR: Adaptive Streaming Reasoning with Hierarchical Relative Policy Optimization
summary: This paper introduces AdaSR, a method for Adaptive Streaming Reasoning that allows large reasoning models to process continuous data streams, unlike traditional static context processing. It uses Hierarchical Relative Policy Optimization to manage dynamic information arrival.

title: Indirect Computing Model with Indirect Formal Method
summary: This paper discusses an indirect computing model combined with an indirect formal method for optimizing cloud computing technology within collaborative intelligent computing systems. It explores principles for human-computer interface and collaborative program integration.

title: Incentives Of EdTech: A Systematic Review Of EduNLP Research
summary: This paper presents a systematic literature review of EduNLP (Educational Natural Language Processing) research to identify the stakeholders whose interests are best served by educational technologies. It examines the incentives driving EdTech development within the NLP community.

title: Multimodal Speaker Identification in Classroom Environments
summary: This study evaluates a multimodal framework for speaker identification in K-12 classroom environments, combining acoustic embeddings with semantic context derived from large language models. It aims to address challenges posed by background noise and variable child speech.

title: ADORE: Iterative Query Expansion with Retrieval-Grounded Relevance Feedback
summary: This paper introduces ADORE, a method for iterative query expansion that uses retrieval-grounded relevance feedback to enhance LLM-based information retrieval. It aims to prevent retrieval drift by verifying how the target corpus responds to expanded queries.

title: Same-Origin Policy for Agentic Browsers
summary: This paper explores the application of the Same-Origin Policy, a fundamental web security mechanism, to agentic browsers that integrate autonomous AI agents. It addresses preventing unauthorized cross-origin data flows in these AI-powered web environments.

title: Knowledge Graph Enhanced Memory-Augmented Retrieval for Long Context Modeling
summary: This paper introduces Knowledge Graph Enhanced Memory-Augmented Retrieval (KGERMAR) to improve long context modeling by maintaining coherent understanding of entity states and relationships. It uses knowledge graphs to go beyond simple semantic similarity in retrieval.

title: Diffusion-Refined Segmentation and Vision-Language Interpretation for Pediatric Brain Tumor MRI
summary: This paper presents a two-stage deep learning framework for improving pediatric brain tumor MRI segmentation and vision-language interpretation. It uses diffusion models to address challenges like limited data and heterogeneous imaging phenotypes in healthcare.

title: Simulating Students' Java Programming Errors with Large Language Models
summary: This paper explores using large language models to simulate student Java programming errors, aiming to generate representative error sets. This approach helps overcome the slow and costly process of accumulating authentic student submissions for programming education.

title: Connections Between Pairs of Filters Improve the Accuracy of Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: This research investigates how connections between pairs of filters can improve the accuracy of Convolutional Neural Networks, proposing a new approach to network structures. It explores alternatives to traditional stacking of convolutional blocks.

title: CineOrchestra: Unified Entity-Centric Conditioning for Cinematic Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces CineOrchestra, a method for cinematic video generation that provides unified entity-centric conditioning for fine-grained control. It allows for precise manipulation of subjects, camera movements, and shot transitions.

title: Compressing Image Style Training into a Single Model Forward
summary: This paper proposes a method to compress image style training for diffusion-based style transfer into a single model forward pass. The approach aims to balance inference efficiency with stylization fidelity in generative image models.

title: Explaining RhythmFormer: A Systematic XAI Analysis of Periodic Sparse Attention for Remote Photoplethysmography
summary: This paper presents a systematic XAI (Explainable AI) analysis of RhythmFormer, a transformer model for remote photoplethysmography (rPPG). It focuses on understanding and explaining the model's decisions, especially concerning periodic sparse attention.

title: Temporal Backtracking Search for Test-time Generative Video Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces Temporal Backtracking Search, a method designed to improve generative video reasoning by addressing logically flawed rollouts in diffusion models. It aims to enhance test-time performance for video generation.

title: Mirage Probes: How Vision Models Fake Visual Understanding
summary: This paper introduces Mirage Probes to investigate "mirage behavior" in vision-language models, where models exhibit confident but ungrounded answers to image-based questions. It aims to reveal how current benchmarks misrepresent true visual understanding.

title: Avatar V: Scaling Video-Reference Avatar Video Generation
summary: This research introduces Avatar V, a method for scaling video-reference avatar video generation to produce behaviorally recognizable avatars. It aims to faithfully reproduce a subject's talking rhythm, gestural tendencies, and expression dynamics.

title: How do Self-Supervised Remote Sensing Vision Models Transfer to Downstream Tasks?
summary: This paper studies the transferability of self-supervised geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) to downstream tasks, characterizing their behavior and representations learned from remote sensing data.

title: HiLo-Token: Input-Adaptive High-Low Frequency Token Compression for Efficient Image Editing
summary: This paper introduces HiLo-Token, an input-adaptive token compression method designed to reduce latency and improve efficiency for generative AI models used in creative image editing tools.

title: PMOF: A Dataset and Benchmark for Passenger Monitoring Using Overhead Fisheye Cameras
summary: This introduces PMOF, a new dataset and benchmark designed for reliable in-vehicle passenger monitoring in autonomous public transport using overhead fisheye cameras.

title: Overhead Wildlife Locator (OWL): Benchmarking Weakly Supervised Learning for Aerial Wildlife Surveys
summary: This paper introduces the Overhead Wildlife Locator (OWL) and a new benchmark for evaluating weakly supervised learning methods in automated aerial wildlife surveys.

title: Self-Evolving Visual Questioner
summary: This research explores the ability of vision-language models (VLMs) to actively ask diverse, visual-centric questions, introducing a "Self-Evolving Visual Questioner" to address limitations in current systems.

title: CaricHarmony: Contrastive Diffusion Paths for Identity-Preserving Caricature Synthesis
summary: This research introduces "CaricHarmony," a method using contrastive diffusion paths to enable identity-preserving caricature synthesis, addressing destructive interference issues in diffusion models.

title: Prompt2Effect: Training-Free Image-to-Video Model Specialization via LoRA Generation
summary: This paper presents Prompt2Effect, a training-free method that uses LoRA generation to specialize Image-to-Video diffusion models for generating specific visual effects.

title: Context-Guided Semantic Alignment for Feature Fusion Networks
summary: This research proposes "Context-Guided Semantic Alignment," a method to improve feature fusion networks in object detectors by addressing semantic inconsistency when aggregating multi-scale features.

title: HARBOR: Heading Analysis and Reconstruction from Behavioral Observation and Radar
summary: This paper introduces HARBOR, a method for heading analysis and reconstruction of vessel movements using behavioral observation and radar, designed for maritime situational awareness when AIS data is unavailable.

title: RT-VLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Models via Knowledge Distillation
summary: This research introduces RT-VLA, a method using knowledge distillation to enable real-time Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, addressing the substantial inference latency of existing VLA models for autonomous driving.

title: ViT-Up: Faithful Feature Upsampling for Vision Transformers
summary: This paper presents ViT-Up, a method for faithful feature upsampling in Vision Transformers (ViTs), addressing limitations associated with their operation on small patch-token grids.

title: GarmentSketch: Large-scale Sketch-to-Fashion Benchmark
summary: This paper introduces GarmentSketch, a large-scale benchmark designed to facilitate progress in sketch-based fashion image synthesis by providing high-quality paired resources.

title: Toward 360-Degree Indoor Panorama Editing via Tuning-Free Diffusion Model with Refocusing Cross-Attention
summary: This research proposes a method for 360-degree indoor panorama editing using a tuning-free diffusion model enhanced with refocusing cross-attention, addressing challenges in text-guided image editing.

title: Rethinking One-Step Image Editing through ChordEdit: Reproduction, Simplification, and New Insights
summary: This paper re-examines the ChordEdit method for one-step image editing through reproduction, simplification, and ablation, providing new insights into its underlying mechanisms.

title: WAM4D: Fast 4D World Action Model via Spatial Register Tokens
summary: This paper introduces WAM4D, a fast 4D World Action Model that addresses the limitations of existing 2D WAMs by incorporating spatial register tokens for more accurate modeling of executable robot actions.

title: ShearFuse-UNet: Hadamard, DCT, and Shearlet Transform Fusion for Next-Day Wildfire Spread Prediction
summary: This paper proposes ShearFuse-UNet, a lightweight and efficient deep learning model that integrates Hadamard, DCT, and Shearlet transform fusion for next-day wildfire spread prediction using multi-modal satellite data.

title: Clay-CNN Hybrids: Leveraging Geo-Foundational Models as Auxiliary Context for Landslide Detection
summary: This study investigates "Clay-CNN Hybrids" and evaluates how Clay v1.5, a Geo-Foundational Model, can be leveraged as auxiliary context to improve pixel-level landslide detection and segmentation.

title: FEMOT: Multi-Object Tracking using Frame and Event Cameras
summary: This paper introduces FEMOT, a multi-object tracking system that leverages both frame and event cameras to enhance performance under challenging conditions like motion blur and low illumination.

title: A New Multi-Domain Benchmark for Micro-Action Recognition and Detection
summary: This paper introduces a new multi-domain benchmark specifically designed for micro-action recognition and detection, addressing limitations of previous benchmarks in this area.

title: Conditioning Matters: Stabilizing Inversion and Attention in Diffusion Image Editing
summary: This research investigates the role of textual conditioning in stabilizing inversion and attention mechanisms within diffusion models for inversion-based image editing, aiming to improve accuracy and fidelity.

title: BoRAD: Bootstrap your Own Representations for Multi-class Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper introduces BoRAD, a method for multi-class anomaly detection in industrial inspection, which uses self-supervised learning to reconstruct normal appearances without copying abnormal details.

title: Encoder Winners Do Not Reliably Transfer Across VLA Backbone Scale: A Frozen-Backbone Grafting Diagnostic
summary: This research studies the transferability of vision encoders across different scales of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies and proposes a frozen-backbone grafting diagnostic to evaluate encoder choices.

title: VideoWeave: Unlocking Geometric Consistency in Video Generation via Joint Geometry-Video Modeling
summary: This paper presents VideoWeave, a method that improves large-scale video diffusion models by unlocking geometric consistency in video generation through joint geometry-video modeling.

title: MUSE: Agentic 3D Scene Authoring via Memory-Grounded Incremental Requirement Satisfaction
summary: MUSE is proposed as an agentic system for 3D scene authoring, using a memory-grounded approach to incrementally satisfy requirements for digital content creation and embodied AI simulation.

title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum (HCQ) Alzheimer's Classification via Supervised $\beta$-VAE and Quantum Kernels
summary: This paper introduces a Hybrid Classical-Quantum (HCQ) pipeline for Alzheimer's disease classification, combining a supervised 3D $\beta$-VAE with quantum kernels using structural MRI volumes.

title: A Multi-Domain Feature Fusion Framework for Generalizable Deepfake Detection Across Different Generators
summary: This research proposes a multi-domain feature fusion framework to improve generalizable deepfake detection across different generative models, addressing challenges in countering disinformation.

title: HiST: A Hierarchical Sparse Transformer for Cross-Modal Spatial Transcriptomics Modeling
summary: HiST, a Hierarchical Sparse Transformer, is introduced for cross-modal spatial transcriptomics modeling, aiming to infer gene expression from histology images to overcome cost and throughput limitations.

title: One Layer's Trash is Another Layer's Treasure: Adaptive Layer-wise Visual Token Selection in LVLMs
summary: This paper explores adaptive layer-wise visual token selection in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to reduce computational burden while maintaining performance across diverse multimodal tasks.

title: A Robust Point Cloud Analysis Framework Inspired By Primary Visual Cortex
summary: This paper presents a robust point cloud analysis framework inspired by the primary visual cortex, addressing energy consumption and robustness limitations in existing Convolutional Neural Networks.

title: Pix2Pix-Hybrid: Structure-Guided Conditional Synthesis of Hajj Crowd Images with Multi-Channel Conditioning and Weak Attribute Supervision
summary: Pix2Pix-Hybrid is proposed for structure-guided conditional synthesis of Hajj crowd images, using multi-channel conditioning and weak attribute supervision to address data scarcity for crowd-counting models.

title: What Drives Test-Time Adaptation for CLIP? A Controlled Empirical Study from an Update Perspective
summary: This empirical study investigates the factors driving Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP, analyzing their vulnerability to distribution shifts during deployment.

title: Pano3D: Unified 3D Reconstruction and Panoptic Segmentation
summary: Pano3D introduces a unified approach for 3D reconstruction and panoptic segmentation, enabling dense reconstruction from images with robust semantic understanding without camera parameters.

title: CausalMotion: Structured Physical Reasoning as Keyframe and Trajectory Guidance for Training-Free Video Generation
summary: CausalMotion presents a method for training-free video generation that enhances physical consistency and causal dynamics by using structured physical reasoning as keyframe and trajectory guidance.

title: ForceForget: Reinforcement Concept Removal for Enhancing Safety in Text-to-Image Models
summary: ForceForget introduces a reinforcement concept removal method to enhance safety in text-to-image models by selectively erasing concepts that can lead to the generation of unsafe content.

title: Point Cloud Upsampling through Patch-based Frequency Superposition
summary: This paper presents a method for point cloud upsampling using patch-based frequency superposition, aiming to provide a more interpretable and less data-dependent alternative to neural network approaches.

title: IndustryBench-MIPU: Benchmarking Multi-Image Attribute Value Extraction for Industrial Products
summary: IndustryBench-MIPU is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating multi-image attribute value extraction from technical specifications of industrial products across various supply chain applications.

title: MooMIns -- Monocular 3D Reconstruction and Object Pose Estimation from Multiple Instances
summary: MooMIns proposes a method for monocular 3D reconstruction and 6D object pose estimation from multiple instances, particularly relevant for industrial settings where objects are randomly arranged.

title: Value-order Decomposition for Generalist Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper introduces Value-order Decomposition for Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD), a method designed to improve cross-domain generalization for anomaly detection in industrial settings with limited data.

title: Scratched Lenses, Shifted Depth: Passive Camera-Side Optical Attacks
summary: This research explores passive camera-side optical attacks on vision systems, such as scratched lenses, which can induce shifted depth perceptions and are distinct from scene manipulation techniques.

title: Visual Quality Score Assessment of Large White Goods in Remanufacture with Multi-View Deformable-DETR
summary: This paper describes a multi-view Deformable-DETR approach for visual quality score assessment of large white goods in remanufacturing, automating a process traditionally bottlenecked by manual inspection.

title: NEST3D: A High-Resolution Multimodal Dataset of Sociable Weaver Tree Nests
summary: Sociable weaver nests function as complex ecological structures offering thermoregulatory microhabitats and sustaining diverse species; however, datasets used in prior studies lack fine-grained 3D structural detail. Producing usable and accurate 3D weaver nest data is challenging due to their irregular geometry and integration with complex host vegetation. We bridge this gap with an open-access, 1.4 TB multimodal drone dataset of 104 nest-bearing trees, comprising 27,945 RGB images, 111,780 multispectral images, approximately 781 million 3D points, and expert-annotated semantic segmentation labels. We benchmark semantic segmentation using KPConv, RandLA-Net, and Point Transformer V3, with PT-v3 achieving an mIoU of 86.35% on the test set. While the results demonstrate strong performance for transformer-based and point-wise methods, they also highlight architecture-dependent challenges, particularly for convolution-based approaches such as KPConv. By uniquely combining spectral, spatial, and structural information, the presented dataset advances 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and classification algorithms, enabling ecological applications from nest volume estimation to species conservation, and serves as a demanding benchmark that exposes architecture-dependent performance under extreme class imbalance.

title: A Qualitative Review of GenAI-Based Methods for Data Generation and Augmentation in Industrial Computer Vision Applications
summary: AI-driven computer vision applications require a profound database to ensure predictable behaviors and performance. Such predictable behaviors are especially important for industrial applications in gaining trust from users. However, such a database is not readily available in industrial applications, and its acquisition is not trivial either. Active learning methods can be applied to ramp up data within a project deployment to iteratively increase the database, and thus the application predictability. Unfortunately, we observe that this often leads to a loss of user trust in the application, which is difficult to regain once lost. This leads to a "chicken-and-egg" dilemma in which neither the database nor the application is developed. In this work, we review state-of-the-art methods and approaches to further boost the database the initial active data ramp-up phase. Here, we focus on recent advancements in GenAI-based data generation and augmentation methods and review their adaptability on an industrial computer vision classification use case. Although we observe a potential for automatic data ramp-up, we also see a domain miss match in between the source (training environment) and target (industrial use-case) - regarding context defined in natural language and object characteristics.

title: S$^2$COPE: Self-Supervised Concept Discovery via Preference Learning
summary: Current representation learning paradigms force a fundamental compromise: self-supervised methods scale to massive datasets but yield opaque features, whereas interpretable models remain bottlenecked by the need for dense human annotation. We introduce Self-Supervised Concept discOvery via Preference lEarning (\model), a label-free framework that resolves this dilemma. Instead of treating Vision-Large-Language Models (VLLMs) as static feature extractors, \model leverages them as active participants in a self-supervised preference optimization loop. By autonomously hypothesizing, validating, and reinforcing candidate visual attributes directly from raw imagery, our framework discovers novel, structured concepts without a single label. Extensive experiments across natural, medical, and physics domains demonstrate that \model successfully extracts domain-specific concepts where standard VLLMs often fail to generate. By amortizing concept discovery directly into the VLLM backbone through our self-supervised preference objective -- rather than relying on static generation and disjoint filtering -- we achieve up to a 24-point absolute improvement in downstream top-1 classification accuracy on unseen data. Our work suggest that interpretability can emerge through a model's autonomous interaction with incidental visual structures, without any human supervision.

title: StereoGeo: an end-to-end stereo camera calibration method
summary: In this work, we propose StereoGeo, an end-to-end network-based approach for stereo camera calibration. Our method estimates the focal lengths and gravity directions of the left and right cameras, as well as the relative extrinsic transformation relating them. Existing methods often rely on calibration patterns in structured environments or address only a single camera configuration, being limited to either intrinsic or extrinsic estimation, and depending on a multi-view setups. StereoGeo extends the GeoCalib algorithm, integrating deep neural network feature extraction with a differentiable optimizer. Extensive experiments on real-world benchmarks demonstrate that StereoGeo achieves competitive performance for intrinsic calibration and provides accurate stereo extrinsic estimation, outperforming existing methods that are limited to monocular settings. The dataset used in this work is partially publicly available at https://github.com/meddourimane/StereoGeo-dataset.

title: SED:Lightweight Saliency prediction for Event-based data via Distillation
summary: Event-based saliency prediction has gained attention recently, as combining event cameras with saliency estimation can act as an upstream stage that naturally improves the efficiency of downstream eventbased perception at the edge. However, current approaches are either neuromorphic, underperforming on event-based saliency benchmarks, or too heavy for resource-constrained edge applications due to their reliance on transformers or 3D convolutions. Drawing inspiration from efficient convolutional modules, SED and aiming to exploit the temporal information in event data, we propose a lightweight network, trained through knowledge distillation, built on a Depthwise Spatio-Temporal Block (DSTconv) -- a factorization of the 3D depthwise separable convolution. Relative to its teacher, our model reduces the model size from 180 MB to 0.32 MB (562x) and the parameter count from 45M to 81k (554x), while matching or outperforming it on the N-DHF1K and N-UCF Sports datasets. Moreover, it generalizes strongly beyond its training distribution, transferring from synthetic to real event data where a model trained from scratch fails.

title: Improving Lunar Topography with Deep Learning Schr\"odinger Bridges
summary: Increasing the resolution of planetary topography models can enable a better understanding of surface processes and geomorphology; however, existing analytical super-resolution methods are expensive and difficult to apply at large scales. Generative models provide the tools to learn complex relationships within data and can be applied at scale due to hardware accelerators and parallelization. We present a diffusion-based Schr\"odinger Bridge (SB) generative modeling approach for lunar topography super-resolution, connecting the distribution of low-resolution topography to that of high-resolution topography, incorporating physically-constraining optical imagery. Our approach is inspired by existing Shape-from-Shading methods, which improve a priori low-resolution topography by using optical images at the target resolution. We train SBs on a novel dataset of rendered lunar topography, emulating optical imagery from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Narrow Angle Camera. The result is a flexible approach for topography super-resolution which can provide pixel-level uncertainties in the reconstruction.

title: HPSv3++: Scaling Reward Models Across the Full Spectrum of Diffusion Model Capabilities
summary: Reward models guide text-to-image (T2I) systems toward outputs aligned with human preferences. However, typical reward models such as HPSv3 are trained on pre-annotated data from earlier T2I models, without accounting for quality discriminative shifts arising from evolving model capabilities and reinforcement learning (RL) iterations, limiting their broader applicability. In this work, we propose HPSv3++, a reward model framework that elevates the HPSv3 model for varying T2I model capabilities and their RL iteration changes across the full capability-iteration spectrum. Specifically, we first introduce HPDv3++, a 212K dual-dimension preference dataset annotated for text fidelity and aesthetic quality using a recent high-capability (Qwen-Image) model with human supervision. We then propose a two-stage training framework. Stage 1 employs data-aware orthogonal gradient projection to incorporate diverse aesthetic perception from HPDv3++ while preserving the original effective human preference knowledge in HPSv3. Stage 2 further leverages unlabeled data from T2I models spanning different capability levels and RL iterations, and introduces a joint capability-iterations conditioned signal for the reward model together with a standard deviation-driven unsupervised guidance mechanism, strengthening reward model across the capability-iteration spectrum. HPSv3++ achieves state-of-the-art preference prediction, outperforming HPSv3 9.8% on HPDv3, 5.5% on GenAI-Bench, while achieving 79.1%/88.1% on our proposed HPDv3++. When used for T2I RL training, it consistently improves GenEval scores across diverse T2I models, demonstrating its wide-range capabilities. The code is available at https://github.com/PlantPotatoOnMoon/HPSv3-PlusPlus.

title: Scalable Dynamic Tactile Sensing Enabled by Passive and Flexible Acoustic Waveguides
summary: Artificial dynamic tactile sensing requires sensitivity, robustness, and compliance, yet existing technologies face trade-offs when scaling to large-area arrays, compounded by wiring complexity and cost. Here, we report a passive distributed paradigm using deep sub-wavelength acoustic waveguides that decouples performance from structural flexibility. Elastic-membrane-capped Helmholtz resonators interconnected by spring-reinforced microtubes form an enclosed network with invariant acoustic transmission under macroscopic bending. By sparsely embedding microphones, the system achieves real-time localization (4 mm highest spatial resolution; >99% accuracy in a 4 microphones 64-node sensing array) and waveform reconstruction of low-frequency signals (<100 Hz). Fast Continuous Wavelet Transform and a lightweight neural network enable inference within 5.5 ms. We demonstrate conformable prototypes-fingertip arrays, a tactile glove, and large-area skins-detecting stimuli from single-hair contact to 5-mg particle impacts, arterial pulse waves, feather touches, and finger contact. This establishes a scalable, flexible, low-cost paradigm for next-generation human-machine interfaces.

title: $\mu_0$: A Scalable 3D Interaction-Trace World Model
summary: World models that capture how actions induce physical change enable scalable robot learning without reliance on embodiment-specific action labels. Pixel-space video models provide broad visual priors but expend model capacity on dense appearance reconstruction, while direct action models require embodiment-specific labels that hinder scalability. We present $\mu_0$, a scalable world model based on 3D traces. Rather than predicting dense pixels or directly modeling actions, $\mu_0$ forecasts smooth 3D trajectories for salient interaction points such as objects, tools, hands, and contact regions, yielding a compact, embodiment-agnostic motion interface. To enable training from diverse video sources, our TraceExtract system automatically extracts 3D supervision by selecting keypoints, constructing globally aligned traces, and associating motion segments with hierarchical language captions. This TraceExtract supervision pretrains $\mu_0$ by combining a pretrained vision-language backbone with a modular trace expert, which represents each query via B-spline control points and predicts future traces. Experiments show that $\mu_0$ outperforms baselines in both 2D and 3D trace prediction, including trace prediction models and tokenized VLM methods. Because $\mu_0$ is frozen and reusable, it can be paired with action experts for downstream robot embodiments. Despite action-free pretraining, the resulting trace-conditioned policies achieve performance competitive with VLA models pretrained with action supervision, such as $\pi_0$. These results establish 3D traces as a scalable and transferable representation for cross-embodiment manipulation.

title: Multi-Agent Embodied Autonomous Driving: From V2X Information Exchange to Shared World Models
summary: Autonomous driving is shifting from isolated vehicle intelligence toward multi-agent embodied systems that share perception, infer intent, and coordinate action under uncertainty. This survey examines this transition through the lens of Shared World Models (SWMs): predictive cross-agent representations maintained across vehicles, infrastructure, and other traffic participants. We review more than 380 publications spanning vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, collaborative perception, inter-agent cognition, cooperative planning, end-to-end cooperative driving, and simulation and data engines for closed-loop validation. The organizing question is how exchanged observations become aligned state, intent-aware interaction, and coordinated downstream action. Across the surveyed literature, evaluation remains concentrated in simulation, curated benchmarks, and offline protocols. Foundation-model-based coordination also lacks verified real-time safety guarantees in open traffic. These gaps motivate key research priorities for multi-agent embodied autonomous driving (MAEAD): verifiable shared-state maintenance, robust intent and plan alignment, and safe coordinated action under communication, latency, and deployment constraints.

title: Output-Level Regularization Eliminates the Seed Lottery in Single-GPU VLA Fine-Tuning
summary: Fine-tuning a vision-language-action model (VLA-JEPA) on a single GPU should be simple: load a pretrained checkpoint, run training, deploy. There is a hidden danger. Run the same fine-tuning code thirteen times -- same data, same architecture, different random seed -- and twelve runs produce a robot succeeding 91--94% of the time, while one run silently degrades to 65.2%: a 29 pp gap with no error message, no warning, and no way to predict which seed will fail. We call this the seed lottery. We trace the cause to output collapse: the action predictor quietly learns to produce nearly identical outputs regardless of what the robot sees. Existing weight-level methods (L2, EWC) are structurally blind to this collapse -- they penalize weight changes, but collapse occurs in directions weights can move freely without affecting outputs, a gap we formalize via the Jacobian null-space. Across 7 methods x up to 13 seeds x 3 LIBERO benchmarks, three output-level regularizers -- VICReg (n=12 seeds), Dropout (n=4), and a halved learning rate (n=5) -- each eliminate every catastrophic seed (0/21 combined collapses vs. 1/13 Baseline; F(12,11)=28.7, p<0.001), while weight-level methods (L2, EWC) preserve the lottery. The simplest fix is changing one number in your optimizer config.

title: ContactWorld: What Matters in Vision-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires world models to reason over complex contact dynamics from multimodal sensory observations. However, it remains unclear which representation properties fundamentally support stable long-horizon planning in contact-rich settings. In this paper, we present ContactWorld, a benchmark and systematic empirical study of vision-tactile world models spanning 12 contact-rich manipulation tasks, including insertion, disassembly, screwing, and exploratory interaction. Across extensive experiments, we find that representations that are both spatially structured and temporally continuous consistently achieve the strongest planning performance. In particular, point-cloud observations improve average planning success rates from 20.7% with wrist-view observations and 22.0% with front-view observations to 32.1%. We further find that the effectiveness of tactile sensing depends critically on cross-modal representation compatibility rather than modality scaling alone. Combining point-cloud observations with tactile force-field representations, which preserve richer spatial structure and interaction dynamics, further improves performance to 36.1%, yielding the strongest overall planning performance across all evaluated tasks. Moreover, tactile sensing becomes increasingly important under long-horizon planning objectives, where compounding prediction errors and contact uncertainty accumulate over time. Together, these findings highlight the importance of representation structure, multimodal compatibility, and long-horizon robustness in vision-tactile world models for contact-rich robotic manipulation.

title: AnyGoal: Vision-Language Guided Multi-Agent Exploration for Training-Free Lifelong Navigation
summary: End-to-end navigation policies trained on large simulation corpora degrade sharply when transferred to out-of-distribution scenes, categories, or goal modalities. Modular pipelines such as Modular GOAT are bottlenecked by closed-set object detection recall, while 3D snapshot-memory systems (e.g. 3D-Mem) accumulate dense, view-dependent representations that are heavy to maintain. We present AnyGoal, a training-free multi-robot architecture that places a Vision-Language Model (VLM) at the core of frontier-based exploration and coordinates agents through a shared 2D Gaussian Bayesian Value Map (BVM). The BVM maintains a per-pixel (mu, sigma^2) posterior over goal relevance, updated via precision-weighted fusion of VLM scores through a depth-cone mask, and is never reset between subtasks, yielding lifelong evidence accumulation. Frontiers are ranked by a convex blend of a VLM-as-judge softmax and a Bayesian UCB term on the BVM. A greedy allocator with spatial-separation penalty and commitment hysteresis distributes frontiers across agents without a centralized controller. On the full GOAT-Bench val unseen split (360 episodes, 2,669 subtasks), our dual-agent system achieves 52.4% Subtask SR at 12.7% SPL--state of the art under the strict physical regime (discrete 0.25 m steps, no teleportation, 42 deg HFOV) and a +27.5 pp improvement over Modular GOAT (24.9%). Single-agent AnyGoal achieves 41.9% Subtask SR, showing gains arise from the decision architecture. A four-way perception ablation shows that open-vocabulary detectors shift the dominant failure mode from exploration to goal verification.

title: Guided Diffusion with Distilled Vision-Language Reliability for Aerial Navigation
summary: Autonomous UAV navigation is conventionally solved by pipelines that separate perception, mapping, and planning into distinct stages, which propagates errors, accumulates latency, and requires environment-specific retuning. End-to-end generative models remove these interfaces by mapping raw observations directly to trajectories, but inherit a subtle failure mode: trained on clean data, they cannot recognise when an observation is unreliable, and treat degraded regions such as glass, mirrors, and overexposed surfaces as valid evidence for planning. We present a reliability-aware diffusion planner for 3D UAV navigation. It conditions trajectory generation on the observation together with a scene-level reliability heatmap that marks where perception cannot be trusted, produced by a lightweight network that distils the open-vocabulary reasoning of a vision-language model within the real-time planning budget. To generalise to unseen environments without retraining, we steer the denoising process with a differentiable two-stage ESDF cost that treats physical obstacles from depth and virtual obstacles from highly unreliable regions on equal footing. In simulation and on a real quadrotor, our planner produces markedly safer trajectories than a state-of-the-art diffusion baseline, reducing the obstacle-violation rate from 40.3% to 9.6% and raising the mean reliability of traversed regions from 0.588 to 0.925. Ablating the reliability term alone drops mean reliability from 0.898 to 0.783, confirming it as the decisive component, while distillation runs the framework up to 2 times faster than the full vision-language model.

title: PhysVLA: Towards Physically-Grounded VLA for Embodied Robotic Manipulation
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at mapping visual inputs and natural language instructions directly to robotic control policies. However, because they are trained primarily to fit behavioural demonstration data, they do not explicitly enforce fundamental physical principles such as rigid-body dynamics or contact constraints. This exposes a critical physics gap: standard temporal smoothing applied on top of single-step or chunked VLAs trades trajectory quality for added failures that short-term memory cannot resolve. To bridge this gap, we introduce PhysVLA (Physics-VLA), a plug-and-play, inference-time framework designed to wrap any frozen VLA backbone without retraining, fine-tuning, or weight access, with less than 1 ms of overhead per control step. PhysVLA intercepts the predicted control action, captures only the simulator or system state, and applies a dual-layered correction: (i) a phase-aware finite-state machine that structures discrete task segments (approach, grasp, transport, and place), and (ii) a selective Euler-Lagrange gate that activates only when a dynamics oracle detects kinodynamic inconsistency. Evaluated across OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, Force-VLA, and Generalist-VLA on LIBERO-Spatial with a 7-DoF Franka Panda, the framework delivers absolute success rate increases of up to 17% and stability increases of up to 19% with no per-task regressions, improves trajectory efficiency by up to 15% across all four backbones, and shows up to a 10x improvement in trajectory jerk robustness on a Robosuite Lift cross-simulator sweep. We further validate the framework on a real Agilex Piper arm with a pick-and-place task, confirming that PhysVLA transfers to physical hardware without retraining, with success-rate improvements of up to 50%, establishing physical awareness as a composable, backbone-agnostic runtime module.

title: An Attention-based Model for Robust Forecasting with Missing Modality
summary: Learning with missing modalities is a fundamental challenge in multimodal robot learning, as real-world robotic systems often operate in environments with incomplete sensor data. Attention-based models are appealing for processing multimodal data because they can handle multiple modalities with a single backbone network. However, most multimodal models assume that all modalities are available during both training and inference, limiting their applicability in robotic perception and decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a multimodal model designed to handle missing modalities during both training and inference. The model is formulated as a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and incorporates a transformer-based architecture that leverages attention mechanisms to learn a unified, fixed-dimensional representation, even when some modalities are missing. We show that our proposed model can be trained with missing modalities while approximating a robust representation of all modalities. We evaluate our approach on five multimodal datasets across two robot learning tasks: human trajectory prediction and robot manipulation forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that our model effectively learns from incomplete data and is superior to prior multimodal fusion approaches.

title: SplatlessDF: Continuous Distance Field Mapping with Non-Splatting Gaussians
summary: Recent Gaussian splatting (GS) methods have shown that scenes can be represented efficiently with optimisable Gaussians for high-quality reconstruction and rendering. In this paper, building on this principle, we introduce SplatlessDF, a continuous distance field (DF) mapping framework that uses anisotropic Gaussian elements from a spatial rather than photometric perspective. SplatlessDF directly parameterises the Gaussians and optimises to recover a differentiable DF, enabling distances and gradients to be queried in the spatial domain for downstream robotic tasks such as navigation. Furthermore, SplatlessDF can be coupled with 2D Gaussian splatting (2DGS), providing a unified framework based solely on Gaussian primitives that can learn continuous DF and surface models and supports photometric rendering. We consider two settings: a standalone DF-only formulation and a joint DF-rendering formulation coupled with 2DGS. Experiments show that the standalone formulation provides efficient and accurate distance and gradient queries, while the joint formulation improves rendering geometry and simultaneously models a continuous DF. These results highlight the potential of GS-style representations not only for surface modelling and rendering but also for mapping representations suited to robotic navigation.

title: From Attacks to Curricula: Learnability-Guided Adversarial Training for Safe Autonomous Driving
summary: Closed-loop adversarial training improves autonomous driving safety by exposing policies to rare safety-critical scenarios. Standard pipelines first generate adversarial scenarios and then sample them for policy optimization. However, most existing frameworks remain attack-oriented: collision-driven generators often synthesize unsolvable extreme situations, which can degrade learning, while heuristic samplers ignore the evolving capability of the driving policy, causing sample inefficiency and delayed convergence. We propose AlignADV, a learnability-guided closed-loop adversarial training framework that converts adversarial scenarios into resolvable and capability-aligned curricula. First, we reformulate adversarial scenario generation as a preference alignment problem and employ direct preference optimization to guide the generator toward critical yet resolvable scenarios. Second, we introduce behavioral fingerprints to capture the intrinsic characteristics of the evolving policy and construct a multi-modal capability prediction model that estimates policy performance without expensive closed-loop simulations. By combining resolvability-aligned scenarios with capability predictions, AlignADV develops a dynamic curriculum sampling mechanism that prioritizes scenarios targeting the current policy's vulnerabilities. Experiments on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset demonstrate that AlignADV improves convergence efficiency and final performance, reducing training steps by up to 40.6 percent compared with baseline methods while lowering collision rate and improving route completion under both normal and adversarial traffic conditions. These results highlight a shift from attack-oriented scenario generation to learnability-guided policy improvement, offering a principled direction for safer and more efficient autonomous driving training. Project page: https://meiyuewen.github.io/AlignADV/.

title: ReactSim-Bench: Benchmarking Reactive Behavior World Model Simulation in Autonomous Driving
summary: Reactive capability is a key property of data-driven behavior world model simulators for autonomous driving simulation systems. With this capability, simulated world agents can respond feasibly to autonomous vehicle (AV) behaviors that differ from the log. However, existing behavior simulation benchmarks do not directly measure reactive capability. They often let the simulator jointly control the AV and surrounding agents and evaluate realism through log similarity or open-loop prediction metrics. In this work, we introduce ReactSim-Bench for evaluating the reactive capability of behavior world model simulation in autonomous driving. We decouple the control of agents and the AV, using AV behaviors that differ from the log and require agents to respond as independent AV inputs. To obtain these AV behaviors, we construct a pipeline that uses an AV planner model to generate candidate behaviors and filters the data using rules and manual verification. Collision metrics, map-based metrics, and kinematic feasibility metrics are used to evaluate the safety and rule compliance of reactive responses. We construct 2,636 test scenarios with three categories and conduct a systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art models across multiple architectures, including Transformer-based, diffusion-based, and next-token-prediction-based models. We further analyze how replan frequency affects performance and provide insights for future studies.

title: The N2D Haptic Glove: A Multi-Finger Glove for 2D Directional Force Feedback for Contact Rich Manipulation
summary: Humans rely on directional fingertip forces to probe and regulate contact during manipulation, yet most wearable haptic gloves render only vibration or single-axis force, leaving force direction ambiguous. Without directional cues, users must infer contact force from vision alone, often leading to over-pressing, inconsistent control, and reduced precision in robotic teleoperation. We present the N2D Haptic Glove, a multi-finger wearable device that renders planar flexion-extension fingertip forces using capstan-drive transmissions for high-transparency force feedback. Through benchtop validations and a user study involving haptic teleoperation of a robotic arm and hand, we demonstrate that compared to visual-only and single-axis haptic baselines, planar fingertip feedback significantly reduces contact force error during precise manipulation, improves trial-to-trial consistency, and enhances overall user experience in axial probing tasks. These findings establish the N2D Haptic Glove and directional finger-based haptics devices as a promising modality for contact-rich teleoperation, immersive virtual reality simulations, and robot learning from demonstrations. N2D Haptic Glove's hardware and software system will be fully open-sourced at \href{https://ucsdarclab.github.io/n2d-glove/}{this https URL}.

title: Self-Improving VLA Policies: Selected Diffusion Noise for Spurious-Robust Action Smoothing
summary: This paper introduces Selected Diffusion Noise (SDN), a method to improve diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies for more robust robotic manipulation by addressing sensitivity to spurious correlations and noisy action generation.

title: A Modular Dual-Arm Apple Harvesting Robot with Enhanced Field Performance
summary: This paper presents a modular dual-arm apple harvesting robot designed to enhance field performance and address labor shortages in commercial orchards, aiming to improve throughput and reliability.

title: GAIT: Legged Robot Proprioceptive State Estimation with Attention over Inertial-Leg Tokens
summary: This research proposes GAIT, a method using Inertial-Leg tokenization and an attention-based network for proprioceptive state estimation in legged robots, improving how they perceive their own state.

title: Short-Horizon Position Accuracy of Single-Track Models: Implications for Motion Planning of Autonomous Vehicles
summary: This study evaluates the short-horizon positional accuracy of single-track vehicle models, highlighting their importance for accurate and safe motion planning in autonomous vehicles.

title: Selective Agentic Recovery for UAV Autonomy with a Persistent Mission Runtime
summary: This research explores using agentic AI for selective recovery reasoning in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) autonomy, enabling high-level problem-solving during mission execution on physical UAVs.

title: BIM-Loc: BIM-Integrated Discrepancy-Aware LiDAR-based Indoor Localization
summary: This paper introduces BIM-Loc, a LiDAR-based indoor localization method integrated with Building Information Models (BIM) to provide accurate and robust positioning for service and inspection robots.

title: When and How Severely: Scenario-Specific Safety Envelopes for Driving VLAs
summary: This work addresses the safety certification of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) driving planners by defining scenario-specific safety envelopes to determine failure conditions and severity under ISO 21448 standards.

title: SyLink Hand: A Synergy-Inspired Linkage-Driven Anthropomorphic Hand for Human-Like Dexterity
summary: This paper presents the SyLink Hand, an anthropomorphic robotic hand inspired by human hand synergies, designed to achieve human-like dexterity with mechanical simplicity through an integrated linkage mechanism.

title: Optimality-Preserving Decomposition for Scalable QAOA in Natural-Language-Guided Multi-Drone Assignment
summary: This research explores using quantum optimization (QAOA) with optimality-preserving decomposition for scalable, natural-language-guided assignment of multi-drone fleets, tackling complex combinatorial problems.

title: ReactVLA: Fast and Lightweight Reactive Robot Manipulation via Improved Mean Flow Action Generation
summary: This work introduces ReactVLA, a method for fast and lightweight reactive robot manipulation that improves diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies by reducing inference latency for closed-loop control.

title: FloVerse: Floor Plan-Guided Multi-Modal Navigation
summary: This paper introduces FloVerse, a new task for floor plan-guided multi-modal navigation that leverages compact spatial priors from floor plans to enable agents to navigate efficiently in unseen environments.

title: Robust Fall Recovery for Armless Bipedal-Wheeled Robots Via Force-Guided Learning
summary: This research focuses on robust fall recovery for armless bipedal-wheeled robots using force-guided learning, addressing a critical challenge for autonomous legged locomotion in various robot types.

title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models
summary: This research proposes Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning for self-aware policy execution in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, allowing robot manipulation to adapt computational effort based on task difficulty.

title: Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA: From Vision-Language-Action Models to a Real-World Robot Learning Stack
summary: This report presents Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA (HyVLA-0.5), an end-to-end robot learning stack that integrates data collection, model design, pre-training, fine-tuning, RL post-training, and real-world deployment for VLA models.

title: Kine2Go: Kinematic dataset for the Unitree Go2 robot with diverse gaits and motions
summary: This paper introduces Kine2Go, a kinematic dataset for the Unitree Go2 quadruped robot, providing diverse gaits and motions to support and advance robotics research in areas like locomotion.

title: CADET: Physics-Grounded Causal Auditing and Training-Free Deconfounding of End-to-End Driving Planners
summary: This paper presents CADET, a method for physics-grounded causal auditing and training-free deconfounding of end-to-end autonomous driving planners, addressing their susceptibility to statistical shortcuts.

title: AERMANI-PLACE: Language Guided Object Placement with Aerial Manipulators
summary: This work introduces AERMANI-PLACE, a system for language-guided object placement using aerial manipulators, offering a more intuitive interface for complex aerial manipulation tasks than metric coordinates.

title: Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Policy: Learning Precise and Robust Manipulation with a Single RGB Camera
summary: This research proposes a Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Policy for learning precise and robust robot manipulation using only a single RGB camera, overcoming challenges of multi-camera setups.

title: ORCA: A Platform for Open-Source Dexterity Research
summary: This paper introduces ORCA, an open-source platform designed to facilitate research in robotics manipulation, focusing on dexterity with grippers and anthropomorphic hands.

title: Sensitivity Shaping for Latent Modeling
summary: This research addresses safe deployment of generative dynamics models for planning in robotic systems by proposing Sensitivity Shaping for Latent Modeling, enabling reliable detection of out-of-distribution transitions.

title: What Robots Do Matters More Than What They Look Like: Task Context Shapes Trust in Educational HRI
summary: Research investigates how the tasks performed by socially assistive robots (SARs) influence human trust more than their physical appearance, especially in educational settings. It explores the impact of diverse robot embodiments and real-time interaction capabilities enabled by large language models.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning of Autonomous Highway Driving: A Unified Framework for Safety and Efficiency
summary: This paper proposes a unified safe reinforcement learning framework to improve decision-making for autonomous vehicles (AVs) on highways. The framework aims to guarantee safety during training and deployment while optimizing for efficiency.

title: Whole-Body Impedance Model Predictive Control for Safe Physical Human--Robot Interaction on Floating-Base Platforms
summary: This research introduces a Whole-Body Impedance Model Predictive Control framework for floating-base robots to ensure safe physical human-robot interaction. It addresses challenges in balancing and control under contact constraints, aiming to overcome limitations of existing control methods.

title: Provably Safe, Yet Scalable Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research focuses on developing provably safe and scalable reinforcement learning methods, aiming to overcome the lack of formal safety guarantees in current policy optimization approaches. It seeks to learn policies that optimize rewards while rigorously satisfying defined constraints.

title: Instruct-Particulate: Scaling Feed-Forward 3D Object Articulation with Kinematic Control
summary: This paper introduces "Instruct-Particulate," a new method aimed at scaling feed-forward 3D object articulation using kinematic control. It addresses the challenge of limited annotated data for reconstructing articulated 3D objects, which is crucial for applications in animation, gaming, and robotic simulations.

title: Cross-Stage Sensorimotor Perception Scheduling and Sparse Map Encoding for Efficient Edge Embodied Navigation
summary: This research proposes a method for efficient edge embodied navigation using cross-stage sensorimotor perception scheduling and sparse map encoding. It addresses the challenges of deploying embodied agents on embedded hardware with tight latency, memory, and energy constraints for tasks like Object Goal Navigation.

title: ADAPT: An Autonomous Forklift for Construction Site Operation
summary: ADAPT introduces an autonomous forklift designed for operations on construction sites to improve material logistics. This solution aims to streamline on-site operations, reduce inefficiencies, delays, and safety risks associated with manual material handling.

title: Schr\"odinger's Navigator: Imagining an Ensemble of Futures for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
summary: This research explores Zero-Shot Object Navigation (ZSON) for robots, which enables them to find target objects in unseen environments without prior fine-tuning or maps. It proposes imagining an ensemble of futures to improve performance in cluttered real-world scenes for general-purpose service robots.

title: A Pragmatic VLA Foundation Model
summary: This paper introduces LingBot-VLA, a pragmatic Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation model designed for robotic manipulation. The model aims to generalize across various tasks and platforms efficiently, minimizing data and GPU hour requirements for adaptation.

title: AI efficiency gains come at a high energy cost
summary: The article discusses how efficiency gains in artificial intelligence come with a significant energy cost. It highlights the technological challenges in reducing energy waste associated with AI systems.

title: AI holds the key to faster battery tech development
summary: This article suggests that artificial intelligence can accelerate battery technology development by transforming materials discovery. It posits that the benefits of this application could outweigh the risks associated with AI's high energy consumption.

title: Legal AI start-up Legora to double headcount
summary: Legal AI start-up Legora plans to double its headcount following a 900% increase in website visits after a recent marketing campaign. The company currently holds a valuation of $5.6 billion.

title: Why the US government shut down Anthropic’s latest Claude AI model - The Conversation
summary: This article discusses the reasons behind the US government's decision to shut down Anthropic's latest Claude AI model. The content explores the implications of this government intervention on a major AI lab.

title: Macron’s G7 Legacy Hangs on Fickle AI Funding and Data Centers - Bloomberg.com
