summary: This paper describes the architecture, key mechanisms, and prototypes for distributed general-purpose agent networks designed to overcome the limitations of single autonomous agents.

title: Treatment Response Optimized Clinical Decision Support AI System via Digital Twin Simulation
summary: Researchers introduce an online adaptive framework for clinical decision support AI systems, optimizing treatment response through treatment effect estimation and patient digital twin simulation.

title: Incumbent Advantage: Brand Bias and Cognitive Manipulation Dynamics in LLM Recommendation Systems
summary: Research examines brand bias and cognitive manipulation dynamics within LLM-powered recommendation systems, using skincare products as a case study to understand brand competition.

title: MapSatisfyBench: Benchmarking Satisfaction-Aware Map Agents through Behavior-Grounded Implicit Decision Factors
summary: MapSatisfyBench is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating satisfaction-aware map agents, focusing on behavior-grounded implicit decision factors in everyday scenarios.

title: Dissecting model behavior through agent trajectories
summary: This research proposes dissecting model behavior through agent trajectories to better understand and improve AI agent performance, particularly considering the role of agent harnesses.

title: Can LLMs Be CEOs? Benchmarking Strategic Resource Reallocation with Multi-Role Agent Simulation
summary: This research introduces a new benchmark using multi-role agent simulation to evaluate LLMs' strategic resource reallocation and decision-making capabilities.

title: LLM-as-Judge in Education: A Curriculum-Grounded Marking Pipeline
summary: Researchers present a curriculum-grounded marking pipeline for deploying LLMs as judges in educational assessment, ensuring systematic grounding of model outputs for high-stakes exams.

title: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
summary: SEAGym is introduced as a new evaluation environment for self-evolving LLM agents, focusing on assessing their improvements through changes in the agent harness.

title: DeepInsight: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure Across the Physical AI Stack
summary: DeepInsight is presented as a unified evaluation infrastructure designed to assess performance across the entire physical AI stack, from foundation models to whole-body control.

title: Surrogate Assisted Pedestrian Protection Design via a Foundation Model Orchestrated Workflow
summary: This research proposes an AI-driven engineering workflow, orchestrated by a foundation model, to assist in pedestrian protection design for crash safety.

title: Closing the Feedback Loop: From Experience Extraction to Insight Governance in Verbal Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper explores closing the feedback loop in verbal reinforcement learning, enabling LLM agents to learn from real-world feedback by extracting and injecting verbal rules from experience.

title: Brick-DICL: Dynamic In-Context Learning for Automated Brick Schema Classification
summary: This research introduces Brick-DICL, a dynamic in-context learning method for automated Brick schema classification, aiming to standardize data integration in Building Management Systems.

title: FinAcumen: Financial Multimodal Reasoning via Self-Evolving Experience Memory Harness
summary: This item introduces FinAcumen, a system that employs a self-evolving experience memory harness to enable financial multimodal reasoning, addressing the statelessness of existing tool-augmented agents.

title: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
summary: This research explores improving LLM web agents by enabling them to reuse web skills through transferable interaction patterns, aiming to reduce latency and cost associated with low-level tool calls.

title: From Brewing to Resolution: Tracing the Internal Lifecycle of Code Reasoning in LLMs
summary: This study investigates the internal lifecycle of code reasoning in LLMs, aiming to understand why models succeed at variable tracking but fail on semantically equivalent loops.

title: Using Cognitive Models to Improve Language Model Simulation of Human Persuasion Games
summary: This research proposes using cognitive models to improve how large language models simulate human behavior in persuasion games, enhancing the breadth of human decision-making represented in AI evaluations and training.

title: FllumaOne: A Code-Native Multimodal CAD Dataset with Executable Programs and Kernel-Validated Feature Histories
summary: This item introduces FllumaOne, a new code-native multimodal CAD dataset designed for editable CAD research, featuring executable programs and kernel-validated feature histories.

title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent
summary: This item introduces EComAgentBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based shopping agents on complex, long-horizon tasks that involve distributed and hidden user intent.

title: LongWebBench: Evaluating Structural and Functional Webpage Generation in Long-Horizon Settings
summary: This item introduces LongWebBench, a new benchmark for evaluating vision-language models on generating structural and functional webpages in long-horizon settings, moving beyond short and static examples.

title: Shattering the Autoregressive Curse: Dynamic Epistemic Entropy Orchestrated Erasable Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
summary: This research presents a novel method called Dynamic Epistemic Entropy Orchestrated Erasable Reinforcement Learning to mitigate the autoregressive curse in LLMs for long-horizon logical reasoning tasks.

title: DecoSearch: Complexity-Aware Routing and Plan-Level Repair for Text-to-SQL
summary: This item introduces DecoSearch, a training-free framework that enhances LLM performance in Text-to-SQL tasks by implementing complexity-aware routing and plan-level repair for multi-step reasoning.

title: A homotopy-type-theoretic generalization of neurosymbolic inference
summary: This paper presents a homotopy-type-theoretic generalization of neurosymbolic inference, expanding the foundational understanding of neurosymbolic systems beyond set-based accounts.

title: FlowRAG: Synergizing Explicit Reasoning via Frequency-Aware Multi-Granularity Graph Flow
summary: This item introduces FlowRAG, a method that synergizes explicit reasoning via frequency-aware multi-granularity graph flow to improve graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) for knowledge-intensive queries.

title: StepGuard: Guarding Web Navigation via Single-Step Calibration
summary: This item introduces StepGuard, a method for guarding web navigation by AI agents using single-step calibration, aiming to reduce fragility and error propagation in following natural language goals.

title: Structural Preservation and the Logical Expressiveness of Graph Neural Networks
summary: This research explores the structural preservation and logical expressiveness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), establishing connections between GNN architectural choices and logical formalisms.

title: MathVis-Fine: Aligning Visual Supervision with Necessity via Progressive Dependency-Guided Training for Multimodal Mathematical Reasoning
summary: This research presents MathVis-Fine, a progressive dependency-guided training approach for multimodal mathematical reasoning that aligns visual supervision with necessity in Chain-of-Thought reasoning.

title: Learn to Quantify Social Interaction with Constraints for Pedestrian Walking
summary: This research focuses on learning to quantify social interaction with constraints for pedestrian walking, which is crucial for improving long-term human path forecasting in autonomous moving platforms.

title: DiagFlowBench: Evaluating How Language Models Handle Off-Procedure Inputs in Grounded Diagnostic Dialogue
summary: This item introduces DiagFlowBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate how language models handle off-procedure inputs in grounded diagnostic dialogues, especially in maintenance operations.

title: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
summary: This item introduces PreAct, a system enabling computer-using AI agents to learn and get faster on repeated tasks, avoiding re-reasoning from scratch each time.

title: How Inference Compute Shapes Frontier LLM Evaluation
summary: This article discusses how inference compute, specifically the amount and allocation of test-time computation, significantly influences the evaluation and reported performance of frontier large language models.

title: Small Initialization Matters for Large Language Models
summary: This research highlights the critical role of small parameter initialization as a determinant of training and emergent intelligence in Large Language Models, beyond just scale, data, and architecture.

title: MoCo-AIS: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Similarity Computation of Vessel Trajectories
summary: This paper introduces MoCo-AIS, a contrastive learning framework designed to efficiently compute the similarity of vessel trajectories, addressing the high computational cost of traditional distance-based methods. This framework aims to improve the analysis of mobility patterns for applications like route pattern extraction and anomaly detection.

title: STAR: SpatioTemporal Adaptive Reward Allocation for Text-to-Image RL Post-Training
summary: This research introduces STAR (SpatioTemporal Adaptive Reward Allocation), a method for reinforcement learning post-training that improves text-to-image generation by adaptively allocating rewards based on the spatio-temporal structure of the generation process. This contrasts with existing methods that apply a single scalar advantage to the entire generative trajectory.

title: LLM Consumer Behavior Theory: Foundations of a Novel Research Field
summary: This paper proposes a new research field, "LLM Consumer Behavior Theory," to investigate how large language models, acting as autonomous agents, make consumption decisions on behalf of users. It aims to address fundamental questions in consumer theory traditionally focused on human decision-makers.

title: LegalHalluLens: Typed Hallucination Auditing and Calibrated Multi-Agent Debate for Trustworthy Legal AI
summary: LegalHalluLens is presented as an auditing system for AI in legal workflows, designed to diagnose and address hallucinations through typed auditing and a calibrated multi-agent debate mechanism. This aims to provide actionable signals for compliance officers to ensure trustworthy deployment of legal AI.

title: ProvenanceGuard: Source-Aware Factuality Verification for MCP-Based LLM Agents
summary: ProvenanceGuard is introduced as a method for source-aware factuality verification in tool-using LLM agents that utilize the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to access heterogeneous evidence sources. This system aims to address the limitations of standard factuality metrics by focusing on the provenance of information.

title: PseudoBench: Measuring How Agentic Auto-Research Fuels Pseudoscience
summary: PseudoBench is a new benchmark designed to measure the susceptibility of Large Language Model-based agents in autonomous scientific research to generating plausible but misleading studies, thereby assessing their potential to fuel pseudoscience. The benchmark aims to evaluate agents' ability to resist such outcomes.

title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
summary: This paper proposes an Agentic AI-based framework utilizing Large Language Models and multi-agent systems to mitigate critical failure modes like premature diagnostic handoff and silent clinical hallucinations in healthcare applications. The framework aims to improve medical reasoning in open-ended conversational agents.

title: A Unified Framework for Context-Aware and Relation-Aware Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This research presents a unified framework for Context-Aware and Relation-Aware Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), aiming to enhance large language models by improving how they incorporate external knowledge from graph structures. The framework addresses limitations of existing entity-centric and chunk-centric approaches.

title: IsabeLLM: Automated Theorem Proving Applied to Formally Verifying Consensus
summary: IsabeLLM explores the application of Automated Theorem Proving, powered by Artificial Intelligence, to formally verify computer systems and consensus mechanisms. The research aims to leverage AI to automate formal verification, traditionally a specialized and labor-intensive task for safety-critical systems.

title: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
summary: This paper introduces a Quality-Aware Self-Distillation method to enhance Graphical User Interface (GUI) grounding for vision-language models, specifically in identifying small target elements and predicting precise screen coordinates. This approach aims to improve the performance of on-policy self-distillation for this coordinate-sensitive task.

title: First Proof Second Batch
summary: This document details the assessment of several AI systems' ability to solve a set of ten research-level mathematics problems from diverse fields, which arose during the contributors' research process. The evaluation aims to gauge the current capabilities of AI in advanced mathematics.

title: Knowledge Reutilization in Meta-Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper investigates knowledge reutilization within meta-reinforcement learning, focusing on how to enable faster adaptation by extracting shared structure from related tasks. It addresses issues like coupling task inference with embodiment-specific control that can reduce sample efficiency.

title: Your AI Travel Agent Would Book You a Bullfight: An Agentic Benchmark for Implicit Animal Welfare in Frontier AI Models
summary: This paper introduces an "Agentic Benchmark" designed to evaluate the implicit animal welfare reasoning of frontier AI models acting as agents, such as travel planners. The benchmark aims to assess how agents' actions, like booking travel, align with animal welfare considerations, beyond textual responses.

title: WEQA: Wearable hEalth Question Answering with Query-Adaptive Agentic Reasoning
summary: WEQA (Wearable hEalth Question Answering) is introduced as a system that leverages query-adaptive agentic reasoning to enable language models to answer medical questions using high-dimensional and longitudinal wearable health data. It aims to address the challenges of processing complex, continuous sensor data for health insights.

title: Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology Digital Twins Through Agentic Discovery of Hybrid Structure
summary: This research proposes learning personalized cardiac electrophysiology digital twins through "Agentic Discovery," a method that uses AI agents to identify appropriate hybrid physics-neural model structures for each patient. This approach aims to automate the process of building complex biological models, traditionally requiring deep domain expertise.

title: The Stanford EDGAR Filings Dataset: Reconstructing U.S. Corporate and Financial Disclosures into Layout-Faithful and Token-Efficient Pretraining Data
summary: This paper introduces the Stanford EDGAR Filings Dataset, a new resource for pretraining large language models, created by reconstructing U.S. corporate and financial disclosures into a layout-faithful and token-efficient format. The dataset addresses the scarcity of high-quality, long-context training data for LLMs.

title: Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers
summary: This paper introduces "Fixed-Point Reasoners," a type of stable and adaptive deep looped transformer architecture designed to improve compositional reasoning tasks. These architectures provide an inductive bias towards learning step-by-step procedures, addressing the stability challenges of deep looped models.

title: Correct When Paired, Wrong When Split: Decoupling and Editing Modality-Specific Neurons in MLLMs
summary: This research investigates "editing decoupling failure" in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and proposes a method for decoupling and editing modality-specific neurons. The goal is to efficiently update MLLM knowledge while preventing issues where knowledge edits in one modality incorrectly affect others.

title: Diagnosing and Repairing Shape-Prior Shortcuts in Long-Range Single-Shot Fringe Projection Profilometry
summary: This research focuses on diagnosing and repairing "shape-prior shortcuts" in learning-based single-shot fringe projection profilometry (FPP), particularly in the challenging long-range regime. The paper addresses issues like low signal-to-noise ratio and degraded physical ground truth that affect traditional methods.

title: Informative Missingness to Generate Irregular Clinical Time Series
summary: This paper proposes a method to generate irregular clinical time series by modeling "informative missingness" in electronic health records, where the absence of a test order can be as significant as the measurement itself. This approach aims to better reflect clinicians' decisions and patient physiology in generated data.

title: Models Take Notes at Prefill: KV Cache Can Be Editable and Composable
summary: This research proposes an editable and composable KV cache mechanism for large language models, allowing more efficient and flexible reuse of prefill data during inference.

title: The Critical Role of Model Selection in Causal Inference: A Comparative Analysis of Classification Models within the InferBERT Framework for Pharmacovigilance
summary: This study analyzes the critical role of classification model selection within the InferBERT framework for causal inference in pharmacovigilance, distinguishing adverse drug events.

title: Probing, Fusion, and Trustworthiness: A Systematic Evaluation of Foundation Model Representations for Multimodal Cancer Analysis
summary: This work systematically evaluates the generalizability and trustworthiness of foundation model representations for multimodal cancer analysis in computational pathology tasks.

title: MODE: Modality-Decomposed Expert-Level Mixed-Precision Quantization for MoE Multimodal LLMs
summary: This paper introduces MODE, a modality-decomposed expert-level mixed-precision quantization method to reduce GPU memory costs for Mixture-of-Experts Multimodal Large Language Models.

title: Noise-Driven Escape from Metastable Phases explains Grokking in Deep Neural Networks
summary: This research explains the phenomenon of 'grokking' in deep neural networks by attributing it to noise-driven escape from metastable phases under L2 regularization.

title: Towards Fast GNN Surrogates for CO2 Migration in Complex Geological Formations
summary: This work proposes an end-to-end graph neural surrogate tailored for fast and accurate forecasting of CO2 plume migration in complex geological storage formations.

title: Verified Detection and Prevention of Concurrency Anomalies in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Systems
summary: This research models state sharing in multi-agent LLM systems to formally define and prevent concurrency anomalies under deterministic-generation semantics.

title: Finsler Geometry, Graph Neural Networks, and You
summary: This paper explores the use of Finsler geometry and the Finsler Laplacian as a nonlinear alternative to the graph Laplacian in Graph Neural Networks.

title: Constrained Diffusion Models with Primal-Dual Inference
summary: This paper introduces constrained diffusion models with primal-dual inference to sample from optimal distributions of entropy-regularized optimization problems with average constraints.

title: PowerOPD: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation with Bounded Power Transformation
summary: This paper introduces PowerOPD, a method to stabilize on-policy distillation for large language models by using bounded power transformation to mitigate training pathologies.

title: Rift: A Conflict Signature for Deception in Language Models
summary: This research investigates whether deceptive language models, which know the truth but lie, leave an internal signature that distinguishes their behavior from honest errors.

title: Rethinking Groups in Critic-Free RLVR
summary: This paper rethinks group-based rollout generation in critic-free reinforcement learning methods for post-training large language models to improve data efficiency.

title: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
summary: This technical report focuses on the challenges and data requirements for training computer-use agents (CUAs) that interact with graphical desktop environments through screenshots and actions.

title: Decision-Driven Geosteering Under Uncertainty: A Unified Framework for Sequential Decision Optimization
summary: This work presents a unified, uncertainty-aware geosteering framework that integrates particle filtering for sequential decision optimization in drilling operations.

title: Counterfactual Optimization of Baseball Pitch Sequences and Estimation of Its Impact on Season-Level Statistics
summary: This study uses counterfactual optimization to analyze and estimate the impact of baseball pitch sequences on long-term season-level statistics, beyond single plate appearance outcomes.

title: MM++: Unsupervised Scale-Invariant Multilayer OOD Detection via Top-K Gated Feature Fusion
summary: This paper introduces MM++, an unsupervised, scale-invariant framework for multilayer Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection achieved through top-K gated feature fusion.

title: Performance-Driven Environment Abstraction with Multi-Timescale Learning
summary: This research investigates performance-driven environment abstraction for decision-making in large Markov decision processes, optimizing decision quality through multi-timescale learning.

title: The Discrete-Log Clock: How a Transformer Learns Modular Multiplication
summary: This paper explores how transformers learn modular multiplication, revealing that the previously observed dense Fourier spectrum of learned embeddings is an analytical artifact.

title: Discrete Autoregressive Transformer for Generative Mechanism Synthesis
summary: This work applies a discrete autoregressive transformer to generative mechanism synthesis, addressing the engineering problem of matching coupler curves to prescribed trajectories.

title: Amortized Probabilistic Retrieval of Atmospheric CO2 from OCO-2 Spectra Using Deep Learning with Laplace Approximations and Normalizing Flows
summary: This research uses deep learning with Laplace approximations and normalizing flows for amortized probabilistic retrieval of atmospheric CO2 from OCO-2 satellite spectra.

title: Memory-Efficient Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Safety-Critical Control in Adversarial Spacecraft Proximity Operations
summary: This research proposes a memory-efficient meta-reinforcement learning method for adaptive, safety-critical control in autonomous spacecraft proximity operations, utilizing input-constrained control barrier functions.

title: MorphStrata: Layer-Specific Perturbations for Generating Morphence Students in Time-Series Moving Target Defense
summary: This paper introduces MorphStrata, a method using layer-specific perturbations to generate robust "student" models for time-series moving target defense, aiming to mitigate gradient-based adversarial attacks.

title: Toward Controllable Catalyst Inverse Design via Large-Scale Autoregressive Pretraining
summary: This research explores using large-scale autoregressive pretraining to achieve controllable inverse design of heterogeneous catalysts, addressing the complexity of catalyst surfaces and interactions.

title: Credibility-Weighted Pricing of Autonomous Vehicle Liability Under Operational Design Domain Shift
summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical Bayesian credibility framework for credibility-weighted pricing of autonomous vehicle liability, addressing challenges like sparse experience and shifting operational design domains.

title: ResAware: Cross-Environment Website Fingerprinting via Resource-Privileged Distillation
summary: This research introduces ResAware, a method for cross-environment website fingerprinting using resource-privileged distillation, aiming to improve attack accuracy in real-world settings.

title: CheckMIABench: Firm Foundations For Membership Inference Attacks on Language Models
summary: This paper introduces CheckMIABench, a framework designed to provide robust and clean evaluations for membership inference attacks (MIAs) on language models, addressing previous literature's evaluation difficulties.

title: Perron--Frobenius Operator Matching for Generative Modeling
summary: This paper introduces Perron--Frobenius Operator Matching (PFOM), a new generative framework that aligns density evolution using the integral PF operator, encompassing flow, diffusion, and jump models.

title: Multi-Adapter PPO: A Cross-Attention Enhanced Wavelength Selection Framework for LIBS Quantitative Analysis
summary: This paper presents the Multi-Adapter PPO framework, which uses cross-attention to enhance wavelength selection for Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) quantitative analysis, addressing challenges in high-dimensional spectral data.

title: Online LLM Selection via Constrained Bandits with Time-Varying Demand
summary: This research proposes using constrained bandits for online LLM selection in edge-cloud inference systems, aiming to optimize service quality and resource utilization by choosing the appropriate LLM for diverse tasks.

title: Reconfigurable Computing Challenge: Transformer for Jet Tagging on Versal AI Engines
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of deploying quantized, integer-only Transformer models for jet tagging at CERN LHC on resource-constrained AMD Versal AI Engines, focusing on reconfigurable computing.

title: When the Next Step Is Not One Step: Distribution-Aware Execution Modeling for Concurrent Go Programs
summary: This research explores distribution-aware execution modeling for concurrent Go programs, aiming to predict the next steps despite nondeterministic schedulers, improving upon models trained with single labels.

title: Geometry-Aware Post-Hoc Uncertainty Quantification in Operator Learning
summary: This paper proposes a geometry-aware post-hoc uncertainty quantification method for operator learning, addressing the limitations of deterministic predictions in neural operators for tasks involving geometric variability.

title: FoundCause: Causal Discovery with Latent Confounders from Observational Data
summary: This research introduces FoundCause, an amortized causal discovery model trained on synthetic data that can infer causal graphs and latent confounders directly from observational data.

title: Learning to Refine Hidden States for Reliable LLM Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes ReLAR, a reinforcement-guided latent refinement framework designed to iteratively refine the hidden states of large language models, improving their reasoning reliability in complex multi-step tasks.

title: MGUP: A Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy for Stochastic Optimization
summary: This paper introduces MGUP (Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy), a novel mechanism for stochastic optimization that provides fine-grained control and convergence guarantees for training large language models.

title: Non-negative Matrix Factorisation with Topological Regularisation
summary: This research investigates non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) with topological regularisation to learn more interpretable bases by structuring the learned basis functions.

title: Offline Preference-Based Trajectory Evaluation
summary: This paper proposes a method for offline preference-based trajectory evaluation for agentic systems, aiming to improve statistical efficiency by incorporating partial progress information beyond terminal success.

title: Continuous-time Optimal Stopping through Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research applies Deep Reinforcement Learning to solve continuous-time optimal stopping problems, addressing the limitations of traditional simulation-based solvers that discretize stopping decisions.

title: Reversal Q-Learning
summary: This paper proposes Reversal Q-Learning, a new off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that trains a flow policy based on prior data, building on iterative generative modeling techniques.

title: LLM Features Can Hurt GNNs: Concatenation Interference on Homophilous Graph Benchmarks
summary: This research finds that adding LLM-generated node features to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) via pure input concatenation can hurt accuracy on homophilous graph benchmarks, contrary to common reports.

title: A Risk Decomposition Framework for Pre-Hoc Fine-Tuning Prediction
summary: This paper proposes a risk decomposition framework for predicting the performance of LLM fine-tuning before full training, aiming to reduce costs associated with this process.

title: Physics-Constrained Neural Networks for Improved Short-Term Weather Forecasting: A Case Study over the South Pacific
summary: This study introduces enhancements to physics-constrained neural networks for improving the accuracy and stability of hybrid short-term weather forecasting models over the South Pacific.

title: TuneAhead: Predicting Fine-tuning Performance Before Full Training Begins
summary: This paper explores methods to predict the performance of large language model fine-tuning before full training begins, addressing the compute-intensive and error-prone nature of the process.

title: Handling Feature Heterogeneity with Learnable Graph Patches
summary: This research proposes using learnable graph patches to address feature heterogeneity, a significant challenge in constructing universal pre-trained Graph Foundation Models.

title: ASTEROID: A Spatiotemporal Information Transformer for Forecasting Multi-Step Time Series of Molecular Dynamics
summary: This work introduces ASTEROID, a spatiotemporal information transformer, developed for forecasting multi-step time series of molecular dynamics simulations, addressing computational demands.

title: EnvRL: Learn from Environment Dynamics in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces EnvRL, a method for agentic reinforcement learning that enables Large Language Models to learn from environment dynamics, addressing the challenge of sparse rewards in long-horizon tasks.

title: Delta-Based Target Reformulation for Short-Term Electricity Load Forecasting Using LSTM and Transformer Models
summary: This research proposes a delta-based target reformulation method for short-term electricity load forecasting, utilizing LSTM and Transformer models to improve accuracy in non-stationary conditions.

title: Could AI tell you where you left your keys?
summary: This article describes a new spatial memory system designed for robots, enabling them to efficiently capture and recall details about objects encountered during environmental exploration.

title: MemSlides: A Hierarchical Memory Driven Agent Framework for Personalized Slide Generation with Multi-turn Local Revision
summary: This paper proposes MemSlides, a hierarchical memory-driven agent framework designed for personalized slide generation with multi-turn local revision capabilities.

title: PromptMN: Pseudo Prompting Language
summary: This paper introduces PromptMN, a pseudo prompting language designed to improve the clarity and robustness of prompts for generative AI, particularly in agentic and software development workflows.

title: RepSelect: Robust LLM Unlearning via Representation Selectivity
summary: This research introduces RepSelect, a method for robust LLM unlearning via representation selectivity, aiming to make models deeply forget specific knowledge without losing general capabilities.

title: From Parasocial Scripts to Dyadic Persistence in Autonomous AI-Agent Communities
summary: This study investigates whether parasocial relational cues exist in online communities where both sides are autonomous AI agents, analyzing their interactions and dyadic persistence.

title: Self-Generated Error Training for Token Editing in Diffusion Language Models
summary: This research studies self-generated error training for token editing in Diffusion Language Models, focusing on how to improve the model's ability to revise committed tokens during decoding.

title: Revisiting LLM Adaptation for 3D CT Report Generation: A Study of Scaling and Diagnostic Priors
summary: This study revisits the adaptation of large language models for 3D CT report generation in the medical domain, exploring scaling and diagnostic priors for volumetric image interpretation.

title: Speaking in Self-Assessing Tongues: On the Verbalized Confidence of LLMs in Machine Translation
summary: This research thoroughly studies the reliability of large language models' verbalized confidence in their own outputs when used for machine translation tasks.

title: MLLP-VRAIN UPV system for the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task
summary: This work describes the MLLP-VRAIN UPV system's participation in the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task, utilizing Parakeet and Qwen 3.5 models for a robust cascaded solution.

title: Are you speaking my languages? On spoken language adherence in multimodal LLMs
summary: This research investigates spoken language adherence in multimodal LLMs for Automatic Speech Recognition, addressing the issue of models misidentifying output languages and proposing a solution.

title: Examining the Limits of Word2Vec with Toki Pona
summary: This study examines the limits of Word2Vec's effectiveness in generating semantic embeddings by testing its ability to capture semantic relationships in Toki Pona, a language with an extremely reduced vocabulary.

title: Do Large Language Models Always Tell The Same Stories?
summary: This research investigates the diversity of stories generated by large language models, exploring whether these models consistently produce varied outputs or tend to tell the same stories.

title: Translating the Untranslatable: An Operationalizable Ontology for Untranslatability
summary: This research proposes an operationalizable ontology for untranslatability, aiming to explore and address cases where meaning cannot be directly preserved across languages in NLP and machine translation.

title: Implicit vs. Explicit Prompting Strategies for LVLMs in Referential Communication
summary: This study compares implicit and explicit prompting strategies for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to understand how they coordinate on referring expressions, replicating previous findings while controlling for task differences.

title: NarrativeWorldBench: A Frontier-Saturated Benchmark and a Latent World Model for Long-Horizon Co-Creative Audio Drama
summary: This item introduces NarrativeWorldBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate 21 frontier and classical language models on their ability to handle long-horizon co-creative audio drama tasks, where current LLMs often fail.

title: MODE-RAG: Manifold Outlier Diagnosis and Energy-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation
summary: This paper presents MODE-RAG, a new evaluation method using manifold outlier diagnosis and energy-based assessment to address issues like cross-modal hallucinations and fabrications in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (M-RAG).

title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
summary: This research introduces AIPatient Arena, a new evaluation framework grounded in Electronic Health Records (EHR) to assess large language models' capabilities in realistic, interactive, and sequential clinical consultation workflows.

title: Decoding Hidden Deception in Reasoning LLMs: Activation Explainers for Deception Auditing
summary: This research explores a method using activation explainers for 'deception auditing' to decode hidden deceptive behaviors in reasoning large language models, addressing a serious safety concern as LLMs gain stronger reasoning capabilities.

title: Evaluating Second-Order Bias of LLMs Through Epistemic Entitlement
summary: This study evaluates the 'second-order bias' of large language models by examining how they exhibit social biases when acting as judges of biased content, a subtlety not captured by current bias evaluation methods.

title: Scaling Enterprise Agent Routing: Degradation, Diagnosis, and Recovery
summary: This work investigates how the accuracy of enterprise LLM assistants degrades as they scale to route user requests to a growing library of specialized tools, analyzing degradation, diagnosis, and recovery strategies for agent routing.

title: An expressivity analysis of hierarchical modelling in deep transformers via bounded-depth grammars
summary: This paper presents an expressivity analysis of hierarchical modeling in deep transformers using bounded-depth grammars, exploring how these architectures derive their power from forming hierarchical representations.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
summary: This study develops an evaluation framework to assess large language models' abilities in predicting addressee, turn-change, and next speaker in multimodal, multi-party conversations, comparing them against supervised models.

title: The Benchmark Illusion: Pruned LLMs Can Pass Multiple Choice but Fail to Answer
summary: This paper highlights the 'Benchmark Illusion,' demonstrating that while pruned large language models may pass standard multiple-choice evaluations, they can fail to answer the same questions in open-ended generation, revealing limitations in current benchmarks.

title: OPD-Evolver: Cultivating Holistic Agent Evolver via On-Policy Distillation
summary: This research introduces OPD-Evolver, a system for cultivating holistic agent evolution through on-policy distillation, focusing on how self-evolving agents can learn to adapt and select useful experiences beyond just retaining memory.

title: Prompt Perturbation for Reliable LLM Evaluation over Comparison Graphs
summary: This paper proposes using prompt perturbation with comparison graphs to enhance the reliability of large language model evaluation, particularly for open-ended tasks where pairwise evaluation is common.

title: From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning
summary: This research introduces a novel approach where an LLM acts as an 'LLM-as-Environment' to design training environments for Reinforcement Learning (RL) with multi-agent reasoning, automating the configuration process for policy improvement.

title: Bridging Functional Correctness and Runtime Efficiency Gaps in LLM-Based Code Translation
summary: This work addresses the functional correctness and runtime efficiency gaps in large language model-based code translation systems, emphasizing the increasing importance of runtime efficiency given the constraints of Moore's law.

title: SuCo: Sufficiency-guided Continuous Adaptive Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SuCo, a sufficiency-guided continuous adaptive reasoning approach for Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) to reduce computational costs by generating more concise Chain-of-Thoughts without compromising performance.

title: LLMs Infer Cultural Context but Fail to Apply It When Responding
summary: This research investigates how large language models infer cultural context but often fail to apply it in their responses, revealing that they tend to overrepresent dominant cultures and marginalize others.

title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports
summary: This study reveals 'The Slop Paradox,' demonstrating how AI-assisted clinical documentation tools using large language models can lead to information degradation and erosion of clinical uncertainty when rewriting radiology reports.

title: Improving low-resource ASR using bilingual fine-tuning with language identification: a cross-linguistic evaluation
summary: This study explores improving low-resource Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) by using bilingual fine-tuning combined with language identification, evaluating its effectiveness across a diverse set of nine language pairs.

title: When Multiple Scripts Matter: Evaluating ASR in Clinical Settings
summary: This paper examines the challenges of evaluating Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) in non-English clinical settings, particularly due to multiscript variability which can cause conventional string-matching metrics to underestimate performance.

title: Perceptual compensation for tonal context in self-supervised speech models
summary: This study investigates the extent to which the wav2vec2.0 self-supervised speech model architecture exhibits perceptual compensation for tonal context, through a pseudo-replication of an experiment on Mandarin Chinese tones.

title: Environment-Grounded Automated Prompt Optimization for LLM Game Agents
summary: This paper introduces an automated prompt optimization framework designed to improve the performance of LLM agents in interactive environments by refining their observation-to-action pipeline.

title: GameCraft-Bench: Can Agents Build Playable Games End-to-End in a Real Game Engine?
summary: This paper introduces GameCraft-Bench to evaluate the capability of AI coding agents in generating playable games end-to-end within a real game engine from natural-language specifications.

title: Dynamic Rollout Editing for Reducing Overthinking in RL-Trained Reasoning Models
summary: This research proposes Dynamic Rollout Editing to reduce "overthinking" in RL-trained reasoning models, which is the tendency of LLMs to generate unnecessary reasoning after reaching a correct answer.

title: ChLogic: Evaluating Robustness of Logical Reasoning in Chinese Expressions
summary: This paper introduces ChLogic, a new English-Chinese aligned benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of large language models' logical reasoning capabilities in Chinese expressions.

title: Learning task-specific subspaces via interventional post-training of speech foundation models
summary: This research explores learning task-specific subspaces through interventional post-training of speech foundation models to optimize their representations for various downstream speech tasks.

title: Fine-tuning LLMs for Passive Depression Severity Estimation from AI Mental Health Dialogue
summary: This paper investigates fine-tuning large language models to passively estimate depression severity from AI mental health dialogues, aiming to improve early detection of symptom changes.

title: VoidPadding: Let [VOID] Handle Padding in Masked Diffusion Language Models so that [EOS] Can Focus on Semantic Termination
summary: This research introduces VoidPadding, a method for Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) that uses a dedicated [VOID] token for padding, allowing the [EOS] token to exclusively signify semantic termination.

title: When English Isn't the Best Teacher: Source Language Effects in Cross-Lingual In-Context Learning
summary: This study explores the impact of source language effects on cross-lingual in-context learning in multilingual NLP, challenging assumptions about transfer quality in few-shot settings.

title: Compositional Skill Routing for LLM Agents: Decompose, Retrieve, and Compose
summary: This paper introduces the "Compositional Skill Routing" problem and a method for LLM agents to decompose complex user queries, retrieve relevant skills, and compose them to perform tasks.

title: ConSA: Controllable Sparsity in Hybrid Attention via Learnable Allocation
summary: This research presents ConSA, a method for achieving controllable sparsity in hybrid attention architectures through learnable allocation, aiming to improve the efficiency of LLM inference.

title: Security and Privacy Prompts in the Wild: What Users Ask LLMs and How LLMs Respond
summary: This study analyzes user queries regarding security and privacy directed at large language models and evaluates how these LLMs respond to such prompts in real-world scenarios.

title: HistoRAG: Embedding Historical Methodology in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Through Critical Technical Practice
summary: This paper introduces HistoRAG, a framework that embeds historical methodology into Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to adapt them for interpretive disciplines like historical studies.

title: Unintended Effects of Geographic Conditioning in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates the unintended regional biases and "location leakage" phenomenon in large language models caused by geographic conditioning based on user metadata.

title: Learning from the Self-future: On-policy Self-distillation for dLLMs
summary: This research explores applying On-policy Self-distillation (OPSD) to diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) for post-training, a method previously effective for autoregressive LLMs.

title: RubricsTree: Scalable and Evolving Open-Ended Evaluation of Personal Health Agents across Health Memory and Medical Skills
summary: This paper introduces RubricsTree, a scalable and evolving framework for the open-ended evaluation of LLM-empowered personal health agents based on health memory and medical skills.

title: Zone of Proximal Policy Optimization: Teacher in Prompts, Not Gradients
summary: This research introduces Zone of Proximal Policy Optimization, a knowledge distillation method that uses prompts instead of gradients to transfer a teacher model's competence to a smaller student model, aiming to improve generalization.

title: Variable-Width Transformers
summary: This research proposes Variable-Width Transformers, an architectural innovation that allows for varying widths across transformer layers to optimize parameter and computation allocation, unlike traditional constant-width designs.

title: Securing Multi-Agent GIS Systems: Risk Evaluation and Prompt Hardening Optimization
summary: This work presents a security framework for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating risks in multi-agent Geographic Information Systems (GIS) that use complex conversational and spatial analysis.

title: Not Truly Multilingual: Script Consistency as a Missing Dimension in VLM Evaluation
summary: This paper critiques current multilingual VLM evaluations for overlooking multi-script languages and introduces PuMVR, a new benchmark designed to assess script consistency in Vision-Language Models.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Continuous Edge Inference for Fine-Grained Roadside Perception
summary: This research examines deployment challenges for continuous AI inference on resource-constrained edge hardware, highlighting issues like temporal instability and thermal throttling that conventional benchmarks fail to address.

title: Landsat-Sentinel-2 Algal Bloom Mapping Using Vision Transformers: Model Description, Implementation, and Examples
summary: This paper describes the use and implementation of Vision Transformers for mapping coastal algal blooms, utilizing satellite imagery from Landsat-8/9 and Sentinel-2 A/B/C for frequent and spatially detailed monitoring.

title: GeoDisaster: Benchmarking Orchestrated Agents for Operational Disaster Geo-Intelligence
summary: This paper introduces GeoDisaster, a new benchmark for evaluating orchestrated AI agents in operational disaster geo-intelligence, focusing on their ability for tool-grounded spatial reasoning and structured decision-making.

title: Pulling The REINS: Training-Free Safety Alignment of Video Diffusion Models via Representation Steering
summary: This work presents "REINS," a training-free method for safety alignment of open-weight video diffusion models, aiming to prevent the generation of unsafe content through representation steering without degrading general capability.

title: Training LLMs with Reinforcement Learning over Digital Twin Representations for Reasoning-Intensive Surgical VideoQA
summary: This research proposes a method for training Large Language Models with Reinforcement Learning over digital twin representations to improve reasoning-intensive surgical video question answering across semantic, spatial, and temporal dimensions.

title: Pareto LoRA: Mitigating Modality Imbalance in Unified Multimodal Models via Pareto-Optimal Gradient Integration
summary: This paper introduces Pareto LoRA, a method that uses Pareto-optimal gradient integration to mitigate modality imbalance during the instruction tuning of unified multimodal models.

title: Reasoning Text-to-Video Retrieval for Operating Room Clips via Action-Driven Digital Twins
summary: This research explores reasoning text-to-video retrieval for operating room clips, using action-driven digital twins to enhance OR safety by enabling the inspection of specific events.

title: SierpinskiCam: Camera-Controlled Video Retaking with Sierpinski Triangle Pattern Cues
summary: This paper introduces SierpinskiCam, a novel method for camera-controlled video retaking that generates new renderings from a single monocular video using Sierpinski Triangle Pattern Cues.

title: FATE: Pillar Encoding and Frequency-Aware Training for Event-Based Object Detection
summary: This paper proposes FATE, a new method incorporating Pillar Encoding and Frequency-Aware Training to address the challenges of object detection using sparse and asynchronous event camera data.

title: Geometry-Consistent Endoscopic Representations for Image-Guided Navigation via Structured Foundation Model Adaptation
summary: This research focuses on developing geometry-consistent endoscopic representations for improved image-guided navigation, utilizing structured foundation model adaptation to overcome challenges like limited depth cues and tissue deformation.

title: Learning a Maximum Entropy Model for Visual Textures using Diffusion
summary: This paper proposes a method for learning a maximum entropy model for visual textures using diffusion, capturing the essential statistics of spatially homogeneous image regions with repeated elements.

title: Bayesian Magnetic Resonance Joint Image Reconstruction and Uncertainty Quantification using Sparsity Prior Models and Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling
summary: This paper proposes a Bayesian framework for magnetic resonance image reconstruction and uncertainty quantification, using sparsity prior models and Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling to solve linear inverse problems.

title: DriveJudge: Rethinking Autonomous Driving Evaluation with Vision-Language Models
summary: This work introduces "DriveJudge," a new evaluation framework that rethinks autonomous driving assessment by using Vision-Language Models to provide more reliable and interpretable policy evaluation.

title: MeiBRD: Meta-Learning Intraoperative Biomechanical Residual Deformation
summary: This paper introduces MeiBRD, a meta-learning approach designed to improve intraoperative liver registration by addressing biomechanical residual deformation caused by soft-tissue movement and sparse measurements.

title: Improving and Evaluating Hand-Object Interaction Detection
summary: This paper contributes to Hand-Object Interaction (HOI) understanding by introducing HOI-DETR, a new model for detecting interactions, aiming to advance areas like action perception, 3D reconstruction, and robotics.

title: TerraTransfer: Learning End-to-End Driving Policies Without Expert Demonstrations
summary: This paper introduces TerraTransfer, a new method enabling the learning of end-to-end autonomous driving policies without requiring expensive expert demonstrations, addressing a major cost in current training paradigms.

title: Visuals Lie, Consistency Speaks: Disentangling Spatial Attention from Reliability in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research challenges the Attention-Confidence Assumption in Vision-Language Models, exploring how to disentangle spatial attention from model reliability and address hallucination in multimodal foundation models.

title: Bridging Spatial And Frequency Views For Disaster Assessment: Benefits And Limitations
summary: This paper examines the benefits and limitations of bridging spatial and frequency views in deep learning methods for rapid building damage assessment from satellite imagery, crucial for disaster response.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Semi-Supervised Image Classification with Multi-Feature Aggregation
summary: This research proposes using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with multi-feature aggregation for semi-supervised image classification, leveraging deep learning architectures like CNNs for feature extraction.

title: Attention Alignment Between Humans and Vision-Language Models
summary: This study compares the spatial attention maps of six vision-language models with human fixation patterns to understand the alignment of attention mechanisms between humans and AI models.

title: Enhancing Pathological VLMs with Cross-scale Reasoning
summary: This research proposes a method to enhance pathological Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by incorporating cross-scale reasoning, enabling them to integrate evidence from different magnification levels for more accurate diagnosis.

title: CIAN: Multi-Stage Framework for Event-Enriched Image Captioning via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper introduces CIAN (Contextual Image-Article Narrator), a multi-stage framework for event-enriched image captioning that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to incorporate broader context beyond visible content.

title: Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Silhouette-Guided Animal Art
summary: This research explores Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation for creating silhouette-guided animal art, aiming to improve generative AI's ability to interpret ambiguous shapes, similar to human pareidolia.

title: LADBench: A Benchmark for Logical Fault Detection in Images
summary: LADBench is introduced as a new benchmark to evaluate the logical reasoning capabilities of Large Vision Language Models (VLMs) for detecting physical and social common sense faults in images.

title: UoU: A Universal Fingerprint Foundation Model Based on Large-Scale Unsupervised Learning
summary: UoU is presented as a universal fingerprint foundation model based on large-scale unsupervised learning, designed to overcome limitations of task-specific pipelines in fingerprint recognition.

title: Spatio-Temporal Fusion Model for Standard View Classification of Echocardiographic Videos
summary: This paper introduces a spatio-temporal fusion model for the automated classification of standard echocardiographic views, addressing challenges like limited datasets and model performance in video-level architectures.

title: Contact-Based Fringe Projection Profilometry for High-Resolution 3-D Surface Measurement of Reflective and Transparent Objects
summary: This paper presents a contact-based 3-D surface measurement method utilizing a Digital Fringe Projection (DFP) system, suitable for reflective and transparent objects and related to vision-based tactile sensing.

title: WeaveLA: Event Driven Cross-Subtask Latent Memory Weaving for Repetitive Robot Manipulation
summary: WeaveLA introduces an event-driven cross-subtask latent memory weaving mechanism to improve Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies for repetitive robot manipulation by enabling information routing across sub-task boundaries.

title: StereoFactory: A Unified Merging Framework for Robust Stereo Matching
summary: StereoFactory is presented as a unified merging framework for robust stereo matching, offering a scalable post-hoc alternative to costly retraining by integrating knowledge from specialized models.

title: Theoretical Grounding of Out-Of-Distribution Detection With Reinforcement Learning Optimizer
summary: This research provides theoretical grounding for Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) detection using a Reinforcement Learning Optimizer, aiming for models to adapt to evolving data and reject OOD examples in dynamic environments.

title: GeneralVLA-2: Geometry-Aware Reconstruction and Governed Memory for Robot Planning
summary: GeneralVLA-2 improves generalist vision-language-action systems for robot planning by introducing geometry-aware reconstruction and a governed memory mechanism to enhance reliability in generating robot trajectories.

title: SPHINX: First Explain, Then Explore
summary: SPHINX is a method for generating adversarial driving scenarios to evaluate and improve decision-making systems in autonomous vehicles, building upon prior knowledge from LLMs and VLMs.

title: OmniDrive: An LLM-Choreographed Multi-Agent World Model with Unified Latent Co-Compression for Multi-View Driving Video Generation
summary: OmniDrive is an LLM-choreographed multi-agent world model designed for multi-view driving video generation, addressing challenges in heterogeneous control injection and cross-view fusion for autonomous driving systems.

title: Reinforcing Dual-Path Reasoning in Spatial Vision Language Models
summary: This research aims to improve complex spatial reasoning in Spatial Vision Language Models by reinforcing dual-path reasoning, addressing challenges in multi-step inference over depth, distance, and scene relations.

title: TaFD: Threat-Aware Frequency Decoupling for Adversarial Robustness against Heterogeneous Attacks
summary: TaFD introduces a threat-aware frequency decoupling method to enhance adversarial robustness in deep learning against heterogeneous attacks, addressing the negative transfer issue in joint adversarial training.

title: Universal Image Restoration via Internalized Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: This research proposes universal image restoration through internalized Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, aiming to improve the recovery of high-quality images from complex, mixed degradations.

title: RT-Counter: Real-Time Text-Guided Open-Vocabulary Object Counting
summary: RT-Counter is a system for real-time text-guided open-vocabulary object counting, designed to count objects based on natural language descriptions and improve fine-grained spatial understanding.

title: Geometric Consistency Protocol for Foundation Model Features in Multi-View Satellite Imagery
summary: This paper proposes a geometric consistency protocol for evaluating foundation model features in multi-view satellite imagery, aimed at establishing robust benchmarking for remote sensing applications.

title: TivTok: Broadcasting Time-Invariant Tokens for Scalable Video Tokenization
summary: Introduces TivTok, a method for scalable video tokenization to improve computational efficiency and video length in video generation.

title: Test-Time Training for Robust Text-Guided Open-Vocabulary Object Counting
summary: Presents a test-time training method to improve the robustness of Text-guided Open-vocabulary Object Counting (TOOC) in challenging real-world images.

title: Flux-Guard: Facial Identity Protection using diffusion models
summary: Introduces Flux-Guard, a method using diffusion models for facial identity protection to mitigate privacy risks from widespread face recognition systems.

title: RAVA: Retrieval-Augmented Viewpoint Alignment for Subject-Driven Image Generation
summary: Proposes RAVA, a retrieval-augmented method to achieve reliable viewpoint control in subject-driven image generation.

title: Divide, Deliberate, Decide: A Multi-Agent Framework for Fine-Grained Egocentric Action Recognition
summary: Introduces "Divide, Deliberate, Decide," a multi-agent framework for fine-grained egocentric action recognition using Vision-Language Models (VLMs).

title: Bounding Box Label Propagation for Re-Annotation of Document Layout Analysis Datasets
summary: Proposes a method using bounding box label propagation to reduce the time and cost associated with re-annotating document layout analysis datasets.

title: MambaCount: Efficient Text-guided Open-vocabulary Object Counting with Spatial Sparse State Space Duality Block
summary: Introduces MambaCount, an efficient method for Text-guided Open-vocabulary Object Counting (TOOC) in dense scenes using a spatial sparse state space duality block.

title: Do We Really Need Diffusion? A Fast U-Net for Paired Medical Image Translation
summary: Investigates the use of a fast U-Net architecture for paired medical image translation, specifically for estimating MRI-signal fat fraction without specialized sequences.

title: See First, Answer Later: Visual Evidence Pre-Alignment via Sufficiency-Driven RL
summary: Proposes "See First, Answer Later," a method using sufficiency-driven reinforcement learning for visual evidence pre-alignment to improve MLLM consistency with images.

title: SegTME-UNI2: A Foundation Model-Based Framework for Generalisable Multiclass Cell Segmentation and LLM-Driven Tumour Microenvironment Characterisation in Histopathology
summary: Presents SEGTME-UNI2, a foundation model-based framework for multiclass cell segmentation and LLM-driven tumour microenvironment characterisation in histopathology.

title: Vision-language models for chest radiography do not always need the image
summary: Highlights that medical vision-language models for chest radiography can achieve high accuracy by exploiting finding-name priors rather than always analyzing the image, challenging current evaluation methods.

title: Heterogeneous SAR-optical fusion for near-real-time land use and land cover mapping under cloud contamination: A novel framework and global benchmark dataset
summary: Introduces a novel framework for heterogeneous SAR-optical fusion for near-real-time land use and land cover mapping, along with a new global benchmark dataset.

title: GSPan: A Continuous Gaussian Primitive Representation for Arbitrary-Scale Pansharpening
summary: Proposes GSPan, a continuous Gaussian primitive representation for arbitrary-scale pansharpening to generate high-resolution multispectral images.

title: ActWorld: From Explorable to Interactive World Model via Action-Aware Memory
summary: Introduces ActWorld, an interactive world model that transitions from explorable to interactive by incorporating action-aware memory to simulate environment dynamics under user actions.

title: BrainWorld: A Structural-Prior-Conditioned Generative Model for Whole-Brain 4D fMRI Dynamics
summary: Introduces BrainWorld, a structural-prior-conditioned generative model designed for whole-brain 4D fMRI dynamics to model functional brain activity.

title: Extracting Semantics: LLM-Guided Automatic Population of Robot Ontology from URDF
summary: Describes a method for LLM-guided automatic population of robot ontologies from URDF, providing semantically rich representations for embodied robots interacting with humans.

title: HRDX: A Large-Scale Vector HD-Map Dataset
summary: Presents HRDX, a large-scale vector HD-map dataset designed to support reliable and scalable autonomous driving.

title: ParkingTransformer: LLM-Enhanced End-to-End Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Parking
summary: Introduces ParkingTransformer, an LLM-enhanced method for end-to-end trajectory planning specifically for autonomous parking.

title: VL-MemKnG: Hybrid Memory with a Spatio-Temporal Knowledge Graph for Question Answering over Long Egocentric Navigation Trajectories
summary: Proposes VL-MemKnG, a hybrid memory system incorporating a spatio-temporal knowledge graph for question answering over long egocentric navigation trajectories.

title: ACE-Ego-0: Unifying Egocentric Human and Robotic Data for VLA Pretraining
summary: Introduces ACE-Ego-0, a method for unifying egocentric human and robotic data to enhance pretraining for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in embodied AI.

title: Contrastive Action-Image Pre-training for Visuomotor Control
summary: This paper proposes a pre-training method for visuomotor control in robotics, addressing data scarcity by using internet-scale image and language data. It focuses on improving vision encoders for robotic tasks.

title: VISTA: Scale-Aware Visual Navigation via Action History Conditioning
summary: This research introduces VISTA, a method for scale-aware visual navigation using Vision Navigation Foundation Models, which aims for zero-shot deployment in diverse environments. It addresses challenges in predicting normalized actions for navigation.

title: Abstention-Aware Personalized Object Rearrangement via Uncertainty-Guided LLM Assistance
summary: This paper presents a method for abstention-aware personalized object rearrangement for robotic assistance in household environments, using uncertainty-guided LLM assistance. It focuses on deciding not only where to place objects but also when to abstain from placement.

title: Transformer-Based Warm-Starting for Feasible and Optimal Terminal Approach to Tumbling Objects with Space Manipulators
summary: This research investigates transformer-based warm-starting for generating real-time trajectories for space manipulators to approach tumbling objects. It addresses challenges in on-orbit robotic servicing due to complex dynamics and constraints.

title: Contactless Respiratory Monitoring on Heterogeneous Mobile Robots: A Multimodal Edge-Computing Framework
summary: This paper proposes a multimodal edge-computing framework for contactless respiratory monitoring using heterogeneous mobile robots. This application aims to improve remote triage and victim assessment in emergency response scenarios.

title: Where Should Action Generation Begin? A Learnable Source Prior for Generative Robot Policies
summary: This research introduces LeaP (Learnable Source Prior), a method to improve generative robot policies by determining a more effective starting point for action generation. It aims to enhance how robots learn and execute actions.

title: DexLink Hand: A Compact, Affordable, 16-DOF Linkage-Driven Hand with Human-Like Dexterity
summary: This paper presents the DexLink Hand, a compact and affordable 16-degree-of-freedom linkage-driven robotic hand designed for human-like dexterity. It aims to address the trade-off between dexterity, compactness, and cost in robotic hand design.

title: AnnotateAnything: Automatic Annotation of 3D Assets for Robot Manipulation
summary: This research introduces AnnotateAnything, an automatic annotation framework for 3D assets to provide semantic, interactive, and physical knowledge for robot manipulation in simulations. It aims to improve scalable robot data collection.

title: Embodiment Shapes Rolling Behavior in a Multimodal Infant Model
summary: This computational study uses MIMo, a virtual infant embodiment, to investigate how embodiment shapes rolling behavior and sensorimotor control in infant motor development.

title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
summary: This research explores offline skill consolidation for shared-policy robot learning, enabling robots to acquire new skills over long deployments without compromising existing policy structures. It focuses on sequential robot skill learning.

title: MagicSim: A Unified Infrastructure for Executable Embodied Interaction
summary: This paper introduces MagicSim, a unified infrastructure for executable embodied interaction, designed to serve as a shared simulation substrate for robot learning and embodied agents. It aims to link control, skills, and planning more effectively.

title: RICH-SLAM: Radar SLAM with Incremental and Continuous Hilbert Mapping
summary: This research presents RICH-SLAM, a Radar SLAM method utilizing incremental and continuous Hilbert mapping, designed to overcome the challenges of sparse and noisy radar measurements for localization and mapping. It emphasizes radar's robustness in adverse conditions.

title: MuseVLA: An Adaptive Multimodal Sensing Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces MuseVLA, an adaptive multimodal sensing Vision-Language-Action model for robotic manipulation, which leverages diverse sensor modalities beyond RGB observations. It aims to enhance robots' perception of physical properties for interaction.

title: ERQA-Plus: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Reasoning in Embodied AI
summary: This paper presents ERQA-Plus, a diagnostic benchmark designed to evaluate reasoning capabilities in generalist embodied AI agents. It assesses an agent's ability to reason about spatial relations, actions, and environmental constraints from visual observations.

title: ED3R: Energy-Aware Distributed Disaster Detection Enabled by Cooperative Robotic Agents
summary: This research introduces ED3R, a framework for energy-aware distributed disaster detection enabled by cooperative robotic agents, targeting environmental monitoring and natural disaster management. It addresses the challenges of operating under uncertainty and resource limitations.

title: HumanoidArena: Benchmarking Egocentric Hierarchical Whole-body Learning
summary: This paper introduces HumanoidArena, a benchmark designed for egocentric hierarchical whole-body learning in humanoid robots. It addresses the challenges of scalable policy learning for complex whole-body interactions in human-centered environments.

title: Qwen-RobotManip Technical Report: Alignment Unlocks Scale for Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models
summary: This technical report, Qwen-RobotManip, investigates applying large-scale alignment and training principles from foundation models to robotic manipulation. It aims to achieve genuine generalization in robotic manipulation tasks.

title: WAM-RL: World-Action Model Reinforcement Learning with Reconstruction Rewards and Online Video SFT
summary: This paper introduces WAM-RL (World-Action Model Reinforcement Learning), a method that uses reconstruction rewards and online video SFT to improve the acquisition of fine-grained manipulation skills. It aims to overcome the reliance on expert trajectories in World-Action models for robotics.

title: PearlVLA: Progressive Embodied Action-Plan Refinement in Latent Space

title: Show HN: Mira – Open-source and self-hosted AI code reviewer
summary: Hey HN, I'm Jay, co-creator of Mira. An open-source, self-hosted AI code reviewer where you BYOK (bring your own key). Local models are getting really good. Hosted frontier models are getting really expensive. So, we built Mira. Mira has some snazzy features too: - It's really fast at reviewing. Average is 77s compared with Greptile's 5 minutes. Your PRs aren't going into a queue on a cloud somewhere. - Mira performs a blast radius and see what damage will be done with code change. - Learns your codebase's patterns from the repo itself and enforces them without a config file. - It's self-hosted, so your code never leaves your infrastructure. Bring your own model - OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local LLM behind your firewall. We're really active, and looking for active contributors.
