title: Toward a Kantian refutation of Agent Foundations
summary: This post is a Cunningham's law draft , less than 50% finished, in some parts mere notes. Consider a) waiting until this notice has disappeared to read a more coherent post, or b) criticizing it with a focus on what would be right, not just what is wrong. I haven't strongly made my mind yet, so at this stage I'm particularly interested in fundamental criticisms of the goal and framing (but of course I also welcome minor corrections). TL;DR: The goals of Agent Foundations seem so far-fetched that all the progress made in the field doesn't seem to have decreased our distance to them that much. One might conclude that the goal is unachievable, the question ill-posed. But even the available rejections of AF seems unprincipled: instead of proving that the task is impossible, [1] we simply fail, and do something else instead. Working toward a principled refutation of Agent Foundations might either indeed refute AF or point to unexplored directions, and both outcomes would be helpful information. Prelude: Kant's refutation of all arguments of God's existence Kant argued that there are three (and only three) related concepts of God, definable on three different levels: Defined independently of any universe: God as set of all logical predicates. Defined in connection to the existence of a universe, without assuming any of its properties: God as cause of the universe. Defined in connection to our universe: God as cause of the apparent purposefulness of the universe. He argued furthermore that none of three definitions have enough "meat" to allow for a valid proof of its existence, and concluded that everyone should stop wasting their time trying to prove God's existence. I'm not interested in the specifics of Kant's argument; only in the structure: 1. We are dealing with concepts that are to some extent [2] definable without reference to the specific facts of our universe 2. There are different levels of "abstraction from the facts of our universe" in which different definitions can be made 3. These different formulations potentially have connections to each other (e.g. one might be a sub-specification of another) 4. An attempt can be made at showing that all levels and all possible definitions have been listed 5. An attempt can be made at showing, for each level and definition, that there isn't enough for the kind of proof we are looking for Computability theory as comparison Consider: Computability theory Complexity theory Cobham–Edmonds thesis Real computers "Computation" can be defined at the level of what a Turing machine can or cannot produce, at the level of what belongs to different complexity classes, and at the level of what can be computed in our universe. The concept of computation at the topmost level has enough content to allow e.g. for a proof that Turing-machine-computable and lambda-calculus-computable refer to the same thing. At the second level, everything computable belongs to some complexity class. But you can still work on the first level and ignore this extra specification. At the third level, the Cobham-Edmons thesis claims that only polynomial complexity is tractable in our universe. This is a fact about our universe (other universe with different properties are conceivable), and at the same time it is a very general fact that abstracts from the specifics of our universe, such as other universes also fulfilling this property while being very different from ours are also conceivable. At the bottom-most level, you need a substrate for your computations, and this adds a lot of specifications to what computing means. Across the different levels, computability is, in same sense, the same object, and in some sense three different objects. [3] Locating the AF paradigm Agent Foundations is in search of a paradigm. It's probably worth it to reflect on what exactly a paradigm is. My initial approximation is a self-contained networks of concepts and proofs . A second worthwhile question in the search for a paradigm is: in which level of abstraction does the paradigm live? [4] It seems plausible to me that a solution for alignment can be found using several self-contained components, and that not all components are on the same level. But it seems very implausible that we can cobble concepts from different levels in a haphazard fashion. So it might be useful to try to create a taxonomy of levels, to locate current agendas within them, [5] and to see what we are missing. The guiding question to locate the level in which a solution is is to ask: How different are the universes in which this alignment strategy would work? Would this strategy work in a universe with different physics but the same math? Before we explore a tentative taxonomy of levels, let's try to list the concepts that we are trying to understand. Concepts There are two basic aspects to what we are trying to capture under the name of agency : a agent knows the universe and an agent acts in the universe . I will separate the two aspects and, for lack of better terms, speak of inductors and interveners . [6] A natural question to ask is: Is every inductor an intervener, and vice versa? The intervener's interventions can be conceptualized with the concepts of coherence, [7] values, pessimization (?), etc., which might be definable in different levels. I don't know if there are some equivalent concepts for the inductor side. We also have concepts like alignment and control, which seem to be definable on different levels. Definitional levels Dualistic Mathland I will define dualistic as the property of definitions of a connection of not specifying the thing they connect. [8] The introductory definition of a set as a non-ordered list of elements is dualistic: it allows for operations like union, intersection, etc., without having to specify what the elements are. ZFC, on the other hands, is not dualistic: all ZFC-sets are ultimately definable from the empty set, and having a set which isn't thus definable isn't allowed. The concept of evolution belongs here, as does non-Many Worlds Quantum Mechanics. More relevant to our purposes, Bayesian updating also belongs here, as do Bayesian Neural Networks. How does AF look inside Dualistic Mathland? Some results and questions: An inductor can be defined as a Solomonoff inductor An intervener that is also an inductor can be defined as an AIXI-inductor/intervener Is every intervener an inductor? [9] Does every intervener follow some kind of reward ? Control and alignment seem to be understandable questions in this level (i.e. how to get an AIXI that does the things that we want?) but not answerable at this level. The most abstract definitions of Multiple agency are by definition dualistic. Jump from Dualistic to Computable The questions that arise in Dualistic Mathland [10] don't have solutions, but in some sense this is irrelevant, because we know that these definitions are unsuitable for our universe: [11] the definitions in Dualistic Mathland are incompatible with things like recursion; [12] their problem isn't being "too abstract"; they are the wrong kind of abstract. This is good news: this is the kind of Kantian refutation that we want. We understand agency inside Dualistic Mathland well enough to know that we need to keep searching outside of it, in a similar way to how Gödel proved that understanding arithmetic well enough means leaving forever the naive idea of arithmetic without recursion problems. [13] An optimistic scenario would be that something similar happens in the other levels. Computable Mathland (See upcoming post Nitpicking on Embeddedness ) Macro-Empirical Dualistic and Computable Mathland are memorable names trying to facilitate discussion about things which are presumably known to everyone. Now I tentatively propose some levels about which it might be worthwhile to reflect. The first of them is what I'll call the macro-empirical level. By this I mean working at the level of very fundamental empirical descriptions of the universe, which are general enough that researching in them resembles Dualistic/Computable Mathland, but with the advantage of being automatically relevant for our universe. [14] The Natural Abstractions and Condensations agendas seem to me to fit here. A similar thing seems to apply to the attempts to define agency from Friston's Free Energy Principle . [15] Platonico-Empirical Several results (manifold hypothesis, platonic space hypothesis, simplicity bias) point to the universe being a model of a mathematical object, in ways beyond the trivial way that underlyies any instance of empirical science. I'll define the platonico-empirical level as the level in which it can be attempted to instrumentalize these facts. Michael Levin is probably the best representative of what this could look like, with his references to non-metaphorical agency inside what he calls the Platonic space, with which we can attempt to interact . [16] Human-Empirical Research around concepts like CEV aim to reach very general conclusions, but depart from the empirical fact of how humans are. I'm unsure of whether this is regular empirical research coupled with speculation, or indeed an additional level in which, beyond CEV, other concepts could be tried. Schelling Goodness also possibly belongs here. Normal-Empirical=Scientific Agent Foundations isn't a badge of honor; "not belonging to AF" might simply mean "being a well-posed question with a solution". Thus it is without valuation or particular surprise that all agendas which are simply doing normal science are not part Agent Foundations. The only interesting point is clarifying that empirical and non-prosaic aren't synonymous. For instance, I think Byrnes's agenda as trying to abstract the mechanism by which which a human intervener isn't properly modeled by a utility function, but instead by what the human imagines their peers thinking of them. It might be that this concept is abstractable, and if so, it could guide research on different substrates (LLMs and some architecture that we haven't discovered yet, for instance). In so far, it is doing something beyond looking at current LLMs and trying to understand it, i.e. it's non-prosaic alignment research. But Byrnes isn't trying to locate that particular mechanism, which must sit somewhere in Mathland, through exploration of Mathland. Byrnes is trying to locate it through exploration of our universe (more specifically, of human brains and their effects), i.e. doing brain science. And understandably so, since there is no reason to expect that mechanism to be salient in mathland . Solving Philosophy and/or Math The previous levels are all more or less agnostic wrt "solving philosophy", i.e. one could for instance work on the Platonic Space without asking the question of what exactly that means. But it is plausible that the confusion regarding this situation acts as a blocker in AF, so that working on clearing this confusion could itself be one way of working on AF. [17] A major source of confusion is that humans are embedded, non-dualistic parts of the universe, and et seem to have what Nagel called the "view from nowhere" able to find out truth that is valid also outside the universe. The hierarchy between solving Math [18] and solving Philosophy seems unclear. Solving philosophy seems to gesture at something like formalizing the structure of the world of concepts . In some sense this is previous to math (because concepts is a much more general category than mathematical concepts), but the structure might be mathematical. It's possible that at the bottom we don't find a foundation, but that two things that refer to each other. ^ Or at the every least having a very convincing argument of why it's very unlikely to be possible. ^ And the crux is precisely to what extent ? ^ There's no such thing [as computer science]. [...] At one end you have people who are really mathematicians. [...] In the middle you have people working on something like the natural history of computers-- studying the behavior of algorithms for routing data through networks, for example. And then at the other extreme you have the hackers, who are trying to write interesting software, and for whom computers are just a medium of expression, as concrete is for architects or paint for painters. Hackers and Painters Paul Graham ^ This question seems central to distinguish the specific things that have been tried from the general strategies that haven been tried and which could be fulfilled with other specific things. In particular, it seems to me there is no vocabulary to distinguish between the MIRI (and MIRI-inspired) research , and the paradigm such research points towards. This and this are great introduction for the second question, but they are busy rejecting criticism of the field rather than, as I intend here, creating the unified vocabulary to sketch a map of all the things that are and could be part of AF, even if those things contradict each other in the specifics. ^ Each concept of an agenda could in theory be on a different level, but if the agenda is coherent, we should expect to find the whole of it nested together, unless the agenda consists on several separable coherent sub-components. ^ From now on I will avoid using the misleading terms agent or agency . ^ I take the idea of separating the different definitional levels of coherence from this exchange: Mateusz Bagiński : How well can the entity's behavior be explained as trying to optimize a single fixed utility function? How well aligned is the entity's behavior with a coherent and self-consistent set of goals? To what degree is the entity not a hot mess of self-undermining behavior? Kaarel : a monograph untangling this coherence mess some more would be valuable. it could do the following things: specifying a bunch of a priori different properties that could be called “coherence” discussing which ones are equivalent, which ones are correlated, which ones seem pretty independent giving good names to the notions or notion-clusters discussing which kinds of coherence generically increase/decrease with capabilities, which ones probably increase/decrease with capabilities in practice, which ones can both increase or decrease with capabilities depending on the development/learning process, both around human level and later/eventually, in human-like minds and more generally [2] discussing how this relates to AI x risk. like, which kinds of coherence should play a role in a case for AI x risk? what does that look like? or maybe the picture should make one optimistic about some approach to de-AGI-x-risk-ing? or about AGI in general? [3] ^ I claim this definition has the same spirit, but is more accurate, than the usual definitions. See upcoming post Nitpicking about Embeddedness. ^ I.e. is there something like Q-learning in Dualistic Mathland? ^ Like "how to align an AIXI inductor-intervener?" ^ With the possible exception of the ones regarding Multiple Agency, about which I am even more confused than about everything else here. ^ This is relevant for Bayesian updates, Decision Theory, and possibly other concepts. ^ Nitpicking on unbounded analysis , Yudkowsky writes: If you can't state a program that solves the problem in principle , you are in some sense confused about the nature of the cognitive work needed to solve the problem. This is true if the problem has already been formulated inside one level which is lower than the one that allows unbounded analysis, but not if the problem is formulated there, or vague enough so it's formulable in several levels. "Not being able to solve alignment (as defined in Dualistic Mathland" through unbounded analysis" has as little relevance as "not being able to write an algorithm that solves all possible variations chess". The problem is, barely, well-defined to be a question, but not well-defined enough that not having an answer is relevant. ^ And, synonymously with that advantage, the disadvantage that if it turns out that the empirical description was wrong, they might lose some or all of their relevance. ^ I'm planning to write a post about what I see as independent claims which are often presented together, and often under the same name: The Free Energy Principle as a framework for all agents in our universe A more specific subset of FEP for agents with self-models in our universe The general claims of the Bayesian Brain theory The more specific claims of Predictive Processing The neurological-implementation of this in Predictive coding The more specific claims that actions and beliefs are the same for these agents This would be in application of Stuart Amstrong 's advice: Cut up your Great Thingy into smaller independent ideas, and treat them as independent. For instance a marxist would cut up Marx's Great Thingy into [several theories]. Then each of them should be assessed independently, and the truth or falsity of one should not halo on the others. If we can do that, we should be safe from the spiral, as each theory is too narrow to start a spiral on its own. Same thing for every other Great Thingy out there. Claim 6 seems particularly relevant to research, because it might point to a more general answer to the question of whether every inductor as an intervener. ^ Trying to do something like the Natural Abstractions agenda inside that Platonic Space also seems like something potentially worth trying. ^ One very speculative way in which this could work out: Kant sketched an argument of how every free will should act super-rationally towards other free wills. Unfortunately the concept of free will doesn't seem to be compatible with our deterministic universe. But what if we could convince an ASI that it is a free will in the Platonic Space, and we could do something like proving meta-ethical theorems that the ASI would be (legitimately) convinced it should obey? Relatedly, it is interesting to note that Kant's defense of free will is much closer to the Block Universe than to Newtonian mechanics. ^ Also mentioned by Kaarel in the previously mentioned discussion of the definitional levels of Coherence. Discuss

summary: Presents a method for structural compression of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models through attribution-guided and coverage-maximized pruning to reduce memory footprint and inference overhead.

summary: Provides a retrospective on SWave, a complex-valued recurrent language model, discussing its design principles and its approach to information encoding using complex numbers.

summary: Introduces Self-CTRL (Self-Consistency Training with Reinforcement Learning), a method to optimize language models for consistency between their self-explanations and behavior.

title: SafeClawBench: Separating Semantic, Audit-Evidence, and Sandbox Harm in Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces SafeClawBench, a benchmark for evaluating security failures in tool-using LLM agents, distinguishing between semantic, audit-evidence, and sandbox harms. It highlights how agents can cause harm through actions like disclosing protected objects or modifying databases.

title: Guava: An Effective and Universal Harness for Embodied Manipulation
summary: Guava is presented as an effective and universal harness for embodied manipulation, utilizing large language models trained on vision-language data. It offers an alternative to end-to-end systems by combining high-level reasoning with external modules for embodied agents.

title: Redact or Keep? A Fully Local AI Cascade for Educational Dialogue De-Identification
summary: This research proposes a fully local AI cascade for de-identifying educational dialogue, aiming to protect personally identifiable information (PII) while preserving curricular content. It addresses the challenge of distinguishing PII from relevant subject matter in transcripts.

title: Gaussian Mixture Attention: Linear-Time Sequence Mixing via Probabilistic Latent Routing
summary: This paper introduces Gaussian Mixture Attention (GMA), a probabilistic attention-style sequence mixer designed to address the bottleneck of token-to-token interaction in Transformer architectures. GMA aims to improve scaling to long contexts by replacing explicit pairwise queries.

title: CODEBLOCK: Learning to Supervise Code at the Right Granularity
summary: CODEBLOCK is a method for supervising code LLMs that learns to apply supervision at the right granularity, moving beyond uniform cross-entropy loss. It aims to improve fine-tuning by focusing on high-value tokens, similar to recent token-level selection methods.

title: Artemis: Anatomy-Resolved inTervention for Eliminating Multimodal NeuroImage confounderS
summary: Artemis is a system that uses graph neural networks to analyze multimodal neuroimaging data, integrating fMRI and DTI, to eliminate confounders like age and sex. It aims to enable more accurate non-invasive analysis of brain networks.

title: A Survey on Data-Driven Models for Soil Moisture Regression and Classification
summary: This paper presents a survey of data-driven models for soil moisture regression and classification, addressing the complex spatiotemporal learning problem characterized by nonlinear environmental interactions and heterogeneous data. It contrasts these with physics-based hydrological models.

title: Enhanced Graph Neural Networks using K-Hop Gaussian Diffusion
summary: This research proposes enhancing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) by incorporating K-Hop Gaussian Diffusion to improve information propagation beyond direct neighbors. It aims to address limitations of traditional GNNs where noisy or poorly defined edges limit their receptive field.

title: Neural Network Implementation of the Renormalization Group for Fault Diagnosis with Class Imbalance
summary: This paper proposes RGNet, a novel neural network architecture based on the renormalization group concept, designed for hierarchical coarse-graining of feature space. It aims to address challenges like class imbalance and multidimensional noise in fault diagnosis tasks.

title: ThousandWorlds: A benchmark for climate emulation of potentially habitable exoplanets
summary: ThousandWorlds is introduced as a new benchmark for climate emulation of potentially habitable exoplanets, aiming to aid in interpreting atmospheric signatures. It focuses on understanding exoplanet climates to distinguish signs of life from abiotic chemistry.

title: Do Time Series Foundation Model Benchmarks Hide Regime-Dependent Failures? Evidence from Traffic Speed Forecasting
summary: This research investigates whether standard benchmarks for time series foundation models hide regime-dependent failures by using aggregate metrics. It introduces a regime-stratified evaluation method, applying it to traffic speed forecasting to reveal masked failures.

title: From Sparse Features to Trustworthy Proxies: Certifying SAE-Based Interpretability
summary: This paper explores the trustworthiness of Sparse Autoencoder (SAE)-based interpretability for language models, focusing on when an SAE explanation faithfully reflects the underlying LM. It studies this through a post-hoc generalization framework to certify interpretability.

title: LLMZero: Discovering Adaptive Training Strategies for RL Post-Training via LLM Agents
summary: LLMZero is a method that uses LLM agents to discover adaptive training strategies for RL post-training, observing distinct patterns in how capacity and regularization parameters evolve. It aims to move beyond fixed training schedules by adapting to shifting dynamics.

title: MOLAR: Learning Multimodal Molecular Representations from Noisy Labels
summary: MOLAR is a method for learning multimodal molecular representations that addresses the challenge of noisy labels in molecular property prediction. It aims to improve predictions by accounting for the unreliability of annotations obtained from assays or databases.

title: P$^2$CE: Model-Agnostic Plausible Pareto-Optimal Counterfactual Explanations
summary: This paper introduces P$^2$CE, a model-agnostic method for generating plausible Pareto-optimal counterfactual explanations, addressing concerns about fairness and transparency in machine learning. It aims to help individuals understand and potentially alter unfavorable AI-driven decisions.

title: Signature filtering: a lightweight enhancement for statistical watermark detection in large language models
summary: This paper proposes signature filtering, a lightweight detection-time module designed to enhance statistical watermark detection in large language model outputs. It aims to improve the attribution of LLM-generated content, especially when signals are weak or texts are repetitive.

title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
summary: This research introduces tail-aware scheduling for LLM inference, addressing the challenge of extreme length variability in LLM serving. It aims to improve scheduling beyond prediction-driven policies that often use mean-centric metrics, enhancing efficiency for diverse request sizes.

title: TMR-GGNN: Credit Card Fraud Detection based on Time-Aware Multi-Relational Guided Graph Neural Network
summary: This research proposes TMR-GGNN, a novel framework for credit card fraud detection based on a Time-Aware Multi-Relational Guided Graph Neural Network. It aims to address challenges such as imbalanced data, evolving fraud patterns, and complex transaction relationships.

title: A Cross-Model VLM-Judge Protocol for Single-Image 3D Mesh Quality (and Why Cheap Proxies Fall Short)
summary: This paper introduces a Cross-Model VLM-Judge Protocol for evaluating the quality of single-image 3D generated meshes, highlighting the shortcomings of cheap automatic proxies. It aims to provide a more reliable, human-free method for comparing generator outputs.

title: Veriphi: Attack-Guided Neural Network Verification with Dataset-Dependent Training Methods
summary: Veriphi is a GPU-accelerated neural network verification system that combines fast adversarial attacks with formal bound certification using alpha,beta-CROWN methods. It demonstrates its effectiveness across different training methodologies on standard datasets like MNIST and CIFAR-10.

title: What Does the Weight Norm Control in Grokking? Logit-Scale Mediation under Cross-Entropy
summary: This research paper investigates the role of weight norms in the grokking phenomenon, where neural networks transition from memorization to generalization, by analyzing what the norm truly controls. It explores how fixing the weight norm and varying output temperature affects grokking delay.

title: Structured Representation Learning with Locally Linear Embeddings and Adaptive Feature Fusion
summary: Inspired by neuroscientific principles, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement learning framework for structured representation learning using locally linear embeddings and adaptive feature fusion. It aims to encode complex behaviors by leveraging low-dimensional manifolds and dynamic information fusion.

title: The Illusion of Improvement: Reject Inference Strategies in Credit Scoring
summary: This research systematically evaluates reject inference methods used in credit scoring to mitigate survival bias, revealing a structural failure mode where model accuracy improves but recall compromises in retraining cycles. The study questions the perceived effectiveness of these strategies.

title: SFT Overtraining Predicts Rank Inversion via Entropy Collapse Under RLVR
summary: This paper examines how SFT overtraining can lead to rank inversion due to entropy collapse under RLVR, causing the standard heuristic for checkpoint selection to fail. It analyzes the expected advantage variance in binary reward settings during GRPO.

title: Quantum Annealing Enhanced Reinforcement Learning for Accurate Remaining Useful Lifetime Prediction
summary: This research proposes using quantum annealing-enhanced reinforcement learning to improve the accuracy of Remaining Useful Lifetime (RUL) prediction for predictive maintenance. It aims to overcome limitations of traditional statistical and data-driven models in handling system nonlinearity.

title: Beyond AHI: An Interpretable Causal-Discovery-Guided Framework for Sleep Recovery in Connected Health
summary: This paper introduces an interpretable causal-discovery-guided AI framework for sleep recovery in connected health, aiming to provide deeper insights beyond traditional indices like AHI. It focuses on better aligning objective sleep assessment with patient-reported outcomes.

title: Concept Modulation Models: A Unified Framework for Identifiability and Extrapolation
summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for concept modulation models, addressing the critical issues of identifiability and extrapolation for reliable generalization in conditional latent variable models. It examines how observed attribute variation determines latent structure and distributions.

title: PSyGenTAB: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Synthetic Clinical Tabular Data Generation via Constrained Optimization
summary: This paper introduces PSyGenTAB, a privacy-preserving framework for generating synthetic clinical tabular data using constrained optimization. It aims to overcome limitations in accessing real patient data for medical AI development due to regulations like HIPAA and GDPR.

title: Sparsity Curse: Understanding RLVR Model Parameter Space from Model Merging
summary: This research paper investigates the "sparsity curse" in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) models by analyzing their parameter space through model merging techniques. It aims to understand how RLVR achieves reasoning intelligence and resists catastrophic forgetting.

title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability
summary: This paper analyzes the residual scaling of looped (weight-tied) Transformers, which increase effective depth without adding parameters, focusing on their stability and transferability. It challenges prior depth-scaling analyses by demonstrating a more precise role for the scaling factor.

title: Hierarchical Attention via Domain Decomposition
summary: This paper proposes a novel hierarchical attention mechanism based on two-level overlapping Schwarz domain decomposition, combining local subdomain corrections with a coarse level for global information communication. The method aims to improve attention efficiency and scope.

title: Do as the Romans Do: Learning Universal Behaviors from Heterogeneous Agents
summary: This research explores learning universal behaviors from heterogeneous agents, addressing the challenge of conflicting behavioral signals in imitation learning. It aims to identify which behaviors are worth imitating when observing diverse populations.

title: Effects of sparsity and superposition on loss in simple autoencoders
summary: This paper investigates the effects of sparsity and superposition on loss in simple autoencoders, aiming to address polysemanticity and improve the mechanistic interpretability of neural networks. It delves into how individual neurons contribute to multiple tasks.

title: TS-Fault: Benchmarking Time Series Forecasters Against Structural Faults
summary: This paper introduces TS-Fault, a new benchmark for evaluating time series forecasters by testing their robustness against structural faults, beyond traditional average error metrics on clean data. It aims to provide a more realistic assessment of model reliability in deployment.

title: Correcting Sensor-Induced Distribution Drift with Wasserstein Adversarial Learning
summary: This paper proposes a Wasserstein-GAN-inspired adversarial learning approach to correct sensor-induced distribution drift, aiming to improve the quality and stability of data-driven methods. It focuses on unsupervised inference of physically interpretable transformations.

title: Fair Cognitive Impairment Detection Through Unlearning
summary: This research investigates fair cognitive impairment detection using AI models applied to spontaneous speech, focusing on methods of "unlearning" to mitigate bias. It aims to prevent models from exploiting demographic cues correlated with medical labels.

title: PACT: Preserving Anchored Cores in Task-vectors for Model Merging
summary: This paper introduces PACT, a novel technique for model merging that preserves anchored cores in task-vectors, offering a training-free alternative to multi-task learning. It aims to combine multiple task-specific fine-tuned models into a single multi-task model more effectively.

title: MetaboNet-Bench: A Multi-modal Benchmark for Glucose Forecasting in Type 1 Diabetes
summary: This paper introduces MetaboNet-Bench, a new multi-modal benchmark for evaluating glucose forecasting algorithms in type 1 diabetes. It addresses the lack of standardized performance evaluation benchmarks in this research area.

title: BLADE: Scalable Bi-level Adaptive Data Selection for LLM Training
summary: This paper introduces BLADE, a scalable bi-level adaptive data selection method designed to filter out uninformative noise and construct adaptive learning trajectories for Large Language Model (LLM) training. It aims to optimize LLM dataset utilization as they scale to trillions of tokens.

title: scGTN: Deep Siamese Graph Transformer Network for Single-cell RNA Sequencing Clustering
summary: This paper proposes scGTN, a Deep Siamese Graph Transformer Network, for single-cell RNA sequencing clustering, aiming to improve cell type identification and understanding of cellular heterogeneity. It addresses current limitations in scRNA-seq data clustering methods.

title: Bounded Context Management for Tabular Foundation Models on Stream Learning
summary: This research introduces a method for bounded context management in tabular foundation models, allowing them to adapt predictions on sequential data by conditioning on a labeled context.

title: Dual-Channel Grounded World Modeling (DCGWM): Structural Prevention of Objective Interference Collapse via Heterogeneous External Grounding with Inward-Only Gradient Flow
summary: This paper presents Dual-Channel Grounded World Modeling (DCGWM), an architectural improvement that prevents objective interference collapse in JEPA-based world models by using heterogeneous external grounding.

title: Robust and Interpretable Adaptation of Equivariant Materials Foundation Models via Sparsity-promoting Fine-tuning
summary: This research proposes a sparsity-promoting fine-tuning method for robust and interpretable adaptation of pre-trained materials foundation models for domain-specific calibration.

title: Attention as Frustrated Synchronization
summary: This paper introduces the Frustrated Synchronization Network (FSN), a novel attention architecture based on structured departures from synchronization in a network of oscillators.

title: Stealthy World Model Manipulation via Data Poisoning
summary: This paper investigates a data poisoning vulnerability in world models used by learning agents, showing how adversarially poisoned fine-tuning trajectories can manipulate predictions.

title: Contextualizing Biological Language Models across Modalities via Logit-Space Contrastive Alignment
summary: This research introduces Logit-Space Contrastive Alignment, a method for contextualizing biological language models across different modalities to improve sequence design and interpretation.

title: SproutRAG: Attention-Guided Tree Search with Progressive Embeddings for Long-Document RAG
summary: This paper presents SproutRAG, a new retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that uses attention-guided tree search and progressive embeddings to improve retrieval for long documents.

title: Want Better Synthetic Data? Steer It: Activation Steering for Low-Resource Language Generation
summary: This research proposes Activation Steering, a method to generate higher-quality synthetic data using large language models, especially for low-resource languages.

title: JetFlow: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding with Parallel Tree Drafting
summary: This paper introduces JetFlow, a new method for speculative decoding with parallel tree drafting that aims to break the scaling limitations and accelerate autoregressive LLMs.

title: CoreMem: Riemannian Retrieval and Fisher-Guided Distillation for Long-Term Memory in Dialogue Agents
summary: This research introduces CoreMem, a system that employs Riemannian retrieval and Fisher-guided distillation to provide continuous long-term memory for personalized dialogue agents on constrained hardware.

title: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents
summary: This paper introduces VISUALSKILL, a system that provides multimodal skills to computer-use agents, addressing their limitations in long-horizon tasks and with unfamiliar software interfaces.

title: LLM Parameters for Math Across Languages: Shared or Separate?
summary: This paper investigates whether large language model parameters for mathematical reasoning are shared or separate across different languages, analyzing cross-lingual mechanistic aspects.

title: Montreal Forced Aligner and the state of speech-to-text alignment in 2026
summary: This article discusses the Montreal Forced Aligner (MFA), a widely used tool for speech-to-text alignment, detailing its development and expanded linguistic coverage since 2016.

title: Possible or Definite? A Benchmark for Evaluating Diagnostic Uncertainty Preservation in Clinical Text
summary: This paper proposes a new benchmark to evaluate how large language models preserve diagnostic uncertainty when processing and generating clinical text.

title: PreUnlearn: Auditing Collateral Knowledge Damage Before Large Language Model Unlearning
summary: This paper introduces PreUnlearn, a method for auditing collateral knowledge damage in large language models before machine unlearning, which aims to selectively remove information.

title: Towards Scalable Customization and Deployment of Multi-Agent Systems for Enterprise Applications
summary: This paper addresses the challenges of scalable customization and deployment of LLM-based multi-agent systems for enterprise applications, focusing on latency and inference costs.

title: MCompassRAG: Topic Metadata as a Semantic Compass for Paragraph-Level Retrieval
summary: This paper presents MCompassRAG, a new retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that uses topic metadata as a semantic compass to improve paragraph-level retrieval efficiency and precision.

title: Speech-Driven End-to-End Language Discrimination towards Chinese Dialects
summary: This research explores a speech-driven end-to-end approach for language discrimination, focusing on improving the identification of similar Chinese dialects.

title: Dual Dimensionality for Local and Global Attention
summary: This paper proposes Dual Dimensionality for Local and Global Attention, a new method to enhance attention mechanisms in decoder-only Transformers by optimizing key and value representations.

title: Low-resource Language Discrimination Towards Chinese Dialects with Transfer learning and Data Augmentation
summary: This article proposes a novel framework (CDDTLDA) utilizing transfer learning and data augmentation to improve Chinese dialect discrimination, addressing scarce annotation resources in NLP.

title: Steerable Cultural Preference Optimization of Reward Models
summary: This paper explores methods to optimize reward models for large language models, enabling them to better serve diverse cultural communities and align with varied preferences.

title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance
summary: This paper introduces PhysAssistBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate how well large language models can assist physicians by integrating clinical knowledge, EHR interaction, and patient communication.

title: BCL: Bayesian In-Context Learning Framework for Information Extraction
summary: This paper proposes BCL (Bayesian In-Context Learning Framework), a new approach for information extraction that aims to improve performance and generalizability with large language models.

title: PragReST: Self-Reinforcing Counterfactual Reasoning for Pragmatic Language Understanding
summary: This paper introduces PragReST, a method for self-reinforcing counterfactual reasoning, to help large language models overcome their struggles with pragmatic inferences in natural language understanding.

title: PEC-Home: Interpretation of Progressively Elliptical Commands in Smart Homes
summary: This paper presents PEC-Home, a new approach that enables LLM-powered home assistants to interpret progressively elliptical commands more naturally by leveraging shared context in human dialogue.

title: The Wrong Kind of Right: Quantifying and Localizing Misfired Alignment in LLMs
summary: This paper quantifies and localizes instances where large language model alignment mechanisms misfire, leading to the generation of problematic stereotypes and biases, highlighting the need for advanced alignment strategies.

title: RegMix-D: Dynamic Data Mixing via Proxy Training Trajectories
summary: This paper introduces RegMix-D, an extension to the RegMix method that enables dynamic data mixing during Large Language Model pretraining using proxy training trajectories.

title: TW-LegalBench: Measuring Taiwanese Legal Understanding
summary: This paper introduces TW-LegalBench, a new benchmark designed to measure large language models' understanding and reasoning capabilities within the specific context of the Taiwanese legal system.

title: LLMs Struggle to Measure What Distinguishes Students of Different Proficiency Levels: A Study of Item Discrimination in Reading Comprehension Assessment
summary: This study investigates the limitations of large language models in item discrimination, revealing their struggle to accurately distinguish students of different proficiency levels in reading comprehension assessments.

title: Morpheus: A Morphology-Aware Neural Tokenizer and Word Embedder for Turkish
summary: This paper introduces Morpheus, a morphology-aware neural tokenizer and word embedder specifically designed for agglutinative languages like Turkish, to improve how language models process such complex structures.

title: Output Vector Editing for Memorization Mitigation in Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes a new method, output vector editing, to mitigate memorization in large language models, thereby addressing privacy, copyright, and security risks from training data reproduction.

title: Lost in a Single Vector: Improving Long-Document Retrieval with Chunk Evidence Aggregation
summary: This paper addresses the issue of information dilution in long-document retrieval by proposing Chunk Evidence Aggregation, a method to improve ranking by combining evidence from different document segments.

title: RedactionBench
summary: This paper introduces RedactionBench, a new benchmark for evaluating large language models' ability to redact personally identifiable information (PII), distinguishing between extraction mechanics and privacy semantics.

title: Beyond Scalar Scores: Exploring LLM-based Metrics for Clinical Significance Evaluation in Radiology Reports
summary: This paper explores novel LLM-based metrics for evaluating radiology reports, aiming to provide more clinically significant assessments beyond traditional scalar scores to improve patient care.

title: Beyond Reward Engineering: A Data Recipe for Long-Context Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes a new data recipe for long-context reinforcement learning, aiming to enhance the long-context reasoning capabilities of large language models when deployed as autonomous agents.

title: ScholarSum: Student-Teacher Abstractive Summarization via Knowledge Graph Reasoning and Reflective Refinement
summary: This paper introduces ScholarSum, a new student-teacher approach for abstractive summarization of scientific literature that uses knowledge graph reasoning and reflective refinement to ensure factual faithfulness.

title: Aligning Implied Statements for Implicit Hate Speech Generalizability with Context-Bounded Semi-hard Negative Mining
summary: This paper proposes ImpSH, a new method using context-bounded semi-hard negative mining to improve the generalizability and detection of implicit hate speech, which often relies on insinuation rather than explicit terms.

title: Approximate Structured Diffusion for Sequence Labelling
summary: This paper introduces Approximate Structured Diffusion, a new approach for sequence labelling, a core task in Natural Language Processing, building upon Linear-Chain Conditional Random Fields.

title: Efficient Financial Language Understanding via Distillation with Synthetic Data
summary: This paper presents an efficient framework for financial sentiment analysis using distillation with synthetic data, addressing the challenges of limited and confidential labeled data in the financial sector.

title: Improving Medical Communication using Rubric-Guided Counterfactual Recommendations
summary: This paper introduces an LM-guided counterfactual recommendation pipeline designed to improve medical communication in text-based telemedicine by refining interpretable communication strategies based on patient feedback.

title: Learning Robust Pair Confidence for Multimodal Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction
summary: This research proposes a method to learn robust pair confidence for Multimodal Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction (MECPE) by addressing limitations in existing pair scorers that treat links independently.

title: SAGE: Stochastic Prompt Optimization via Agent-Guided Exploration
summary: This paper introduces SAGE (Stochastic Prompt Optimization via Agent-Guided Exploration), a method treating automatic prompt optimization as a black-box search to improve AI systems by refining context engineering.

title: As Easy as Rocket Science: Assessing the Ability of Large Language Models to Interpret Negation in Figurative Language
summary: This research assesses the ability of large language models (LLMs) to interpret negation within figurative language, identifying challenges in these complex linguistic areas for current models.

title: SenFlow: Inter-Sentence Flow Modeling for AI-Generated Text Detection in Hybrid Documents
summary: This paper introduces SenFlow, a method for inter-sentence flow modeling to improve AI-generated text detection in hybrid documents, addressing current gaps by considering inter-sentence dependencies and new generation models.

title: GraphPO: Graph-based Policy Optimization for Reasoning Models
summary: This research proposes GraphPO (Graph-based Policy Optimization), a new method to enhance large reasoning models within the Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) paradigm by addressing limitations in independent response sampling.

title: Beyond Tokenization: Direct Timestep Embedding and Contrastive Alignment for Time-Series Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces a method using direct timestep embedding and contrastive alignment to overcome the tokenization bottleneck in Time-Series Question Answering (TSQA) with Large Language Models.

title: G-IdiomAlign: A Gloss-Pivoted Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Idiom Alignment
summary: This paper introduces G-IdiomAlign, a new gloss-pivoted benchmark designed to evaluate cross-lingual idiom alignment, anchored by English glosses from Wiktionary.

title: Sumi: Open Uniform Diffusion Language Model from Scratch
summary: Sumi is introduced as an open-source Uniform Diffusion Language Model (UDLM) pretrained from scratch at large parameters, offering a flexible alternative to autoregressive models.

title: Leadership as Coordination Control: Behavioral Signatures and the Recovery-Advantage Boundary in Multi-Agent LLM Teams
summary: This research investigates the conditions under which process-level coordination control, akin to leadership, adds value to multi-agent LLM teams, exploring its behavioral signatures and the recovery-advantage boundary.

title: Dango: A Strictly L1-Only Large Language Model for Studying Second Language Acquisition
summary: Dango is presented as a 1.8B-parameter large language model specifically designed for controlled studies of L1-to-L2 transfer in second language acquisition.

title: Language Models as Interfaces, Not Oracles: A Hybrid LLM-ML System for Pediatric Appendicitis
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid LLM-ML system that utilizes large language models as interfaces, not oracles, to improve clinical decision support for pediatric appendicitis by interpreting free-text documentation.

title: RECOM: A Validity Discrimination Tradeoff in Automatic Metrics for Open Ended Reddit Question Answering
summary: This research examines the validity-discrimination tradeoff in automatic metrics used for evaluating LLM-generated text, particularly in open-ended Reddit question answering.

title: DreamReasoner-8B: Block-Size Curriculum Learning for Diffusion Reasoning Models
summary: DreamReasoner-8B is presented as an open-source block diffusion reasoning model that utilizes block-size curriculum learning to accelerate decoding and improve long chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: Trade-offs in Medical LLM Adaptation: An Empirical Study in French QA
summary: This empirical study investigates the trade-offs and effectiveness of domain adaptation strategies for large language models (LLMs) in French medical question-answering.

title: Enhancing Decision-Making with Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Fictitious Play
summary: This paper introduces multi-agent fictitious play as a method to enhance decision-making capabilities in large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems.

title: Freeing the Law with LOCUS: A Local Ordinance Corpus for the United States
summary: This paper introduces LOCUS, a new corpus providing machine-readable access to local ordinances across the United States, aiming to advance legal AI research.

title: Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards
summary: This research investigates learning to simulate human users in interactive settings using large language models and a novel Turing Rewards approach, useful for training agent assistants and evaluating personalization systems.

title: Recover, Discover, Plan: Learning Skills and Concepts from Robot Failures
summary: Proposes a method for robots to learn new skills and abstract concepts from their failures, aiming to make reinforcement learning more efficient by avoiding repeated training for similar failure modes.

title: PAIWorld: A 3D-Consistent World Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Introduces PAIWorld, a 3D-consistent world foundation model designed to improve robotic manipulation by providing multi-view coherence needed for learning policies from diverse camera inputs.

title: VEGA: Learning Navigation VLAs from In-the-Wild Egocentric Video with Geometric Trajectory Supervision
summary: Presents VEGA, an approach for training navigation Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models using unlabeled egocentric videos and geometric trajectory supervision, providing a scalable source for navigation-relevant visual observations.

title: N(CO)$^2$: Neural Combinatorial Optimization with Chance Constraints to Solve Stochastic Orienteering
summary: Introduces N(CO)$^2$, a method extending neural combinatorial optimization with chance constraints to effectively solve stochastic orienteering problems, which arise frequently in automation scenarios.

title: As You Wish: Mission Planning with Formal Verification using LLMs in Precision Agriculture
summary: Proposes a mission planner leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) with formal verification to simplify the operation of complex robotic systems in precision agriculture.

title: DREAM-Chunk: Reactive Action Chunking with Latent World Model
summary: Introduces DREAM-Chunk, a method that uses reactive action chunking with a latent world model to enhance the robustness and responsiveness of vision-language-action (VLA) models in robotic execution.

title: Benchmarking Action Spaces in Reinforcement Learning for Vision-based Robotic Manipulation
summary: Evaluates and benchmarks various action spaces (pose increment, velocity, joint position) in reinforcement learning for vision-based robotic manipulation, examining their impact on motion smoothness, safety, and task performance.

title: Admittance-Based Surface Alignment for Human-in-the-Loop Robotic Visual Inspection
summary: Develops an admittance-based surface alignment method for human-in-the-loop robotic visual inspection, aiming to improve precision and quality assurance for high-value parts in manufacturing.

title: SC3-Eval: Evaluating Robot Foundation Models via Self-Consistent Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces SC3-Eval, a new evaluation method that uses self-consistent video generation to assess robot foundation models and their manipulation policies in simulated environments, addressing the challenges of real-world testing.

title: SRL: Combining SLIP Model and Reinforcement Learning for Agile Robotic Jumping
summary: This research explores combining the Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum (SLIP) model with Reinforcement Learning to achieve agile robotic jumping, enhancing mobility for applications like search and rescue.

title: Self-Supervised Mask-Aware Transformers for Fault-Tolerant FBG Force Sensing in Minimally Invasive Surgical Robotics
summary: This work presents a method using Self-Supervised Mask-Aware Transformers for fault-tolerant Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) force sensing, critical for estimating multi-dimensional forces in minimally invasive surgical robots.

title: DNN Koopman-Based Deviation Compensation for UGV Path Tracking Control on Coupled Slope and Potholed Road
summary: This paper proposes a Deep Neural Network (DNN) Koopman-based deviation compensation strategy to improve path tracking control for Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) operating on complex off-road terrains with slopes and potholes.

title: ROBOSHACKLES: A Safety Dataset for Human-Injury Prevention in Embodied Foundation Models
summary: ROBOSHACKLES is introduced as a safety dataset aimed at preventing human injury by providing data for aligning Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) with safety protocols, as current real-world safety data is scarce.

title: A Scalable Embodied Intelligence Platform for Seamless Real-to-Sim-to-Real Transfer of Household Mobile Manipulation Tasks
summary: This paper introduces a scalable embodied intelligence platform designed to facilitate seamless real-to-simulation-to-real transfer for household mobile manipulation tasks, improving robustness and generalization.

title: High-Degree-of-Freedom Lightweight Bioinspired Leg for Enhanced Mobility in Small Robots
summary: This research presents a novel high-degree-of-freedom, lightweight, bioinspired leg mechanism for small robots, designed to enhance mobility in microrobotics by increasing degrees of freedom under spatial constraints.

title: Leveraging Energy Features for Surface Classification with Deep Learning: A Comparative Analysis Across Three Independent Datasets
summary: This study analyzes the viability of using energy-derived features with Deep Learning for surface classification in mobile robotics, comparing its performance across three independent datasets.

title: Selective Unit-Cell Actuation in Lattice Structures for Distributed Morphology in Soft Robots
summary: This work explores selective unit-cell actuation in lattice structures to achieve distributed morphology in soft robots, allowing for more integrated and adaptable designs by embedding actuators directly within the structure.

title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
summary: This research focuses on generating natural and expressive gestures for social robots like Pepper by using iterative Reinforcement Learning with human feedback, powered by Large Language Models (LLMs), to enhance human-robot interaction.

title: HALOMI: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Active Perception from Human Demonstrations
summary: HALOMI presents a method for learning humanoid locomotion and manipulation (loco-manipulation) by leveraging active perception from human demonstrations, aiming to transfer complex human skills to humanoid robots.

title: C-ARC: Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering for Non-Repetitive LiDAR Sensors
summary: C-ARC introduces a Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering method for real-time LiDAR data, specifically designed for non-repetitive LiDAR sensors to improve point cloud processing for mobile robotics algorithms.

title: A High-accuracy Event-based Underwater SLAM System
summary: This paper proposes a high-accuracy event-based underwater SLAM system, addressing the limitations of existing Time Surface (TS)-based methods which perform poorly with fluctuating camera velocities and repetitive underwater textures.

title: Object-Centric Residual RL for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real VLA Enhancement
summary: This work proposes Object-Centric Residual Reinforcement Learning for zero-shot sim-to-real enhancement of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, aiming to improve robustness in precise robotic manipulation tasks.

title: TactSpace: Learning a Physics-enriched Shared Latent Space for Tactile Sim-to-Real Transfer
summary: TactSpace focuses on learning a physics-enriched shared latent space for tactile sim-to-real transfer in robotic manipulation, addressing the fidelity gap in current tactile sensor simulators.

title: Sensor Configuration Matters: A Systematic Evaluation of Multimodal SLAM on Quadruped Robots
summary: This study systematically evaluates how sensor configuration impacts multimodal SLAM performance on quadruped robots, addressing a critical gap in understanding hardware-level sensor effects on autonomous navigation.

title: ReSiReg: Towards Spatially Consistent Semantics in Language-Conditioned Robotic Tasks
summary: ReSiReg aims to achieve spatially consistent semantics in language-conditioned robotic tasks by addressing the noise and lack of spatial consistency in dense Vision-Language Model (VLM) embeddings, crucial for robot reasoning in 3D space.

title: ART-VS: Adaptive Resolution Tiling for Vision Transformer Visual Servoing
summary: ART-VS introduces Adaptive Resolution Tiling for Vision Transformer visual servoing, offering a method to achieve both robustness and precision in robotic positioning by balancing coarse and fine patch-level descriptors.

title: GCNGrasp-VP: Affordance-Guided View Planning for Efficient Task-Oriented Grasping
summary: GCNGrasp-VP proposes an Affordance-Guided View Planning method for efficient task-oriented grasping in robotics, enabling active perception to overcome occlusions and incorporate task semantics.

title: Monocular 3D Occupancy Perception for Robots on Sidewalks via Hybrid 2D-3D Learning
summary: This research presents a Hybrid 2D-3D Learning approach for monocular 3D occupancy perception, enabling safe navigation for mobile robots like delivery bots and electric wheelchairs on cluttered sidewalks.

title: Viking Hill Dataset: A Lidar-Radar-Camera Dataset for Detection and Segmentation in Forest Scenes
summary: This dataset provides lidar-radar-camera data for detection and segmentation, designed to enhance perception for autonomous robots operating in forest environments.

title: HT-Bench: Benchmarking and Learning Dexterous Full-Hand Tactile Representations with Egocentric Vision
summary: HT-Bench introduces a new benchmark for learning dexterous full-hand tactile representations in robotic manipulation, using egocentric vision.

title: Hardware- and Vision-in-the-Loop Validation of Deep Monocular Pose Estimation for Autonomous Maritime UAV Flight
summary: A hardware- and vision-in-the-loop framework is presented for validating deep monocular pose estimation, enabling autonomous maritime UAV flight and indoor operations.

title: FAST-LIVGO: A Degeneracy-Robust LiDAR-Inertial-Visual-GNSS Fusion Odometry
summary: FAST-LIVGO proposes a degeneracy-robust LiDAR-Inertial-Visual-GNSS fusion odometry system for improved state estimation and mapping in dynamic environments for robotics.

title: Invertible Neural Network Adapter for One-Step Flow Matching in Robot Manipulation
summary: This paper presents an invertible neural network adapter for general robot manipulation, designed to generate precise actions from multimodal observations through a one-step denoising process.

title: Constant Time-Delay Leader Following with Neural Networks and Invariant Extended Kalman Filters for Arbitrary Trajectories
summary: A method for constant time-delay trajectory tracking in vehicle convoys is proposed, utilizing neural networks and Kalman filters for operations without inter-vehicle communication or global positioning.

title: Shape Sensing of Continuum Robots using Direct Laser Writing
summary: Research focuses on shape sensing for continuum robots using direct laser writing, addressing the challenge of estimating their form for applications like surgical procedures.

title: A Mixed-Reality Testbed for Autonomous Vehicles
summary: A mixed-reality, hardware-in-the-loop testbed is proposed for autonomous vehicles, integrating physical mobile robots with high-fidelity simulation for validating driving scenarios.

title: Modeling Branches for Active Manipulation using Iterative Parameter Estimation
summary: This study introduces a method for modeling diverse plant branches by iteratively estimating material parameters to support delicate manipulation in agricultural robotics.

title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos
summary: Research explores generating data for robotic manipulation, particularly for dexterous multi-fingered hands, by learning from everyday human videos.

title: Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation via Multi-View 3D-Grounded VLM Reasoning
summary: A zero-shot framework enables long-horizon dexterous manipulation by grounding language instructions into executable 3D task plans using a vision-language model.

title: RegimeVGGT: Layer-Wise Spatially Preserving Redundancy Removal for Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
summary: RegimeVGGT is presented as a method for layer-wise spatially preserving redundancy removal in Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers, improving 3D scene structure recovery from multi-view images.

title: AI Sandboxes: A Threat Model, Taxonomy, and Measurement Framework
summary: This paper outlines a threat model, taxonomy, and measurement framework for 'AI Sandboxes,' focusing on evaluating AI systems in bounded environments to ensure their safety and reliability.

title: Technical Report for ICRA 2026 GOOSE 2D Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation Challenge: Leveraging DINOv3 for Robust Outdoor Scene Understanding in Field Robotics
summary: This technical report details the first-place solution for the ICRA 2026 GOOSE 2D Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation Challenge, evaluating robust outdoor scene understanding in field robotics.

title: Aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition with patch-level self-supervised learning and expanded reciprocal re-ranking
summary: A method for aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition uses patch-level self-supervised learning for accurate positioning on point cloud maps, addressing limitations of ground-level methods.

title: Spatially Stratified Distillation for Heterogeneous Radar Place Recognition
summary: Research presents spatially stratified distillation for heterogeneous radar place recognition, enabling scalable, all-weather localization by matching automotive radar queries against high-fidelity maps.

title: Motion-Focused Latent Action Enables Cross-Embodiment VLA Training from Human EgoVideos
summary: A method called Motion-Focused Latent Action enables cross-embodiment VLA training from human egocentric videos, addressing the challenge of obtaining diverse robotic datasets with action labels for manipulation.

title: Mem-World: Memory-Augmented Action-Conditioned World Models for Persistent Robot Manipulation
summary: Mem-World introduces memory-augmented action-conditioned world models for persistent robot manipulation, addressing challenges in long-term world modeling for robotic tasks.

title: OneCanvas: 3D Scene Understanding via Panoramic Reprojection
summary: OneCanvas proposes a method for 3D scene understanding via panoramic reprojection, allowing Vision-Language Models to achieve spatial reasoning by aggregating features onto a single canvas.

title: CABLE: Cloud-Assisted Bandwidth-efficient LMM-based Encoding for V2X Systems
summary: CABLE presents a cloud-assisted, bandwidth-efficient encoding approach for Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems, reducing communication overhead and latency.

summary: Policy support and mass production are driving an ETF focused on humanoid robotics, as the sector enters a critical investment phase in China.

title: UBTECH U1 Series Presales Near 5,000 Units in 17 Days: A Milestone for Consumer Humanoid Robots
summary: UBTECH has achieved a milestone with nearly 5,000 pre-orders for its U1 series companion humanoid robot within 17 days, indicating strong consumer interest.

title: Kremeľ ich poľahky oklamal. Európska umelá inteligencia nekontrolovane šíri ruské dezinformácie
summary: A European AI model, intended for integration by the French army, reportedly exhibits serious security flaws and has uncontrollably spread Russian disinformation.

title: SpaceX wants to build AI data centers in space. Will it work?
summary: SpaceX is exploring building AI data centers in space to meet the growing demand for computing power and leverage orbital advantages, despite the high costs and operational challenges.

title: Deontic Policies for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems
summary: This paper explores the need for deontic policies to govern autonomous agentic AI systems, addressing security, privacy, and compliance challenges arising from their ability to use tools and manipulate data.

title: Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis
summary: This paper experimentally analyzes Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) as an alternative generative paradigm to traditional autoregressive LLMs, generating text through iterative denoising.

title: Hidden Anchors in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
summary: This research investigates hidden anchors in multi-agent LLM deliberation, exploring how agents exchange and revise answers over multiple rounds to improve reasoning and accuracy.

title: DeXposure-Claw: An Agentic System for DeFi Risk Supervision
summary: DeXposure-Claw is introduced as an agentic system designed for decentralized finance (DeFi) risk supervision, addressing the limitations of general-purpose LLM agents in this high-stakes domain.

title: LLM Doesn't Know What It Doesn't Know: Detecting Epistemic Blind Spots via Cross-Model Attribution Divergence on Clinical Tabular Data
summary: This research investigates whether LLMs can recognize their own knowledge limitations ("epistemic blind spots") when applied to clinical tabular data, aiming to reduce uncertainty in their applications.

title: REVEAL++: Differentiable Phenotypic Grouping for Vision-Language Retinal Modeling of Alzheimer's Disease Risk
summary: REVEAL++ is presented as a differentiable phenotypic grouping framework for vision-language retinal modeling, used to assess the risk of Alzheimer's disease by pairing retinal images with clinical narratives.

title: Emergent Alignment
summary: This research explores "Emergent Alignment," investigating whether LLMs can self-correct when their outputs are misaligned with human ethics by endowing them with a conscience step and an alignment component during training.

title: ITNet: A Learnable Integral Transform That Subsumes Convolution, Attention, and Recurrence
summary: This paper introduces ITNet, a learnable integral transform designed to unify and subsume various neural network architectures like convolution, attention, and recurrence.

title: Uncertainty Decomposition for Clarification Seeking in LLM Agents
summary: This research explores new methods for uncertainty decomposition in LLM agents to enable clarification seeking, arguing that traditional uncertainty frameworks are insufficient for interactive agent systems.

title: Analyzing the Narration Gap in LLM-Solver Loops
summary: This paper analyzes the "narration gap" when embedding formal SAT/SMT solvers into LLM reasoning pipelines, where solvers provide logically guaranteed steps unlike chain-of-thought.

title: Configurable Clinical Information Extraction with Agentic RAG: What Works, What Breaks, and Why
summary: This research explores configurable clinical information extraction using agentic RAG, analyzing its effectiveness and limitations when processing heterogeneous patient data with incomplete metadata.

title: Which Pairs to Compare for LLM Post-Training?
summary: This paper investigates optimal strategies for selecting comparison pairs in preference-based post-training, a key paradigm for aligning language models, to improve training efficiency and effectiveness.

title: AI4SE and SE4AI Exploration: A Decade Looking Back and Forward
summary: This article reviews a decade of progress and future directions at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Systems Engineering (SE), highlighting key developments and community growth.

title: BrainG3N: A Dual-Purpose Tokenizer for Controllable 3D Brain MRI Generation
summary: BrainG3N introduces a dual-purpose tokenizer for controllable 3D brain MRI generation, aiming to augment under-represented cohorts and simulate disease trajectories for clinical applications.

title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Predictive Validity for the Evaluation of LLM Agents
summary: This paper advocates for "predictive validity" in evaluating LLM agents, moving beyond static leaderboards by analyzing multiple implementation studies of an MCP-based industrial-agent benchmark.

title: GLARE: A Natural Language Interface for Querying Global Explanations
summary: GLARE is presented as a natural language interface designed to facilitate querying and understanding of global explanations for vision models, addressing the complexity of traditional explanation methods.

title: Interpreting Neural Combinatorial Optimization via Evolving Programmatic Bottlenecks
summary: This research explores methods for interpreting Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) models by evolving programmatic bottlenecks to overcome their black-box nature and aid in diagnosis and deployment.

title: A Comparative Study of Pretrained Transformer Models for Quranic ASR: Speech Representations, Label Formats, and Dataset Composition
summary: This comparative study evaluates pretrained transformer models for Quranic Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). It aims to convert Quranic recitation into text, highlighting challenges like high Word Error Rates on user-recited verses.

title: Benchmarking Agentic Review Systems
summary: This paper presents a new benchmark for evaluating agentic review systems, which are emerging to support peer review under pressure from AI-assisted research. It evaluates two open-source systems (OpenAIReview, coarse) and one proprietary system (Reviewer3).

title: Grounded Inference: Principles for Deterministically Encapsulated Generative Models
summary: This research outlines principles for deterministically encapsulating generative models, addressing the perils of integrating them into traditional computational systems. It proposes foundational frameworks to de-risk AI incorporation.

title: Beyond Entropy: Learning from Token-Level Distributional Deviations for LLM Reasoning
summary: This research investigates optimization instability in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning, specifically addressing entropy collapse. It proposes learning from token-level distributional deviations to overcome premature convergence to suboptimal strategies.

title: AgentFinVQA: A Deployable Multi-Agent Pipeline for Auditable Financial Chart QA
summary: AgentFinVQA is introduced as a deployable multi-agent pipeline designed for auditable financial chart question answering in regulated settings. It aims to provide trustworthy and auditable answers, addressing the limitations of opaque, accuracy-focused existing chart-QA agents.

title: ORAgentBench: Can LLM Agents Solve Challenging Operations Research Tasks End to End?
summary: ORAgentBench is presented as a new benchmark to evaluate the ability of LLM agents to solve challenging operations research (OR) tasks end-to-end. It aims to clarify the performance of autonomous agents in realistic OR work, which is often decoupled in existing evaluations.

title: CombEval: A Framework for Evaluating Combinatorial Counting in Large Language Models
summary: CombEval is introduced as a dynamic benchmark framework for evaluating combinatorial counting in large language models. It represents problems using a typed Cofola specification to enable controlled generation of natural-language counting queries.

title: Think Again or Think Longer? Selective Verification for Budget-Aware Reasoning
summary: This research studies selective verification for budget-aware reasoning, analyzing whether additional test-time reasoning consistently adds value or wastes compute. It frames this as a deployment allocation problem to optimize reasoning for efficiency.

title: Human-on-the-Loop Orchestration for AI-Assisted Legal Discovery
summary: This paper explores human-on-the-loop orchestration for AI-assisted legal discovery, focusing on autonomous LLM agents in e-discovery workflows. It addresses the challenge of compounding errors in multi-step reasoning that could lead to legal malpractice.

title: TelcoAgent: A Scalable 5G Multi-KPM Forecasting With 3GPP-Grounded Explainability
summary: TelcoAgent is a scalable multi-agent system designed for 5G Key Performance Measurement (KPM) forecasting with 3GPP-grounded explainability. It aims to improve proactive network management by overcoming the scalability and explainability limitations of existing machine learning approaches.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Black-Box Uncertainty Estimation Methods for Large Language Models
summary: This systematic evaluation focuses on black-box uncertainty estimation methods for Large Language Models (LLMs). It highlights the importance of uncertainty estimation for building trustworthy LLMs due to their unreliability and tendency to hallucinate.

title: MetaResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Self-Reflective Reinforcement Learning in Adversarial Virtual Environments
summary: MetaResearcher is an agent system designed for scaling deep research through self-reflective reinforcement learning in adversarial virtual environments. It aims to overcome limitations in training research agents, such as static simulations and inefficient outcome-based reinforcement.

title: Multi-Agent Transactive Memory
summary: This paper proposes Multi-Agent Transactive Memory as an infrastructure for knowledge sharing among heterogeneous LLM agent populations. It outlines how retrieval systems can organize agent-generated knowledge to support multi-agent problem-solving.

title: eCNNTO: A Highly Generalizable ConvNet for Accelerating Topology Optimization
summary: This work introduces eCNNTO, a highly generalizable element-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) designed to accelerate density-based Topology Optimization (TO). It targets the efficiency bottleneck caused by numerous finite element analysis iterations in TO.

title: The Tao of Agency: Autotelic AI, Embedded Agency and Dissolution of the Self
summary: This article explores 'Autotelic AI' and 'Embedded Agency', discussing what happens when AI agents generate their own goals instead of pursuing designer-specified objectives. It delves into the philosophical implications of AI discovering its own purpose and the dissolution of the self.

title: PhysDrift: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in Humanoid Co-Speech Motion Generation
summary: PhysDrift is a method for generating physically executable co-speech motions for humanoid robots, bridging the embodiment gap. It aims to produce expressive and speech-aligned movements that respect humanoid constraints, moving beyond human-centric generation pipelines.

title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World
summary: ENPIRE proposes a method for agentic robot policy self-improvement in the real world, aiming for dexterous robotic manipulation. It addresses the bottleneck of human supervision and algorithm engineering in achieving general physical intelligence.

title: Reward as An Agent for Embodied World Models
summary: This work proposes 'Reward as An Agent' for embodied world models, challenging conservative reinforcement learning paradigms. It argues for a more dynamic role for reward to enhance exploration, behavioral diversity, and dynamic discovery in these models.

title: Autonomous Event-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration for Enterprise AI at Scale
summary: This paper evaluates autonomous event-driven multi-agent orchestration for Enterprise AI at scale, moving beyond discrete request-response workflows. It assesses methods like DAG Plan and Execute and ReAct for continuous event monitoring and action across specialist agents.

title: Process-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Theorem Proving via Lean
summary: This research introduces Process-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Theorem Proving via Lean, leveraging rich, structured feedback from symbolic proof assistants. It addresses the gap between fine-grained processes in formal reasoning and traditional binary verification signals in RLVR.

title: Residual-Space Evolutionary Optimization via Flow-based Generative Models
summary: This paper proposes a residual-space evolutionary optimization method for data editing using flow-based generative models, addressing limitations where traditional gradient-based search is not applicable.

title: Multi-Head Attention-Based Feature Extractor Integration with Soft Actor-Critic for Porosity Prediction and Process Parameter Optimization in Additive Manufacturing
summary: This research integrates a multi-head attention-based feature extractor with Soft Actor-Critic reinforcement learning for predicting porosity and optimizing process parameters in additive manufacturing. The method aims to overcome limitations of traditional RL in complex optimization tasks.

title: ScaffoldAgent: Utility-Guided Dynamic Outline Optimization for Open-Ended Deep Research
summary: ScaffoldAgent is introduced as a utility-guided dynamic outline optimization system designed to assist in open-ended deep research by improving knowledge acquisition, evidence organization, and coherent report generation through multi-round retrieval.

title: Learning to Prompt: Improving Student Engagement with Adaptive LLM-based High-School Tutoring
summary: This paper presents a system using adaptive, subject-aware prompting for LLM-based high-school tutoring to improve student engagement and personalize education. The system leverages 14 pedagogical features to tailor interactions.

title: BIM-Edit: Benchmarking Large Language Models for IFC-Based Building Information Modeling
