summary: BIM-Edit is introduced as a benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models' capabilities in IFC-Based Building Information Modeling. It assesses their ability to understand, edit, and semantically preserve existing CAD scenes from textual instructions.

title: Modularity-Free Conflict-Averse Training for Generalized PINNs
summary: This research introduces a modularity-free conflict-averse training method for generalized Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). The method aims to improve the robustness and stability of PINN training by addressing gradient interference.

title: Implicit Semantic-Aware Communication Based on Hypergraph Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes an implicit semantic-aware communication paradigm based on hypergraph reasoning for next-generation communication systems. The goal is to shift from bit-level transmission to reliably recovering and understanding the semantic meaning of information.

title: Apparent Psychological Profiles of Large Language Models are Largely a Measurement Artifact
summary: This research argues that apparent psychological profiles assigned to large language models using human-designed instruments are largely a measurement artifact. It uses a formal psychometric framework to challenge the validity of such assessments.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Measuring Logical Compliance of Predictive Models
summary: This paper proposes new methods for measuring the logical compliance of predictive machine learning models, moving beyond traditional accuracy metrics. It focuses on evaluating whether model outputs respect specified logical constraints.

title: Augmenting Game AI with Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper explores augmenting game AI with Deep Reinforcement Learning to create more believable and complex in-game characters. It addresses the challenge of capturing behavioral complexity beyond hand-coded systems.

title: QMFOL: Benchmarking Large Language Model Reasoning via Quantifiable Monadic First-Order Logic Test Case Generation
summary: QMFOL is a new benchmarking method for evaluating Large Language Model reasoning capabilities, specifically via quantifiable Monadic First-Order Logic test case generation. It aims to provide fine-grained control over logical complexity for evaluation.

title: Thermodynamic Measure of Intelligence
summary: This theoretical paper proposes a thermodynamic measure of intelligence, defining it as the lawful amplification of rare but valid futures. It suggests that intelligence increases the probability of unlikely yet admissible outcomes.

title: A Multi-Agent system for Multi-Objective constrained optimization
summary: This research introduces a multi-agent system designed for multi-objective constrained optimization problems, particularly in dynamic computing and networking environments. It leverages reinforcement learning to handle costs and constraint violations.

title: Navigating Unreliable Parametric and Contextual Knowledge: Explicit Knowledge Conflict Resolution for LLM Inference
summary: This paper investigates explicit knowledge conflict resolution mechanisms for LLM inference, focusing on how large language models navigate unreliable parametric and contextual knowledge during reasoning.

title: Confidence-Aware Automated Assessment of Student-Drawn Scientific Models
summary: This research presents a confidence-aware automated assessment system for evaluating student-drawn scientific models in science education. The system aims to overcome the need for expert human judgment in interpreting complex visual representations.

title: Lagrange: An Open-Vocabulary, Energy-Based Sparse Framework for Generalized End-to-End Driving
summary: Lagrange is introduced as an open-vocabulary, energy-based sparse framework designed for generalized end-to-end autonomous driving. It aims to improve perceptual models and planners for complex, open-world environments.

title: When to Trust, How to Distill: Multi-Foundation Model Guidance for Lightweight, Robust Scientific Time Series Forecasting
summary: This research explores multi-foundation model guidance and distillation techniques to improve the robustness and lightweight deployment of Time-Series Foundation Models for scientific time series forecasting. It addresses issues of distributional misalignment in scientific domains.

title: Closing the Social-Semantic Gap: SPSD for Edge-Based Prompt Compression in Cloud LLM Inference
summary: This paper introduces SPSD (Social-Semantic Prompt Distillation) for edge-based prompt compression to reduce cloud-scale energy costs during Large Language Model inference. It aims to optimize prompts by removing social scaffolding.

title: Performance Analysis and Optimization of 3D Generative Diffusion Models across GPU Architectures
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis and optimization study for 3D generative diffusion models across various GPU architectures. It addresses the substantial GPU resource demands and heterogeneous kernel behavior of these models.

title: Information Lattice Learning as Probabilistic Graphical Model Structure Learning
summary: This research reinterprets Information Lattice Learning as a method for probabilistic graphical model structure learning. It focuses on learning interpretable rules of a signal through projections onto a partition lattice.

title: Weibull Weight-Scale Parameter Evolution under AdamW Training Dynamics
summary: This research studies the evolution of the Weibull weight-scale parameter in transformer weight distributions during AdamW training, deriving a three-force decomposition of the squared weight norm.

title: Human-like autonomy emerges from self-play and a pinch of human data
summary: This research explores training human-like driving policies using self-play reinforcement learning and limited human data, leveraging large-scale simulations to substitute expensive driving demonstrations.

title: ProMUSE: Progressive Multi-modal Uncertainty-guided Staged Evidential Alzheimer Disease Classification
summary: ProMUSE is a new method for early Alzheimer's disease classification that uses progressive multi-modal uncertainty-guided staged evidential learning to improve diagnosis from clinical assessments.

title: cAPM: Continual AI-Assisted Pace-Mapping with Active Learning
summary: cAPM is a novel AI-assisted pace-mapping method that uses active learning for continually identifying intervention targets during catheter ablation of ventricular tachycardia.

title: Protein Representation Learning with Secondary-Structure and Energy-Filtered Hydrogen-Bond Graphs
summary: This paper introduces a new method for protein representation learning that uses graph-based representations incorporating secondary-structure and energy-filtered hydrogen-bond graphs for improved protein modeling.

title: Physics-Informed Discovery of Yield Functions in Plasticity via Convex Neural Representations
summary: This study proposes a physics-informed method to discover anisotropic yield functions in plasticity using convex neural representations, addressing challenges in mechanical measurements and analytical form selection.

title: Cost-Optimal LLM Routing with Limited User Feedback under User Satisfaction Guarantees
summary: This paper proposes a method for cost-optimal LLM routing that incorporates limited user feedback to guarantee user satisfaction in commercial applications while managing rising inference costs.

title: Emyx: Fast and efficient all-atom protein generation
summary: Emyx is a new method for fast and efficient all-atom protein generation that improves upon existing generative models by providing both geometric accuracy and structural diversity for computational enzyme design.

title: A Hybrid GNN-FEM Framework for Phase-Field Fracture Simulation. Physics-Preserving Hybridization for Generalizable Surrogate Modeling
summary: This study proposes a hybrid GNN-FEM framework for phase-field fracture simulation, aiming to provide physics-preserving and generalizable surrogate modeling for complex physical systems using scientific machine learning.

title: How Linear Is a Transformer Feed-Forward Block? Per-Block Linear Recoverability Is Learned, Not Architectural
summary: This research investigates the linearity of transformer feed-forward blocks, measuring their nonlinearity and showing that per-block linear recoverability is learned rather than being an architectural property.

title: VERITAS: Verifier-Guided Proof Search for Zero-Shot Formal Theorem Proving
summary: VERITAS is a zero-shot framework that enhances LLM-based formal theorem proving by routing rich verifier signals back into proof search through a two-phase protocol.

title: Thermodynamic Signatures of Reasoning: Free-Energy and Spectral-Form-Factor Diagnostics for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces a method for detecting hallucinations in large language models by using thermodynamic signatures and spectral-form-factor diagnostics derived from attention-based graph Laplacians.

title: FlexLAM: Resolving the Bottleneck Trade-off in Latent Action Learning
summary: FlexLAM is a new method for Latent Action Learning that resolves the bottleneck trade-off by improving the interface between action-free video and downstream decision-making.

title: Spectral DPPs via NEPv: A Scalable Continuous Relaxation of Determinantal MAP for Diversity-Aware Data Selection
summary: This paper introduces Spectral DPPs via NEPv, a scalable continuous relaxation of Determinantal MAP for diversity-aware data selection, crucial for data curation and coreset selection in machine learning.

title: Does Text Actually Help? Uncovering and Resolving Text Collapse in Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
summary: This research uncovers and resolves 'text collapse,' a failure mode in multimodal time series forecasting where the text branch converges to a context-independent state, hindering the effectiveness of textual information.

title: MortarBench: Evaluating Mortgage Loan Origination Agents
summary: MortarBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the performance and reliability of mortgage loan origination agents in assessing applicant eligibility and risk.

title: 3D-DLP: Self-Supervised 3D Object-Centric Scene Representation Learning
summary: 3D-DLP is a new self-supervised object-centric representation learning model that decomposes 3D scene observations into a set of 3D latent particles, each encoding disentangled attributes like 3D keypoint positions.

title: Can In-Context Learning Support Intrinsic Curiosity?
summary: This research investigates whether in-context learning can support intrinsic curiosity, a mechanism for automated data selection, to improve effective data collection in machine learning.

title: Insulin4RL: Real-Time Insulin Management in the Intensive Care Unit for Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Insulin4RL is a system that applies offline reinforcement learning to real-time insulin management in Intensive Care Units, aiming to improve clinical decision-making using historical electronic health record data.

title: Concept Flow Models: Anchoring Concept-Based Reasoning with Hierarchical Bottlenecks
summary: Concept Flow Models are introduced as an advancement to Concept Bottleneck Models, aiming to enhance interpretability and anchor concept-based reasoning using hierarchical bottlenecks.

title: Algebraic Dead Directions in LayerNorm Transformers: A Forward-Pass-Only Diagnostic at LLM Scale
summary: This paper explores singular minima and "dead directions" in the loss landscape of pretrained LayerNorm transformers, proposing a forward-pass-only diagnostic for these phenomena at LLM scale. It investigates the theoretical properties of transformer models' optimization.

title: Calibrating Generative Models to Feature Distributions with MMD Finetuning
summary: This research introduces MMD finetuning to calibrate generative models, enabling them to produce samples that not only appear plausible but also align with the feature distributions of a target dataset. It addresses issues where models might deviate from desired statistical properties in applications like drug discovery.

title: Interactive Pareto navigation for deep multi-task learning
summary: This paper proposes an interactive Pareto navigation approach for deep multi-task learning to manage increasing objectives and computational challenges. The method aims to help decision-makers choose appropriate trade-offs by aggregating individual losses into a single loss function.

title: Techniques for Peak Memory Reduction for LoRA Fine-tuning of LLMs on Edge Devices
summary: This research investigates techniques for reducing peak memory consumption during LoRA fine-tuning of Large Language Models on edge devices. It aims to overcome severe memory constraints on consumer hardware, enabling personalized and private LLM experiences.

title: Tracking Representation Dynamics in Large Language Models with Persistent Homology
summary: This paper tracks the evolution of internal representations in Large Language Models during supervised fine-tuning by applying persistent homology to analyze the topology of activation spaces. The research aims to understand how LLMs' internal dynamics change during alignment.

title: Predicting Mergeability of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Updates
summary: This research explores methods to predict the mergeability of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) adapters for language models, aiming to reduce the costly process of training and evaluating adapters individually. It addresses the challenge of combining multiple LoRA adaptations efficiently.

title: Displacement Is Not Direction: Evaluating Fidelity Metrics for Quantized LLM Deployment
summary: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of common fidelity metrics, such as per-token KL divergence, as proxies for benchmark quality in quantized LLM deployment. It tests these metrics on various quantized versions of LLMs like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Devstral-Small-2-24B.

title: Understanding Key Features of Time Series Foundation Models from Epidemic Forecasting
summary: This research investigates key features of Time Series Foundation Models through their application to epidemic forecasting, specifically for seasonal influenza. It aims to improve accurate short-term public health predictions for better resource allocation.

title: Advances in Scientific Machine Learning for Coupled Fluid Flow and Transport
summary: This chapter reviews recent advances in Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) applied to modeling coupled fluid flow and transport phenomena, including systems governed by Navier-Stokes equations. It covers applications such as turbidity currents and thermal convection.

title: On the QUEST for Uncertainty Quantification via Highest Density Regions
summary: This paper explores uncertainty quantification (UQ) using Highest Density Regions to enhance reliable decision-making in safety-critical probabilistic machine learning applications. It addresses regression problems and aims to measure uncertainty beyond pointwise predictive risk.

title: IHBench: Evaluating Post-Interruption Recovery in Voice Agents with Structured Workflows
summary: This paper introduces IHBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the post-interruption recovery capabilities of voice agents operating in structured workflows like customer service or healthcare scheduling. It aims to assess how well agents maintain progress despite frequent user interruptions.

title: Comparing Linear Probes with Mahalanobis Cosine Similarity
summary: This paper compares linear probes, widely used in interpretability research, using Mahalanobis Cosine Similarity (MCS) as a refined, task-aware alternative to standard cosine similarity. It explores how MCS reweights inner products by test data covariance to improve comparisons.

title: Latent Confounded Causal Discovery via Lie Bracket Geometry
summary: This paper introduces a method for latent confounded causal discovery through Lie Bracket Geometry, building on previous work on Kan-Do-Calculus. It explores the mathematical foundations of causal inference, distinguishing between passive observation and active intervention.

title: SEAGAN: domain-Specific and Edge-Aware Graph Attention Network for Dynamic Plant Processes
summary: This paper introduces SEAGAN (domain-Specific and Edge-Aware Graph Attention Network), a new GNN architecture designed for learning from scientific data related to dynamic plant processes. It provides a flexible framework for analyzing complex biological and physical relationships in plant physiology.

title: MassSpecGym in the Wild: Uncovering and Correcting Evaluation Pitfalls in AI-Driven Molecule Discovery
summary: This paper uncovers and corrects evaluation pitfalls in AI-driven molecule discovery, specifically for tandem mass spectrometry, emphasizing the importance of reliable benchmarking. It highlights how experimental design issues can compromise the trustworthiness of model evaluations.

title: Hard or Just Unreached? Diagnosing the Sampling Blind Spot in Math-Reasoning Difficulty Estimation
summary: This research diagnoses a "sampling blind spot" in math-reasoning difficulty estimation used in benchmarks, which often rely on `pass@k` as a proxy. It reveals persistent issues with this metric that impact RL with verifiable rewards and data curation.

title: Convex training of Lipschitz-regularized shallow neural networks
summary: This paper introduces a convex training procedure for Lipschitz-regularized shallow neural networks to enhance their robustness against adversarial attacks. The method efficiently solves a non-convex training program by applying a convex restriction.

title: LOKI: Memory-Free Null-Space Constrained Lifelong Knowledge Editing
summary: This paper presents LOKI, a memory-free and null-space constrained method for lifelong knowledge editing in language models. It aims to efficiently and sequentially update models with new information while preserving previously learned knowledge.

title: Multi-Granular Attention-Driven Reinforcement Learning Framework for Web Intelligent Enhancement Systems
summary: This paper proposes a multi-granular attention-driven reinforcement learning framework designed for Web Intelligent Enhancement Systems. The framework aims to improve personalized, context-aware services by better handling heterogeneous and dynamic web data.

title: Efficiently Representing Algorithms With Chain-of-Thought Transformers
summary: This paper explores the theoretical capabilities of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) transformers, demonstrating their efficiency in representing algorithms and simulating Turing machines. It justifies the use of reasoning models by showing their computational power.

title: Efficient Neural Network Model Selection for Few-Class Application Datasets
summary: This research investigates how dataset properties can guide efficient neural network model selection, particularly for few-class application datasets, to optimize the process of choosing models.

title: OnDeFog: Online Decision Transformer under Frame Dropping
summary: This paper introduces OnDeFog, an online Decision Transformer model designed to mitigate performance degradation in reinforcement learning applications caused by communication delays or sensor failures leading to frame dropping.

title: Federated Bilevel Performative Prediction
summary: This research proposes a novel federated bilevel optimization approach to address challenges in nested learning problems across distributed clients, especially when client data distributions are not fixed, for applications like federated hyperparameter tuning and meta-learning.

title: Manifold Bandits: Bayesian Curriculum Learning over the Latent Geometry of Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces Manifold Bandits, a Bayesian curriculum learning method designed to improve the efficiency of reinforcement learning for large language models by optimizing how problems are sampled during training based on their latent geometry.

title: Learning universal approximations for partial differential equations with Physics-Informed Broad Learning System
summary: This paper introduces a Physics-Informed Broad Learning System for learning universal approximations of partial differential equations, aiming to overcome the high computational costs of traditional numerical solvers and limitations of existing Physics-Informed Neural Networks.

title: Flow Map Denoisers: Traversing the Distortion-Perception Plane for Inverse Problems
summary: This research introduces "Flow Map Denoisers," a method designed to navigate the distortion-perception tradeoff in image restoration, allowing for flexible operation points between minimizing error and maximizing perceptual quality for inverse problems.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF
summary: This research proposes an uncertainty-aware reward modeling approach for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to improve the stability and reliability of large language model alignment by addressing challenges in reward model prediction and confidence.

title: Enhancing Graph Neural Networks Using Proximity Graphs for Dust Source Emission Forecasting
summary: This research demonstrates how enhancing Graph Neural Networks with proximity graphs can improve the accuracy of dust source emission forecasting, which is critical for mitigating environmental and health hazards posed by dust storms.

title: When, Where, and How: Adaptive Binning for Tabular Self-Supervised Learning
summary: This research introduces an adaptive binning strategy for tabular self-supervised learning, focusing on medical tabular data to leverage routinely available clinical variables without requiring costly expert adjudication for labels.

title: Neural Additive and Basis Models with Feature Selection and Interactions
summary: This research enhances the interpretability of deep neural networks by introducing Neural Additive and Basis Models with improved feature selection and interaction capabilities, building on Generalized Additive Models.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Squeeze-Excitation-like Attention
summary: This paper introduces SEA-PINN, a novel Physics-Informed Neural Network architecture that incorporates a Squeeze-Excitation-like attention mechanism to dynamically recalibrate neuron importance and achieve highly stable initialization.

title: Exposing the Unsaid: Visualizing Hidden LLM Bias through Stochastic Path Aggregation
summary: This research proposes a method called Stochastic Path Aggregation to visualize and expose hidden representational and syntactic biases within Large Language Models, which are otherwise difficult to evaluate due to the stochastic nature of text generation.

title: Ensembles of Large Language Models for Identifying EQ-5D Studies in PubMed Based on Their Abstracts
summary: This research explores the use of ensembles of Large Language Models to efficiently identify EQ-5D studies in PubMed abstracts, aiming to improve the resource-intensive and inconsistent manual screening process in systematic literature reviews.

title: Disentangling Linguistic Relatedness from Task Alignment in Cross-Lingual Transfer
summary: This research investigates cross-lingual transfer in large language models by fine-tuning them on Arabic and evaluating zero-shot reading comprehension across Semitic and non-Semitic languages, aiming to disentangle linguistic relatedness from task alignment.

title: How LLMs Fail and Generalize in RTL Coding for Hardware Design?
summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models perform and generalize in RTL coding for hardware design, introducing a new error taxonomy to categorize failures and understand the challenges in translating sequential programming into parallel temporal logic.

title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
summary: This item introduces the DeepSeek-V4 series, comprising two new Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models, DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, both supporting an efficient million-token context length.

title: Where to Place the Query? Unveiling and Mitigating Positional Bias in In-Context Learning for Diffusion LLMs via Decoding Dynamics
summary: This research investigates positional bias in In-Context Learning for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) and proposes methods to unveil and mitigate this bias by analyzing decoding dynamics, contrasting with autoregressive models.

title: Pruning via Causal Attribution Preserves Reasoning Performance in Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces Causal Attribution Pruning (CAP), a training-free method that identifies and prunes critical attention heads in large language models to reduce inference cost while preserving multi-step reasoning performance.

title: Detecting Hallucinations for Large Language Model-based Knowledge Graph Reasoning
summary: This research focuses on detecting hallucinations in large language model-based knowledge graph reasoning frameworks, which are increasingly used for tasks like question answering, recommendation, and decision support.

title: Quantifying Aleatoric Uncertainty of In-Context Learning for Robust Measure of LLM Prediction Confidence
summary: This research focuses on quantifying the aleatoric uncertainty of In-Context Learning in large language models to provide a more robust measure of prediction confidence, addressing concerns about reliability and sensitivity to prompt design.

title: Granularity-Regulated Adaptive Computational Efficiency for Optimal Verification in Test-Time Scaling
summary: This paper introduces a method called Granularity-Regulated Adaptive Computational Efficiency (GRACE) for Test-Time Scaling (TTS) to improve the reasoning performance of large language models by optimizing compute at inference time.

title: Trustworthy Multi-Agent Systems: Mitigating Semantic Drift with the Argent Signaling Protocol
summary: This research proposes the Argent Signaling Protocol to mitigate semantic drift in multi-agent LLM systems, improving the trustworthiness and effectiveness of their outputs by distinguishing types of failure.

title: Characterizing Narrative Content in Web-scale LLM Pretraining Data
summary: This study presents the first fine-grained analysis of narrative content within web-scale LLM pretraining corpora, using the 3-trillion-token Dolma dataset to characterize its narrative features.

title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
summary: This paper systematically evaluates the reliability and validity of 'LLM-as-a-Judge' models, finding that current validation metrics overstate their discriminative ability across agreement, consistency, and bias.

title: LaViSA: A Language and Vision Structural Ambiguity Benchmark
summary: This introduces LaViSA, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Vision and Language Models (VLMs) on resolving structural ambiguity in sentences by leveraging visual cues.

title: Where Does Social Reasoning Come From? Capability Provenance in Language Models
summary: This research uses training-data attribution to investigate how different regions of a pretraining corpus contribute to the emergence of social reasoning versus STEM reasoning capabilities in the OLMo3-7B language model.

title: Before the Labels: How Dataset Construction Shapes Suicidality Detection in Clinical Text
summary: This article discusses how the construction of datasets for suicidality detection in clinical text can embed specific operationalizations and biases, impacting the reliability and ethical implications of NLP systems in healthcare.

title: MiqraBERT: Regression-Based Sentence-BERT Finetuning for Biblical Hebrew Parallel Detection
summary: This paper introduces MiqraBERT, a finetuned Sentence-BERT model specifically designed for regression-based detection of textual reuse and parallels in the Hebrew Bible, moving beyond lexical overlap methods.

title: Creating Multilingual Mental Health Dialogue Datasets: Limits of Persona-Based Localization via Nationality and Language
summary: This paper explores the challenges and limitations of creating multilingual mental health dialogue datasets for training AI and large language models, particularly concerning persona-based localization via nationality and language.

title: From 50K to 8.2 Million in 24 Hours: Vozinha's Algorithmic Consecration and the Multilingual Making of World Cup Visibility
summary: This study presents a multilingual computational discourse analysis of how algorithmic processes constructed the visibility and 'consecration' of goalkeeper Vozinha during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, based on social media interactions.

title: SAGE-OPD: Selective Agent-Guided Intervention for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper proposes SAGE-OPD (Selective Agent-Guided Intervention for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation), a method to improve the training of multi-turn LLM agents by mitigating exposure bias through policy distillation.

title: CacheWeaver: Cache-Aware Evidence Ordering for Efficient Grounded RAG Inference
summary: This paper introduces CacheWeaver, a method for cache-aware evidence ordering to improve the efficiency of grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) inference by optimizing prefix caching in serving engines.

title: Code-Switching Reveals Language Anchoring in Multilingual LLMs
summary: This research investigates how code-switching affects the performance of Multilingual Large Language Models (MLLMs), revealing insights into language anchoring and performance degradation with mixed-language inputs.

title: What sentiment analysis can't see: Measuring whether customers were helped, and what went wrong, across 70,000 support conversations
summary: This study analyzes 70,000 customer support conversations to measure customer satisfaction beyond sentiment analysis, testing a richer alternative to determine if customers were helped and identifying issues.

title: TerraMARS: A Domain-Adapted Small-Language-Model Pipeline for Mars Terraforming Literature
summary: This paper introduces TerraMARS, a domain-adapted Small-Language-Model (SLM) pipeline designed to extract comprehensive knowledge from Mars terraforming scientific literature, supporting research into planetary habitability.

title: FineREX: Fine-Tuned NER-RE for Human Smuggling Knowledge Graphs
summary: This research introduces FineREX, a fine-tuned Named Entity Recognition and Relation Extraction (NER-RE) system designed to build knowledge graphs from legal documents to identify and analyze human smuggling networks.

title: NRITYAM: Language Models Meet Art and Heritage of Dance
summary: This paper presents NRITYAM, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the cultural comprehension capabilities of language models, focusing on the art and heritage of dance to bridge global AI effectiveness with local contexts.

title: Beyond Uniform Forgetting: A Study of Sequential Direct Preference Optimization Across Preference Settings
summary: This study investigates sequential Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) as a method for aligning language models with multiple human preferences, examining the implications of applying objectives sequentially.

title: Clusters are All You Need: Pre-Training the Tsetlin Machine with Semantic Clusters from Language Models for Interpretability
summary: This paper proposes pre-training the interpretable Tsetlin Machine with semantic clusters derived from language models like BERT to achieve strong, transparent text classification performance.

title: CREDENCE: Claim Reduction for Decomposition & Enhanced Credibility -- Semantic Metrics and Convergence Analysis
summary: This paper introduces CREDENCE, a method for claim reduction and decomposition using semantic metrics to enhance the credibility and reliability of automated fact-checking systems.

title: Leverage Is Not Reach: A Control-Window Law for Single-Neuron Steering in Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a 'control-window law' framework for single-neuron steering, aiming to predict when interventions in language model neurons coherently control behavior without output collapse.

title: AtomMem: Building Simple and Effective Memory System for LLM Agents via Atomic Facts
summary: This research introduces AtomMem, a simple and effective memory system for LLM agents that uses atomic facts to overcome context window limitations and enable long-term information accumulation.

title: Prompt, Plan, Extract: Zero-Shot Agentic LLMs Workflows for Lung Pathology Extraction from Clinical Narratives
summary: This research presents 'Prompt, Plan, Extract,' a zero-shot agentic LLM workflow designed to extract lung pathology information from clinical narratives, addressing the labor-intensive nature of manual extraction.

title: Large Language Models Do Not Always Need Readable Language
summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can process semantic information encoded in compact, non-standard textual forms, challenging the assumption that they always require human-readable language.

title: The Almost Intelligent Revolution: Options for Scaling Up Deliberation and Empowering People with AI
summary: This article explores the ethical implications and challenges of large language models in democratic deliberation, discussing issues like linguistic constraints, biases, and the need for red teaming strategies.

title: REDACT: A Systematically Controlled Multilingual Benchmark for Personal Information Detection
summary: REDACT is introduced as a systematically controlled multilingual benchmark designed to evaluate and improve the detection of personally identifiable information (PII) by addressing limitations in existing corpora.

title: Light-weight Pronunciation Assessment via Discrete Speech Token Surprisal
summary: This paper proposes a lightweight framework for automated pronunciation assessment that uses discrete speech token surprisal, training only on native speech resources to avoid costly error labeling.

title: GEMS: Geometric Constraints Enable Multi-Semantic Superposition in LLMs
summary: This research introduces GEMS, a method using geometric constraints to enable multi-semantic superposition in LLMs via activation steering, preventing model collapse when integrating multiple semantic directions.

title: Source-Grounded Data Generation for Text-to-JSON Learning
summary: This research proposes a method for source-grounded data generation to facilitate text-to-JSON learning, aiming to reliably extract structured information from long, unstructured documents.

title: IHUBERT: Vector-Based Semantic Deduplication and Domain-Balanced Pretraining for Persian Resources
summary: IHUBERT is presented as a new monolingual Persian pretrained language model (PLM), trained from scratch with a RoBERTa-base encoder and featuring vector-based semantic deduplication and domain-balanced pretraining.

title: Self-Preference Is Weak or Absent in Verifiable Instruction-Following Revision: A Four-Model Test Under Genuine Authorship
summary: This study investigates whether large language models exhibit self-preference bias when performing instruction-following revisions on their own text, finding the bias to be weak or absent under verifiable conditions.

title: HydraHead: From Head-Level Functional Heterogeneity to Specialized Attention Hybridization
summary: HydraHead proposes a new approach to specialized attention hybridization to address the quadratic complexity bottleneck in long-context processing, focusing on integrating Linear Attention with Full Attention.

title: When Does Streaming Tool Use Help? Characterizing Tool-Intent Stabilization in Streaming Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper characterizes when streaming tool use benefits Streaming Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by analyzing tool-intent stabilization, aiming to reduce user-perceived latency by parallelizing queries.

title: From Texts to Scores: Tracing the Emergence of Essay Quality Representations in Large Language Models
summary: This work systematically analyzes the hidden representations of eight large language models to trace the emergence of essay quality representations in Automated Essay Scoring (AES).

title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
summary: MedRLM is introduced as a recursive multimodal AI system for health intelligence, designed for long-context clinical reasoning, sensor-guided screening, evidence-grounded decision support, and referral optimization.

title: ReNikud: Audio-Supervised Hebrew Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion
summary: ReNikud presents an audio-supervised grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion method for Modern Hebrew, which is crucial for text-to-speech applications despite the language's unique unwritten vowel system.

title: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families
summary: This research investigates actionable activation directions for detecting and mitigating emergent misalignment in language models, particularly when fine-tuned on insecure code, addressing AI safety concerns.

title: The Register Gap: A Meaning Intelligence Framework for Nigerian Public Discourse
summary: The Meaning Intelligence Framework (MIF) is introduced as a nine-dimension annotation and evaluation schema for Nigerian public discourse, aiming to differentiate surface sentiment from true communicative intent.

title: PsyScore: A Psychometrically-Aware Framework for Trait-Adaptive Essay Scoring and ZPD-Scaffolded Feedback
summary: PsyScore is presented as a psychometrically-aware framework for trait-adaptive Automated Essay Scoring (AES) that provides ZPD-scaffolded feedback, aiming to integrate assessment and actionable instructional feedback.

title: CATCH-ME if you RAG: a dataset of Contextually Annotated multi-Turn Counterspeech against Hate and Misinformation Exchanges
summary: CATCH-ME is a new dataset of contextually annotated multi-turn counterspeech exchanges against hate and misinformation, designed to improve and evaluate LLM performance in generating effective responses.

title: Your Mouse and Eyes Secretly Leak Your Preference: LLM Alignment using Implicit Feedback from Users
summary: This research proposes a method for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) by using implicit feedback from user mouse and eye movements to train a reward model, overcoming limitations of explicit feedback.

title: StylisticBias: A Few Human Visual Cues Drive Most Social Biases in MLLMs
summary: This study investigates how specific human visual cues contribute to social biases observed in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), aiming to better understand the mechanisms of bias in these systems.

title: Gender Bias in LLM Hiring Decisions: Evidence from a Japanese Context and Evaluation of Mitigation Strategies
summary: This study examines gender bias in Large Language Model (LLM) hiring decisions within a Japanese corporate context and evaluates strategies to mitigate this bias.

title: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
summary: This paper discusses mobile agents, questioning the necessity of a GUI paradigm for their operation and proposing that a command-line interface (CLI) could offer more direct access to device services and data.

title: Scaling Generative Foundation Models for Chest Radiography with Rectified Flow Transformers
summary: This research introduces the first billion-parameter generative foundation model for synthesizing chest radiographs, utilizing Rectified Flow Transformers to address generalization challenges in existing radiographic AI models.

title: LEAP: Layer-skipping Efficiency via Adaptive Progression for Vision Transformer Distillation
summary: This paper introduces LEAP, a method for efficiently distilling large Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones into smaller architectures for edge deployment by employing layer-skipping via adaptive progression.

title: LooseControlVideo: Directorial Video Control using Spatial Blocking
summary: This work presents LooseControlVideo, a method to achieve precise 3D spatial orchestration and directorial control in text-to-video generation, particularly for multi-object scenes.

title: ImageWAM: Do World Action Models Really Need Video Generation, or Just Image Editing?
summary: This paper explores whether World Action Models (WAMs) for robot control truly require full video generation or if image editing techniques could be sufficient, addressing limitations of video-based WAMs.

title: PerceptionDLM: Parallel Region Perception with Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
summary: This work introduces PerceptionDLM, a novel approach that uses Multimodal Diffusion Language Models to enable parallel region perception, enhancing efficiency for visual understanding tasks in MLLMs.

title: Mix-QVLA: Task-Evidence-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This paper proposes Mix-QVLA, a task-evidence-aware mixed-precision post-training quantization framework designed to optimize Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models while preserving task-relevant information.

title: Language-Instructed Vision Embeddings for Controllable and Generalizable Perception
summary: This work proposes a new paradigm where language dynamically guides vision embedding models, moving beyond static feature extraction to enable controllable and generalizable perception in vision foundation models.

title: GB-LSR: A Fast Local Spectral Image Representation with a Single Global Bandwidth for Continuous Reconstruction and Super-Resolution
summary: This paper presents GB-LSR, a fast local spectral image representation with a single global bandwidth, designed for continuous image reconstruction and super-resolution by partitioning image domains into patches.

title: Learning When to Denoise: Optimizing Asynchronous Schedules for Latent Diffusion
summary: This research proposes a method to learn and optimize the asynchronous schedule for multi-representation diffusion models, improving visual synthesis by determining when each representation should be denoised.

title: TeleMorpher: Toward Robust Simultaneous Motion-Location Editing
summary: TeleMorpher is introduced as a method extending diffusion models to achieve robust simultaneous motion and location editing in images and videos, a largely unexplored area.

title: Vortex: Multi-Modal Fusion System for Intelligent Video Retrieval
summary: Vortex is a multimodal fusion system developed for the Ho Chi Minh City AI Challenge 2025, designed for intelligent video retrieval, multimedia search, and temporal reasoning, integrating adaptive keyframe extraction and multimodal metadata generation.

title: Exploring Multi-Modal Large Language Models and Two-Stage Fine-Tuning for Fashion Image Retrieval
summary: This research explores the use of Multi-Modal Large Language Models combined with two-stage fine-tuning for fashion image retrieval, focusing on understanding subtle attribute variations in composed image queries.

title: NEST: Narrative Event Structures in Time for Long Video Understanding
summary: NEST is a framework addressing long video understanding by analyzing narrative event structures in time, improving the ability of vision-language models to process and comprehend extended video sequences.

title: One-Shot Novel View and Pose Human Image Synthesis via 3D Prior Guided Diffusion Model
summary: This paper introduces a method for one-shot novel view and pose human image synthesis, utilizing a 3D Prior Guided Diffusion Model to transfer reference human images to target poses.

title: QueryGaussian: Scalable and Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Retrieval
summary: QueryGaussian proposes a scalable and training-free method for open-vocabulary 3D instance retrieval from large-scale scenes using natural language prompts, moving beyond scene-level embedding paradigms.

title: VFACamou: View-Fused Adversarial Camouflage for Environment-Adaptive Physical Evasion
summary: VFACamou introduces View-Fused Adversarial Camouflage, a method for environment-adaptive physical evasion designed to create robust camouflage against UAV reconnaissance under dynamic viewpoints and illumination.

title: Occ-VLM: Occupancy Grounded Vision Language Model for Indoor Scene Understanding
summary: This paper introduces Occ-VLM, an occupancy-grounded vision-language model designed to enhance 3D indoor scene understanding. It improves upon existing VLMs that rely on explicit 3D inputs.

title: HypOProto: Hyperbolic Ordinal Prototypes for Left Ventricular Filling Pressure Classification
summary: This research introduces HypOProto, a method using hyperbolic ordinal prototypes for classifying Left Ventricular Filling Pressure from echocardiography images. This aims to improve cardiac function assessment in healthcare.

title: Training-Free Metrics for Synthetic Object Detection Data: A Proxy for Detector Performance
summary: This paper explores training-free metrics to evaluate the quality of synthetic object detection data, aiming to predict its effectiveness for training computer vision models without full retraining.

title: CSWinUNETR: Segmentation of Thin Anatomical Structures in Medical Images
summary: This research presents CSWinUNETR, a novel model designed for accurate segmentation of thin and tortuous anatomical structures in medical images. It aims to address challenges like low contrast and class imbalance in medical imaging.

title: 3D-PLOT-LLM: Part-Level Object Tokens for 3D Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces 3D-PLOT-LLM, a new approach that enables 3D multimodal large language models to reason about object parts by using part-level object tokens. This aims to overcome limitations of existing 3D MLLMs in fine-grained understanding.

title: Neural Events: Discrete Asynchronous Autoencoders for Event-Based Vision
summary: This research proposes Neural Events, discrete asynchronous autoencoders designed to process data from event cameras for event-based vision. The method aims to extract meaningful signals from the minimal semantic value of individual events.

title: OTCHA: Optimal Transport-driven Confidence-aware Latent Hub Alignment for Multi-View Medical Image Classification
summary: This research introduces OTCHA, a method utilizing optimal transport-driven confidence-aware latent hub alignment for multi-view medical image classification. It aims to improve diagnostic accuracy by addressing artifacts and registration issues in clinical images.

title: ViCoStream: Streaming VideoLLMs Can Run Beyond 100 FPS with Stage-Wise Coordinated Inference
summary: This paper presents ViCoStream, a method that enables streaming VideoLLMs to achieve over 100 FPS with low latency through stage-wise coordinated inference. This significantly improves real-time processing capabilities for video understanding.

title: Multimodal Concept Bottleneck Models
summary: This research introduces Multimodal Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) to enhance the interpretability of deep learning networks by aligning features with natural concepts. It aims to overcome generalization limitations of existing CBMs.

title: SurgVista: Long-Horizon Surgical World Modeling with Plausible Instrument-Tissue Dynamics
summary: This research presents SurgVista, a surgical world modeling approach that generates realistic, action-conditioned future frames to facilitate robot policy learning for autonomous surgery. It addresses the challenges of expensive demonstrations and safety risks in surgical robotics.

title: Gaussian Process Prior Variational Autoencoder for Endoscopic Videos
summary: This paper proposes a Gaussian Process Prior Variational Autoencoder to enhance endoscopic video analysis by effectively addressing common degradations like specular reflections and motion artifacts. It aims to improve interpretability for gastrointestinal diagnosis.

title: SpatialSV: Internalizing Interpretable 3D Spatial Awareness in MLLMs via Task-Oriented Visual Supervision
summary: This research introduces SpatialSV, a method to equip multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with interpretable 3D spatial awareness using task-oriented visual supervision. It aims to enable better understanding and interaction with the 3D world.

title: CARE: Competence-Aware Reward Shaping for Adaptive Reasoning Length in Video-MLLMs
summary: This paper proposes CARE, a competence-aware reward shaping mechanism for adaptive reasoning length in Video-MLLMs based on reinforcement learning. This aims to improve exploration and prevent redundant reasoning in multimodal video tasks.

title: Spatial-Aware Reduction Framework: Towards Efficient and Faithful Visual State Space Models
summary: This research introduces a Spatial-Aware Reduction Framework to enhance the efficiency and faithfulness of Visual State Space Models (VSSMs) like Mamba. It aims to prevent performance collapse often seen when applying token reduction to these models.

title: Speeding up the annotation process in semantic segmentation industrial applications
summary: This paper explores leveraging unsupervised algorithms to accelerate the annotation process for semantic segmentation in industrial applications. It aims to address the bottleneck of creating large, well-annotated datasets for machine learning models.

title: DiffMath: Symbol- and Graph-Aware Latent Diffusion Transformer for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Generation
summary: This paper introduces DiffMath, a symbol- and graph-aware latent diffusion transformer for generating handwritten mathematical expressions. It addresses the challenges of complex 2D layouts and structural dependencies in HMEG.

title: Timage: A Generative Text-in-Image Paradigm for Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper proposes Timage, a generative text-in-image paradigm designed to improve fine-grained spatial reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It aims to help MLLMs track relevant image regions more effectively.

title: Confidence Calibration for Multimodal LLMs: An Empirical Study through Medical VQA
summary: This paper presents an empirical study on confidence calibration for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in medical Visual Question Answering. It investigates the misalignment between MLLM confidence and actual accuracy, which could impact medical diagnoses.

title: SketchKeyAnime: Reference-anchored Sparse Key-Sketch Animation Synthesis
summary: This paper introduces SketchKeyAnime, a method for reference-anchored sparse key-sketch animation synthesis that reduces manual drawing and refinement. It aims to simplify traditional animation production by moving beyond dense RGB frame dependencies.

title: Addressing Detail Bottlenecks in Latent Diffusion for RGB-to-SWIR Image Translation
summary: This research addresses detail bottlenecks in Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) for RGB-to-SWIR image translation. It identifies and proposes solutions for the loss of fine spatial details during compression in LDMs.

title: ROSE: Benchmarking the Perception-to-Action Gap in Multimodal Models
summary: This paper introduces ROSE, a new benchmark to evaluate how reliably multimodal large language models can translate visual evidence into appropriate actions under different task contexts. It focuses on measuring the perception-to-action gap in MLLMs.

title: CrossFlow: One-Step Generation Across Latent and Pixel Spaces
summary: CrossFlow introduces a new one-step generation method for diffusion and flow-matching generators, allowing simultaneous definition of prior, path, and prediction target in both latent and pixel spaces. This approach aims to improve efficiency in generating samples compared to traditional latent diffusion.

title: Vision-Reasoning-Guided Occlusion Removal from Light Fields
summary: This paper proposes a vision-reasoning-guided light field occlusion removal framework designed to improve scene recovery in natural environments with dense foreground vegetation. The method combines visibility recovery capabilities with object understanding to address a major challenge in computational imaging.

title: QG-MIL: A Gated Transformer Aggregator for Domain-Agnostic Multiple Instance Learning in Medical Imaging
summary: QG-MIL introduces a gated transformer aggregator designed to address attention concentration issues in attention-based Multiple Instance Learning aggregators used in medical imaging. The framework aims to provide more stable and reliable predictions through four synergistic architectural components.

title: ReA-OVCD: Reliability-Aware Open-Vocabulary Change Detection via Semantic and Spatial Refinement
summary: ReA-OVCD proposes a new method for Reliability-Aware Open-Vocabulary Change Detection in remote sensing, enabling flexible identification of land cover changes using text prompts. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods by incorporating semantic and spatial refinement.

title: PU-UNet: Stable Multiplicative Interactions for Medical Image Segmentation
summary: PU-UNet introduces stable multiplicative interactions for medical image segmentation, addressing numerical instability issues often associated with product units. This new approach aims to enhance dense prediction networks by explicitly modeling higher-order feature interactions.

title: FUSE: Frequency-domain Unification and Spectral Energy Alignment for Multi-modal Object Re-Identification
summary: FUSE proposes a new method for Multi-modal Object Re-Identification by unifying frequency domains and aligning spectral energy. It aims to improve ReID by capturing both low-frequency attributes and crucial mid-to-high frequency structures like geometric and textural information.

title: See-and-Reach: Precise Vision-Language Navigation for UAVs within the Field of View
summary: See-and-Reach focuses on precise Vision-Language Navigation for UAVs, addressing the challenge of assessing a critical capability for aerial embodied agents within their field of view. It aims to refine how drones are guided by language commands for target approach.

title: Variable-Length Tokenization via Learnable Global Merging for Diffusion Transformers
summary: This paper introduces Variable-Length Tokenization via Learnable Global Merging for Diffusion Transformers, which enables adaptive compression in latent diffusion models. This method aims to improve the quality-compute trade-off in visual synthesis by varying token counts.

title: The Hidden Evolution of Disguised Visual Context inside the VLM
summary: This research explores how visual tokens are transformed into meaningful representations and interact with the language space within Visual Language Models (VLMs). It analyzes the integration architecture's role in processing disguised visual context.

title: EventVLA: Event-Driven Visual Evidence Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: EventVLA introduces an event-driven visual evidence memory system designed to overcome memory bottlenecks in long-horizon Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies for robotic manipulation. It allows AI systems to robustly store and recall task-relevant cues even when occluded.

title: MakeupMirror: Improving Facial Attribute Preservation in Diffusion Models for Makeup Transfer
summary: MakeupMirror improves facial attribute preservation in diffusion models used for makeup transfer, enhancing realism and accuracy for augmented reality (AR) and virtual try-on (VTO) applications. It addresses limitations in existing state-of-the-art diffusion-based solutions.

title: Stitching and dimensionality effects on large artificially generated volume datasets
summary: This research investigates stitching and dimensionality effects that occur when generating large images using deep learning, due to patching input data and assembling output patches. It examines how these artifacts impact downstream tasks like segmentation.

title: WeGenBench: A Multidimensional Diagnostic Benchmark towards Text-to-Image Model Optimization
summary: WeGenBench is a new multidimensional diagnostic benchmark designed to comprehensively and accurately evaluate text-to-image generation models. It aims to overcome limitations of existing benchmarks in assessing generation capabilities for model optimization.

title: Geometry-Preserving in 3D Gaussian Splatting for LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration
summary: This paper introduces a geometry-preserving method using 3D Gaussian Splatting for accurate LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration, essential for robust multi-modal perception in autonomous systems. It addresses limitations in targetless approaches by reconstructing scenes within a differentiable model.

title: EFIQA: Explainable Fundus Image Quality Assessment via Anatomical Priors
summary: EFIQA proposes an explainable deep learning-based method for fundus image quality assessment by incorporating anatomical priors. It aims to improve generalization and address limitations of traditional classifiers tied to specific labeling criteria.

title: FrozenDrive: Zero-Shot Text-Guided Driving Scene Generation and Data Augmentation with Parameter-Free Frozen Diffusion Model
summary: FrozenDrive introduces a zero-shot text-guided method for generating synthetic driving scenes and data augmentation using a parameter-free frozen diffusion model. This approach addresses challenges in enforcing multi-view and temporal consistency without eroding pre-trained knowledge.

title: Pixel-Level Residual Diffusion Transformer: Scalable 3D CT Volume Generation
summary: This paper proposes the Pixel-Level Residual Diffusion Transformer (PRDiT), a scalable generative framework designed for generating high-resolution 3D CT volumes with fine details. It addresses computational demands and optimization difficulties inherent to existing generative models.

title: Physical Atari: A Robust and Accessible Platform for Real-time Reinforcement Learning on Robots
summary: Physical Atari is a robust and accessible robotic platform, comprising a Robotroller and Atari Devbox, built for real-time reinforcement learning on physical robots. It allows robots to interact with an Atari CX40+ controller based on game frames and reward signals.

title: WorkBenchMark: A LEGO-Based Assembly Benchmark with an Assembly-by-Disassembly Baseline for the Smart Manufacturing League
summary: WorkBenchMark introduces a LEGO Duplo-based robotic assembly benchmark for the RoboCup Smart Manufacturing League. It focuses on challenging robotic assembly tasks that combine low-level manipulation with task-level symbolic reasoning.

title: 3D Scene Graphs: Open Challenges and Future Directions
summary: This paper explores 3D Scene Graphs (3DSGs) as a representation for spatial AI, highlighting their relevance to robotics and computer vision by combining geometric grounding with semantic and relational abstractions.

title: DiffusionVS: A Generative Framework for Robust Visual Servoing Based on Diffusion Policy
summary: This paper presents DiffusionVS, a generative framework based on Diffusion Policy, designed to achieve robust visual servoing for robotic manipulation and navigation by mitigating trajectory jitter and error accumulation.

title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
summary: This research investigates "Playful Agentic Robot Learning," a paradigm where embodied robots acquire reusable skills through play rather than solely explicit task instructions, advancing agentic robot capabilities.

title: Simulating Robotic Locomotion in Sand: Resistive Force Theory in an Open-Source Physics Engine
summary: This paper details the application of Resistive Force Theory (RFT) within an open-source 3D physics engine to simulate robotic locomotion in sand, reducing computational cost compared to individual grain modeling.

title: Proprioceptive Invariant State Estimation for Humanoid Robots on Non-Inertial Ground
summary: This paper introduces an invariant extended Kalman filtering (InEKF) method for real-time state estimation of humanoid robots operating on moving ground, utilizing only onboard proprioceptive sensing.

title: pdSTL: Probabilistic Differentiable Signal Temporal Logic for Stochastic Systems
summary: This paper presents pdSTL, a probabilistic differentiable Signal Temporal Logic designed to help autonomous robots operating in uncertain environments satisfy complex temporal and safety specifications despite stochastic dynamics and sensing noise.

title: One Demo is Worth a Thousand Trajectories: Action-View Augmentation for Visuomotor Policies
summary: This research proposes action-view augmentation for visuomotor policies to enhance their generalization in robotic manipulation, addressing issues caused by minor configuration changes and unseen obstacles with limited data.

title: Safe, Real-Time Active Model Discrimination and Fault Diagnosis for Nonlinear Systems via Differentiable Reachability
summary: This paper introduces a safe, real-time algorithm for active fault diagnosis and model discrimination in uncertain continuous-time nonlinear systems, capable of identifying actuator and sensor faults using differentiable reachability.

title: Fail-RAG : A Retrieval Augmented Generation Informed Framework for Robot Failure Identification
summary: This paper presents "Fail-RAG," a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) informed framework designed to identify failures in intelligent autonomous robots.

title: Formal Verification of Learned Multi-Agent Communication Policies via Decision Tree Distillation
summary: This research introduces a method for formal verification of learned multi-agent communication policies using decision tree distillation, specifically for safety-critical robotic deployments like drone swarms and autonomous vehicle fleets.

title: CTS-MoE: Implicit Terrain Adaptation via Mixture-of-Experts for Perceptive Locomotion
summary: This paper presents CTS-MoE, a Mixture-of-Experts approach for implicit terrain adaptation in perceptive legged locomotion, enabling robots to navigate discontinuous terrain like stairs and gaps.

title: Scaling Self-Play for End-to-End Driving
summary: This research explores scaling self-play to train end-to-end autonomous driving models, aiming to overcome the limitations of offline human-demonstration datasets, including limited state coverage and compounding errors.

title: DF-ExpEnse: Diffusion Filtered Exploration for Sample Efficient Finetuning
summary: This paper introduces DF-ExpEnse, an exploration technique designed to enhance the quality of online experience for sample-efficient finetuning of pre-trained generative control policies in robotic decision-making.

title: ForEnt: A Multi-Modal Dataset for Characterizing Quadruped Robot Entrapments in Forest Environments
summary: This research introduces "ForEnt," a multi-modal dataset designed to characterize entrapments of quadruped robots in forest environments, thereby aiding in the development of more robust autonomous locomotion.

title: Bidirectional Tutoring for Developmental Motor Learning in Robots: Co-Developed Interaction Dynamics Support Stable Learning
summary: This paper investigates bidirectional tutoring for developmental motor learning in robots, drawing parallels with human infant-caregiver interactions to achieve more stable and effective skill acquisition.

title: VOiLA: Vectorized Online Planning with Learned Diffusion Model for POMDP Agents
summary: This paper introduces VOiLA, a vectorized online planning method that leverages a learned Diffusion Model for POMDP agents, enhancing planning under uncertainty for autonomous robots.

title: Temporal Self-Imitation Learning
summary: This research proposes temporal self-imitation learning to improve the efficiency of long-horizon robot manipulation policies by self-supervision, ensuring rare efficient behaviors are not forgotten during training.

title: Data Standards for Humanoid Robotics: The Missing Infrastructure for Physical AI
summary: This paper argues for the necessity of data standards in humanoid robotics, referencing ISO/WD 26264-1, to enable the scalable accumulation of physical experience across different robots, tasks, and organizations.

title: Start Right, Arrive Right: Asynchronous Execution via Initial Noise Selection
summary: This paper explores asynchronous execution via initial noise selection for robot policies, aiming to reduce latency when generating multi-step action sequences with flow-based policies for real-time control.

title: EquiVLA: A General Framework for Rotationally Equivariant Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This paper introduces EquiVLA, a framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that incorporates rotational equivariance to improve generalization in generalist robot manipulation tasks.

title: TIDY: Thermal Infrared Image Denoising via Wavelet Domain Entropy and Directional Stripe Index
summary: This paper proposes TIDY, a method for denoising thermal infrared images using wavelet domain entropy and directional stripe index. This technique aims to improve perception capabilities for field robotics by mitigating severe stochastic and fixed-pattern noise.

title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving
summary: This research introduces "World Engine," a concept for post-training autonomous driving systems to improve their reliability in real-world scenarios. It focuses on addressing rare, safety-critical "long-tail" events that limit the performance of current end-to-end driving policies.

title: One-to-Two Acting: A Novel Framework for Single-arm Agent Action Expansion to Dual Arms
summary: This paper presents ExS2D, a novel hierarchical framework that enables dual-arm robotic manipulation using supervision from single-arm demonstrations. This approach aims to reduce the costly and difficult process of collecting bimanual training data.

title: Co-policy: Responsive Human-Robot Co-Creation for Musical Performances
summary: This research explores human-robot co-creation in musical performances, leveraging embodied artificial intelligence for generative models. It focuses on developing robotic systems that can participate in creative physical actions alongside humans.

title: Deep-Unfolded Coordination
summary: This paper proposes Deep Coordinator, a deep-unfolding framework to address challenges in distributed optimization for multi-agent robotics problems. It aims to improve coordination in robotic systems by overcoming issues with hyperparameter tuning.

title: Motor Angular Speed Preintegration for Multirotor UAV State Estimation
summary: This research focuses on improving the precision of state estimation for multirotor UAVs by integrating motor angular speed. This aims to enable more agile and precise feedback control for near-obstacle flights.

title: Evaluation of Augmented Reality-based Intuitive Interface for Robot-Assisted Transesophageal Echocardiography: A User Study
summary: This study evaluates an intuitive augmented reality-based interface for robot-assisted Transesophageal Echocardiography (TEE). The goal is to simplify the complex and demanding manipulation required for diagnosing and guiding structural heart disease interventions.

title: Tri-Info: Generalizable, Interpretable Failure Prediction for VLA Models via Information Theory
summary: This paper introduces Tri-Info, a method for generalizable and interpretable failure prediction in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models using information theory. It aims to detect systematic differences between successful and failed physical interactions of these models.

title: A Neuromorphic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Efficient Pathfinding in Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems
summary: This research proposes a neuromorphic reinforcement learning framework for efficient pathfinding in Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems (RMFS). The goal is to address the computational challenges and real-time constraints of dynamic environments in these systems.

title: MirrorDuo: Reflection-Consistent Visuomotor Learning from Mirrored Demonstration Pairs
summary: This paper introduces MirrorDuo, a reflection-based formulation for visuomotor learning that uses mirrored demonstration pairs for image-based behavior cloning. This method aims to improve generalization across workspace variations for robotic systems.

title: VFILC: Accurate Frequency Extrapolations in Imitation Learning via Sampling Frequency ILC
summary: This paper presents VFILC, a method for achieving accurate frequency extrapolations in imitation learning for variable-speed robotic motion. It aims to overcome limitations of conventional neural network-based imitation learning when extrapolating beyond trained velocity ranges.

title: Pose6DAug: Physically Plausible Multi-view Object Swapping for Robot Data Augmentation
summary: This paper introduces Pose6DAug, a method for physically plausible multi-view object swapping designed for robot data augmentation. It aims to improve the generalization of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies in robotic manipulation to novel, out-of-distribution objects.

title: Dual-Agent Framework for Cross-Model Verified Translation of Natural-Language Protocols into Robotic Laboratory Platform
summary: This research proposes a dual-agent framework for translating natural-language biological experiment protocols into commands for robotic laboratory platforms. The framework aims to bridge the semantic gap between human instructions and automation system requirements.

title: Frequency-Aware Flow Matching for Continuous and Consistent Robotic Action Generation
summary: This research proposes a frequency-aware flow matching method for continuous and consistent robotic action generation in manipulation tasks. It aims to improve upon existing flow matching approaches by addressing their brittleness due to discretized action chunks.

title: Robust Assembly State Reasoning from Action Recognition for Human-Robot Collaboration
summary: This research investigates robust assembly state reasoning derived from Human Action Recognition (HAR) for Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC). It aims to accurately track the state of a collaborative task by understanding human actions.

title: Belt-Finger: An Affordable Soft Belt-Driven Gripper for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces Belt-Finger, an affordable soft belt-driven gripper designed for dexterous in-hand manipulation. It aims to provide enhanced mobility and dexterity compared to traditional parallel-jaw grippers.

title: Stable Transformer-Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control: A Contraction Analysis Approach
summary: This paper proposes a novel Transformer-Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control (MPC) architecture that focuses on guaranteeing closed-loop stability using contraction analysis. This approach aims to address challenges in controlling complex, non-convex systems with sequence-based learning models.

title: FlowMaps: Modeling Long-Term Multimodal Object Dynamics with Flow Matching
summary: This research introduces FlowMaps, a method for modeling long-term multimodal object dynamics in 3D scenes using flow matching. This aims to enable robots to better understand and reason about evolving household environments.

title: Finetuning Vision-Language-Action Models Requires Fewer Layers Than You Think
summary: This research demonstrates that fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation requires fewer layers than typically assumed. This finding aims to reduce the computational burden during downstream fine-tuning and real-time inference for these models.

title: Efficiently Linking Real Scenes with Synthetic Data Generation for AI-based Cognitive Robotics and Computer Vision Applications
summary: This paper focuses on efficiently linking real scenes with synthetic data generation to train AI vision models for cognitive robotics and computer vision applications. This approach aims to improve semantic environment analysis and grasping pose estimation for robots.

title: Co-VLA: Coordination-Aware Structured Action Modeling for Dual-Arm Vision-Language-Action Systems
summary: This paper introduces Co-VLA, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed for coordination-aware structured action modeling in dual-arm robotic manipulation. It focuses on how coordinated bimanual behaviors emerge from end-to-end learning using large vision-language backbones.

title: Towards 3D karst underwater scene reconstruction from rotating sonar data
summary: This research explores using AI for 3D reconstruction of karst underwater scenes from rotating sonar data, addressing challenges of sparse and noisy data in mapping complex subsurface geometries. It aims to improve the understanding of critical freshwater resources.

title: Autonomous Driving with Priority-Ordered STL Specifications Under Multimodal Uncertainty
summary: This paper discusses autonomous driving systems that use priority-ordered STL (Signal Temporal Logic) specifications to plan trajectories under multimodal uncertainty. The approach aims to address challenges in satisfying multiple requirements like safety and comfort in autonomous vehicles.

title: An Infrastructure-less, Control-Independent Solution to Relative Localisation of a Team of Mobile Robots using Ranging Measurements
summary: This research presents an infrastructure-less and control-independent solution for relative localization of a team of mobile robots using ranging measurements. This capability is crucial for robotic fleets operating in unstructured environments and cooperative navigation tasks.

title: CoLI: A Reproducible Platform for Continuum Robot Learning via Monolithic 3D Printing and Isomorphic Teleoperation
summary: This paper introduces CoLI, a reproducible platform for continuum robot learning, leveraging monolithic 3D printing and isomorphic teleoperation. The platform aims to overcome reproducibility challenges in the fabrication and assembly of continuum robots for manipulation tasks.

title: Agentic AutoResearch forSpace Autonomy: An Auditable, LLM-Driven Research Agent for Aerospace Control Problems
summary: This research presents an auditable, LLM-driven 'Agentic AutoResearch' system designed to function as a research agent for aerospace control problems. It aims to automate the process of developing learned policies for spacecraft guidance, navigation, and control.

title: LIT-GS: LiDAR-Inertial-Thermal Gaussian Splatting for Illumination-Robust Mapping
summary: This paper introduces LIT-GS, a LiDAR-inertial-thermal Gaussian Splatting method for illumination-robust mapping and real-time neural rendering. It addresses the fragility of existing Gaussian mapping pipelines under varying illumination and in texture-deficient scenes.

title: TaCauchy: An Extensible FEM Framework for Vision-Based Tactile Simulation
summary: This paper presents TaCauchy, an extensible Finite Element Method (FEM) framework for high-fidelity vision-based tactile simulation, addressing the need for accurate mechanical stress fields in GPU-accelerated robotics platforms. It aims to improve reinforcement learning for tactile sensors.
